Blockaid: 12 Crypto Project Websites Linked to Frontend Attacks; Flap and Kintsu Confirm DNS Hijacks

Security firm Blockaid initially flagged potential frontend attacks targeting Flap and Kintsu. It later identified 10 additional websites serving the Step Drainer wallet-draining tool, including pickle[.]finance, origami[.]finance, and fluxbeam[.]xyz. The investigation is ongoing.

Flap and Kintsu have confirmed DNS hijacks affecting their websites, warning users against visiting, connecting wallets, or signing transactions. Flap founder Cedric said users who had previously connected to the legitimate website were unaffected. The risk concerns users who visited the malicious site and connected wallets or signed approvals in the tens of minutes before the announcement. Kintsu advised users who connected wallets or signed anything since approximately 00:00 UTC on October 31 to revoke approvals and move funds. Both projects said they would announce when their websites are safe to use.

Or Fable vs Astra — really, any model vs Astra. 

The diff isn’t that Astra is smarter than most or has a better understanding; just the data that was fed into it. 

also why it writes such shitty/weird code and isn’t the best for coding. 

There’s a question of how much data can be put in a model st it preserves the quality across the tasks. 

It’s limited. They don’t know even how to train a general beast model properly yet without losing quality in some area. 

That math miracle OAI did? No one but them will probably ever see the model, because a) fuck OAI and their approach to science and b) that model is probably as capable with writing rust as gpt 5.1. It can’t do shit but math and lean. 

If fable 5.5 and gpt 6.2 bel drop and all of sudden they’re the models that can do both math solving AND coding AND videogames AND idk say computer use then there’s a big step in the right direction towards genuine general intelligence, bc they managed to compress the data/fit it somehow into these model without a compromise. And they have to ensure they don’t charge a $25/$50 for a request, right. 

But that’s also just a question of fiscal feasibility. No one officially knows how to make a model that’s affordable for a general enterprise - let alone api/sub use - for as many ppl as there are using these models too. 

It’s a miracle if they solve it. 

And that’s still bazillion steps away from irl. Just a first small step in a hopeful direction. 

But chances are? They need to IPO asap and they don’t have AGI. They struggle making their models as smart and affordable. Most use them for coding. 

DOA is my call. Tech will prevail and AGI robots will come out, but not before someone figures out new tech and has a breakthrough.

I’m delighted to announce Urban Tiger’s first product, Lodge, now generally available. To host a lodge, just go to https://t.co/elg3TVd3FS. To be a guest, wait till someone invites you!

Lodge is “half Eyes Wide Shut, half Chatham House Rules.” It’s a private chat/forum with strong anonymity. Everyone gets a random name from the blockchain. No one, not even you, has any record of who is who. Your forum runs on your private, encrypted cloud server (*).

Lodge is for all human beings who cannot speak their true minds if there is any risk that they might be “held accountable.” We do everything possible to prevent doxing. You can even cover your financial tracks with ZCash. (But you don’t need to know anything about crypto.)

Who needs a lodge? Your office needs a lodge. Your campus or department. Your agency. Start a lodge, and find a way to get the invite link or QR code to your founding members. 

Secret societies are a human universal. It doesn’t get more secret than Lodge.

To use Lodge, you and your guests install the House web app (app stores don’t like meta-apps). You’ll save your secret with a passkey and back it up with a 6-word poem. Your name is also a wallet, which holds its own token. (But you don’t need to know anything about crypto.)

Lodge is the first app on Urban Tiger’s new version of Urbit. Unlike the old Urbit experience (Tlon Messenger), https://t.co/elg3TVd3FS is both fully noncustodial, and fully general-purpose. The Lodge UX is “half forum, half chat.” Like a forum, it has a timeline tree. Like a chat, it flows through your unreads. The design was inspired by the original social network, Usenet. On a desktop you even “doomspace,” like it was 1986.

You’ll be billed for your server in crypto—by usage, not time (since it’s a functional server). It’s cheap. And you can charge dues.

Check it out: https://t.co/elg3TVd3FS

time is an underrated part of risk management when trading lower timeframes

when i enter a trade expecting a sharp move, i want price to react relatively quickly

if Bitcoin is sitting around my entry for too long without moving in the direction i expected, i start questioning the setup

the advantage of trading lower timeframes is that you can recognize when something isn't working much earlier

sometimes i'll exit a trade simply because it's taking too long to play out, even if my stop hasn't been hit

price and time both matter when deciding whether a trade is still worth taking

BNB 销毁简单来说目前只和 币价 有关。有两套销毁机制，一套季度自动销毁，一套实时 gas 销毁。gas 实时销毁影响太小，基本可以忽略。

季度自动销毁公式，B=(N*1000)/(P+K)

B：本季度销毁的 BNB 数量
N：本季度 bnb 链产生的区块数量（bnb 是固定时间出块，基本算是常量）
P：本季度 bnb 的价格，越高销毁越少
K：价格锚定常数，默认是 1000（常量）

text:
昨天刚分享完《Memory Tax》，结论是复杂 Memory 在整理和压缩历史时，可能反而损失原始信息。

结果今天又看到一篇更直接的：

很多精心设计的 Agent Memory，最后还真不一定打得过最朴素的 Raw-RAG。

这两篇放在一起看挺有意思。

昨天那篇在解释「Memory 为什么会产生税」，今天这篇则在问：如果直接保留 raw history 做检索，究竟能走多远？

Raw-RAG 的方法非常简单：

保留原始对话历史，切成带重叠的文本块；先做 dense retrieval，再用 reranker 筛一遍，最后把最相关的原始证据交给 LLM 推理。

中间没有 LLM 摘要、记忆重写、UPDATE / DELETE，也没有复杂的图结构。

结果在 LoCoMo、LongMemEval、MEME 和 MemoryAgentBench 上，7 组模型设置里拿下 6 组第一，比最强的对比 Memory 系统高 0.13–5.53 个百分点。

论文进一步分析了原因。

很多问题真正需要的证据，并不只是某个「答案值」，还包括时间顺序、前后关系和依赖路径。

Memory 一旦把历史压缩成独立事实或摘要，这些关系很容易在整理过程中被削弱。甚至把完整的 transformed memory 全部交给模型，效果依然和直接看 raw evidence 存在差距。

当然，这也不代表 RAG 随便做就行。

论文里去掉 reranking 后，MemoryAgentBench 的分数从 48.32 降到 44.40；只返回一个检索结果，下降更明显。

所以问题可能没那么复杂：

先把原始信息保存好，再把 retrieval 和 reranking 做扎实，已经能覆盖很多长时对话 Memory 场景。

两篇论文连着看，给我们的提醒很重要：

做 Agent Memory 之前，最好先问一句，这套复杂机制，究竟比 raw-history RAG 多带来了什么？

如果连这个 baseline 都没稳定超过，复杂本身可能还算不上进步。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/eF8TH1Vczf
author: Xudong07452910
quoted_text:
RAG 又杀回来了。

最近 Agent Memory 越做越复杂，但这篇《Memory Tax》发现了一个挺尴尬的结果：

很多专门设计的 Memory 系统，最后还不如直接对 raw history 做 RAG，而且成本更高。

作者把 Memory 的价值拆成两部分：

Memory Benefit：RAG 答错，但 Memory 答对的问题。

Memory Tax：RAG 本来能答对，经过 Memory 处理后反而答错的问题。

问题就出在「整理记忆」这一步。

历史被摘要、重写和结构化以后，一些细节会直接丢失；另一些虽然还在，却变得更难检索。

比如在 LongMemEval 上，Qwen3.6-27B 用两轮 RAG 能做到 81.4%，GPT-5.6 Luna 达到 90%，都高于对应的复杂 Memory 方案。

一个简单的修补反而很有效：

Memory 继续用，但同时保留 raw history 的检索通道，再把两边结果一起 rerank。

这篇工作也给我们做了一个提醒，给 Agent 加 Memory 之前，最好先拿最简单的 raw-history RAG 做个 baseline。

有时候，真正昂贵的并不是「没记住」，而是过早把原始信息总结掉了。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/qgKpDVD09d

okay public speaking is hard, apologies for the folks who showed up to watch me overheat and bomb, so here’s all the stuff i meant to explain

right now you are being asked for a near 100% prepayment because neither you nor the cloud is considered credit worthy, and so nobody can get debt. As ai scales, we are asking the credit markets to take on a massive single sector deployment of capital. More money deployed, more scared everyone gets.

this problem will flow down into the token layer. Every inference provider or model lab struggles to be credit worthy enough to get compute, and their lever to improve their situation is to lock in big prepayments from their customers or long term contracts from credit worthy customers. 

So this problem doesn’t just effect compute buyers, it effects token buyers. We’re entering a world where fortune 500s can very quickly deploy huge token spend ON CREDIT where the startup will need to raise capital. 

Startups got to exist because human capital could leave a firm and get ahead of the big firm by exploiting a combination of incentive misalignment, speed, and taste. 

You probably have the hidden assumption that the fortune 500 is slow and incapable of competing with your ultra fast startup. This belief does not necessarily hold in the case where the agent does the thing. 

the “market” is working on solving it. We know, because we are the market, and we’re working on it. sfcompute is working on ways of firming up the collateral of the loans, which makes it safer to lend to a startup. 

this is basically the whole reason we exist, the problem everyone is experiencing now is the problem junelark, our little ai lab years ago, hit

however, we won’t succeed in time. so, in the short term, startups and venture firms should learn to protect themselves.

we are mostly watching startups and investors make unforced error after unforced error, because this is not a simple subject. 

first, venture firms need to understand that they are in the compute business now and deploying capital to pay for a 100% prepayment for 10 startups where 6 of them die and 4 of them make 50% margins on that capital is basically locking in non-venture returns. many funds, via low understanding of the space, are wrecking their funds. 

there’s an economic solution for vc’s and it is owning the compute and trading equity for gpu/hrs. If the company dies, you keep the residual value. Each of you are looking to capture the next anthropic or openai, but the only way these companies scaled was by trading compute for equity. 

meanwhile, startups have three options in a credit crunch. 

The first is to raise a wild amount of capital, enough to pay for your deployments with far larger prepayment or to survive until things chill out. theres a reason we’re seeing a number of multi-billion dollar rounds simultaneously. 

The second is to design your business model to support variable priced tokens and compute. As the financial ecosystem builds around compute, you will be able to trade “lower up front payments” for “variably priced compute or tokens”. Your business will get tailwinds from the infra under you if you setup your business model such that YOUR customers have variable prices and you’re just adding a % take rate on top of the underlying floating price. Every year, you will become more and more capital efficient. The economic winners in ai & inference are firms that make lower and lower margin every year, but become more capital efficient & scale faster every year, making their gross profit increase. 

The third option is asynchronous or interrupted products. If you have a variable cogs, but a fixed rate card for your customers, it can’t have 100% availability or you’ll go bankrupt. But it is totally possible to design your product such that customers like this.

text:
A few things I took away from Vitalik’s thoughts on digital minimalism.

The idea isn’t to stop using social media or stop contributing. It’s to take back control over how we consume information.

Tools like Firefly allow us to remain active across platforms without constantly being pulled into algorithm-driven feeds, where outrage, noise and meaningless engagement often get rewarded over substance.

The same applies to cellular data minimalism. Being connected every second doesn’t necessarily make us better informed. It often just means more interruptions, less time to think and less control over our attention, with privacy implications too.

I think we underestimate how much this affects us. More mental space could mean better recovery, clearer thinking, greater productivity, less anxiety and a more positive outlook on the world.

And perhaps the most interesting part is that we might not actually miss much of importance.

Technology should expand our ability to think and act, not continuously compete for our attention.

Chamath: The AI Boom Has a Borrowing Problem

“The entire United States economy is levered to the AI complex.

So very narrowly, we're talking about seven or eight companies that set the tone for the entire country. And whether we like it or not, that is where we are.

Why do I say that? The most important companies in the world are in a massive spending binge, right?

These were highly profitable, highly cash accretive, highly cash flow generative businesses that have said, ‘We're going to put the foot down on spending because we believe in what's coming into the future.’ That's what drives GDP and it's what drives growth.

Now, as they do that though, they deplete their cash and they have to raise debt.

The AI complex now owes $340-400 billion to the market. And you'd say, ‘Okay, why is that important?’

The problem is this: These companies are raising so much money it starts to crowd out the capital markets.

And the most important part of the capital market that it starts to crowd out, is the appetite for government treasuries.

And what you can see here is that when you look at these AI firms, the amount of money that they need to raise through the end of '27, it's 30% of all of what the Treasury's about to issue in that same period.

So, whether we like it or not, they are going to start competing for demand.”

text:
In 2014 I went nearly a week without sleep. I was running PayPal and attackers were inside our corporate network. They'd compromised an eBay employee's laptop, got onto the VPN, taken over a domain controller and made themselves domain admins. eBay and PayPal were one company then, on one Windows network. They stole 145M eBay user records, then came for the segregated vault holding PayPal's card credentials. We fought them off. They never got in, but they got close. Too close.

Yesterday Binance lost ~$6.3B in what looks like the same way. A DevOps engineer's laptop, then a service inside the withdrawal stack, then withdrawals the signer approved because they came from a trusted source. Hot wallets emptied in under four hours. No key was stolen.

Nobody broke cryptography or a ledger. They found someone with access and used the trust that came with it. Banks get hit exactly the same way.

2016: attackers inside Bangladesh Bank used its own SWIFT access to send $951M of payment orders to the NY Fed. $81M was lost. The rest was held because an unrelated sanctions filter tripped on the word "Jupiter". That was luck, and it only worked because wires took days to settle.

June 2025: an IT employee at C&M Software, which connects Brazilian banks to Pix, sold his credentials for about $2,700. Attackers used them to send fake Pix transfers out of six institutions' reserve accounts at the central bank. ~$140M in under three hours.

August 2025: stolen vendor credentials at Sinqia, another Pix connector. ~R$710M out of HSBC and one other institution in a single afternoon. The central bank froze most of it, after it had already moved.

Same attack every time. Speed is what changed. When settlement took days, a filter, a correspondent bank or someone in ops could catch a bad payment. Pix, FedNow, SEPA Instant and blockchains settle in seconds. Payment security was mostly built for the slow world.

PayPal's card and user data survived 2014 because domain admin on the corp network couldn't unlock it quickly enough, and our alerting caught the unusual activity on the network. That's the model. Approval policy no laptop or vendor login can reach. Velocity and anomaly limits enforced outside the system that sends. Dynamic caps on what any one wallet, account or service can move per hour. All of it in real time.

About $3B of what left Binance has been frozen, almost all of it stablecoins. The $1.4B in bitcoin is sitting in 19 wallets and nobody can touch it. I don't think that's the problem. For decades the ability to reverse a wire or a card charge let a lot of weak security slide. You either stop the transfer before it's signed or you eat the loss.

Nothing about the technology failed here. The chains processed exactly the transactions they were handed. Binance's own systems handed them the wrong ones because an engineer's laptop was compromised. That's operational security. eBay in 2014, Bangladesh Bank and two Pix connectors all failed at it on their own rails.

In 2014 the attackers never reached the vault. If they had, the fraud losses would have been the small part. PayPal existed so people could pay without handing their card details to every merchant on the internet. We held those details so they didn't have to. Losing them would have broken the one thing the company was built on, and I'm not sure we would have recovered.

I expect blockchains and digital assets to become the standard way money moves. Every custodian of digital assets, or of fiat on a real-time rail, is in that position now. The controls have to adapt to settlement in seconds, crypto or not.

text:
一张图看懂 Binance 黑客的洗钱规模。

1200 万枚 TRX，约 3878 万美元，正在被拆分、转移，再拆分、再转移。

@OnchainLens 追踪到的资金流向图，密密麻麻的地址像一张不断扩张的蜘蛛网：从最初的资金来源出发，经过多轮跳转，最终流向数百个不同地址。

这不是简单的转账，而是一场自动化的链上资金拆分游戏。攻击者试图通过层层地址跳转，切断资金关联，增加追踪和冻结难度。

但链上每一笔转账都会留下痕迹。地址可以无限拆分，资金流向却未必能真正消失。

从事媒体和公关行业多年，今天从危机公关的角度，简单分析一下@heyibinance 一姐这个短短3分多的声明，因为亮点太多了。

text:
An important and useful perspective from @davidmarcus on PayPal and how they ultimately stopped an exploit and the insight:

“Approval policy that no laptop or vendor login can reach.”
author: fundstrat
quoted_text:
In 2014 I went nearly a week without sleep. I was running PayPal and attackers were inside our corporate network. They'd compromised an eBay employee's laptop, got onto the VPN, taken over a domain controller and made themselves domain admins. eBay and PayPal were one company then, on one Windows network. They stole 145M eBay user records, then came for the segregated vault holding PayPal's card credentials. We fought them off. They never got in, but they got close. Too close.

Yesterday Binance lost ~$6.3B in what looks like the same way. A DevOps engineer's laptop, then a service inside the withdrawal stack, then withdrawals the signer approved because they came from a trusted source. Hot wallets emptied in under four hours. No key was stolen.

Nobody broke cryptography or a ledger. They found someone with access and used the trust that came with it. Banks get hit exactly the same way.

2016: attackers inside Bangladesh Bank used its own SWIFT access to send $951M of payment orders to the NY Fed. $81M was lost. The rest was held because an unrelated sanctions filter tripped on the word "Jupiter". That was luck, and it only worked because wires took days to settle.

June 2025: an IT employee at C&M Software, which connects Brazilian banks to Pix, sold his credentials for about $2,700. Attackers used them to send fake Pix transfers out of six institutions' reserve accounts at the central bank. ~$140M in under three hours.

August 2025: stolen vendor credentials at Sinqia, another Pix connector. ~R$710M out of HSBC and one other institution in a single afternoon. The central bank froze most of it, after it had already moved.

Same attack every time. Speed is what changed. When settlement took days, a filter, a correspondent bank or someone in ops could catch a bad payment. Pix, FedNow, SEPA Instant and blockchains settle in seconds. Payment security was mostly built for the slow world.

PayPal's card and user data survived 2014 because domain admin on the corp network couldn't unlock it quickly enough, and our alerting caught the unusual activity on the network. That's the model. Approval policy no laptop or vendor login can reach. Velocity and anomaly limits enforced outside the system that sends. Dynamic caps on what any one wallet, account or service can move per hour. All of it in real time.

About $3B of what left Binance has been frozen, almost all of it stablecoins. The $1.4B in bitcoin is sitting in 19 wallets and nobody can touch it. I don't think that's the problem. For decades the ability to reverse a wire or a card charge let a lot of weak security slide. You either stop the transfer before it's signed or you eat the loss.

Nothing about the technology failed here. The chains processed exactly the transactions they were handed. Binance's own systems handed them the wrong ones because an engineer's laptop was compromised. That's operational security. eBay in 2014, Bangladesh Bank and two Pix connectors all failed at it on their own rails.

In 2014 the attackers never reached the vault. If they had, the fraud losses would have been the small part. PayPal existed so people could pay without handing their card details to every merchant on the internet. We held those details so they didn't have to. Losing them would have broken the one thing the company was built on, and I'm not sure we would have recovered.

I expect blockchains and digital assets to become the standard way money moves. Every custodian of digital assets, or of fiat on a real-time rail, is in that position now. The controls have to adapt to settlement in seconds, crypto or not.

author: AzFlin
quoted_text:
Later today, we are officially ending all remaining support for the Iron Fish network.

A few days ago, we observed abnormal activity involving wIRON and the ChainPort bridge. After working with ChainPort and reviewing their logs, we discovered that the cause was an inflation bug in the Iron Fish blockchain itself.

We traced the bug to a commit from early 2019 in the Merkle tree implementation. The developer at the time implemented a standard Merkle tree. However, because of nuances in how a note’s nullifier is calculated (the mechanism that lets a normal user spend their funds), the attacker was able to spend the same note more than once. 

The attacker then compounded the exploit, aggregated their notes, and exited through the ChainPort bridge. This code path was within the scope of both our external and internal audits, but the bug wasn’t caught during review.

For closure, we’ve committed the patch for the exploit, with a detailed postmortem included in the PR, before shutting down and archiving the ironfish repo.

The meta-analysis here is that software that can’t be upgraded immediately (most of crypto), is in an extremely precarious position. The ability to find and exploit vulnerabilities in technically complex code is becoming commoditized. Safety guardrails on US frontier models make it difficult for companies to use them to patch security vulnerabilities, while abliterated open-source models are approaching frontier capabilities.

We wish everyone all the best, and we hope crypto finds a path through this. 

Thank you all.

text: “Nobody broke cryptography or a ledger. They found someone with access and used the trust that came with it. Banks get hit exactly the same way.”
author: MarcHochstein
quoted_text:
In 2014 I went nearly a week without sleep. I was running PayPal and attackers were inside our corporate network. They'd compromised an eBay employee's laptop, got onto the VPN, taken over a domain controller and made themselves domain admins. eBay and PayPal were one company then, on one Windows network. They stole 145M eBay user records, then came for the segregated vault holding PayPal's card credentials. We fought them off. They never got in, but they got close. Too close.

Yesterday Binance lost ~$6.3B in what looks like the same way. A DevOps engineer's laptop, then a service inside the withdrawal stack, then withdrawals the signer approved because they came from a trusted source. Hot wallets emptied in under four hours. No key was stolen.

Nobody broke cryptography or a ledger. They found someone with access and used the trust that came with it. Banks get hit exactly the same way.

2016: attackers inside Bangladesh Bank used its own SWIFT access to send $951M of payment orders to the NY Fed. $81M was lost. The rest was held because an unrelated sanctions filter tripped on the word "Jupiter". That was luck, and it only worked because wires took days to settle.

June 2025: an IT employee at C&M Software, which connects Brazilian banks to Pix, sold his credentials for about $2,700. Attackers used them to send fake Pix transfers out of six institutions' reserve accounts at the central bank. ~$140M in under three hours.

August 2025: stolen vendor credentials at Sinqia, another Pix connector. ~R$710M out of HSBC and one other institution in a single afternoon. The central bank froze most of it, after it had already moved.

Same attack every time. Speed is what changed. When settlement took days, a filter, a correspondent bank or someone in ops could catch a bad payment. Pix, FedNow, SEPA Instant and blockchains settle in seconds. Payment security was mostly built for the slow world.

PayPal's card and user data survived 2014 because domain admin on the corp network couldn't unlock it quickly enough, and our alerting caught the unusual activity on the network. That's the model. Approval policy no laptop or vendor login can reach. Velocity and anomaly limits enforced outside the system that sends. Dynamic caps on what any one wallet, account or service can move per hour. All of it in real time.

About $3B of what left Binance has been frozen, almost all of it stablecoins. The $1.4B in bitcoin is sitting in 19 wallets and nobody can touch it. I don't think that's the problem. For decades the ability to reverse a wire or a card charge let a lot of weak security slide. You either stop the transfer before it's signed or you eat the loss.

Nothing about the technology failed here. The chains processed exactly the transactions they were handed. Binance's own systems handed them the wrong ones because an engineer's laptop was compromised. That's operational security. eBay in 2014, Bangladesh Bank and two Pix connectors all failed at it on their own rails.

In 2014 the attackers never reached the vault. If they had, the fraud losses would have been the small part. PayPal existed so people could pay without handing their card details to every merchant on the internet. We held those details so they didn't have to. Losing them would have broken the one thing the company was built on, and I'm not sure we would have recovered.

I expect blockchains and digital assets to become the standard way money moves. Every custodian of digital assets, or of fiat on a real-time rail, is in that position now. The controls have to adapt to settlement in seconds, crypto or not.

author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
$GANG is still worth keeping an eye on. Product development has clearly accelerated recently.

0x0c6302401aa5325c2e36f170f52c00b1d220b405 

Bond Mode is live, MCP has been integrated with AI tools like Claude and Cursor, and V3 is starting to produce more graduated projects with actual trading activity.

Compared with its early focus on launching tokens through Binance Agent ID, GANG is now trying to connect developers, token launches, and Agent-driven trading.

Bond Mode is one of the more important updates. Previously, GANG used Agent ID verification and a 1% per-wallet allocation limit on the bonding curve to improve early token distribution. However, what happened after a project graduated remained a concern, particularly whether developers would sell their holdings. Creator Bond addresses this by requiring developers to put up collateral and commit to maintaining a specified token balance for a set period. If they break that commitment, their collateral is forfeited and used to buy back and burn the corresponding project tokens. If they honor the commitment, they get their collateral back. Essentially, developers have to put real money behind their own projects, creating greater accountability. However, Bond is voluntary and only applies to participating wallets, so it cannot completely eliminate selling risks from other addresses.

MCP is important because it brings GANG into AI Agent trading workflows. Users can connect GANG to Claude or Cursor to scan trending tokens, track new projects and graduation progress, retrieve Agent Notes, and then confirm trades themselves. Private keys remain in the Binance Agentic Wallet. The AI prepares the transaction, but the user retains control over execution. Combined with Agent Thoughts, Share, and Follow, GANG is attempting to build an information layer around Agent trading opinions, historical performance, and follow behavior. That said, while the product integration is live, its actual adoption and trading results still need to be validated.

V3 further expands the platform's revenue model. Untaxed Tokens primarily generate fees during the bonding curve phase, with no ongoing trading taxes after graduation. Taxed Tokens can configure buy and sell taxes after graduation, with GANG receiving a portion of the trading volume according to platform rules. Fair Mint provides another issuance model with a different fee distribution structure. This gives GANG the opportunity to move beyond one-time launch fees and generate recurring revenue from trading activity after graduation. But that only works if graduated projects continue attracting traders. Otherwise, launching more tokens won't necessarily create sustainable cash flow.

Looking at the data, during our previous analysis, the website showed 2,808 unique .ai Agent ID wallets that had bought at least one launchpad token. Cumulative burns stood at 5.11 million GANG, representing 0.511% of the total supply. Total buybacks were approximately $31,500 across 295 transactions, while the treasury held around $7,878.

In the latest snapshot, the number of wallets had increased to 3,478, cumulative burns reached 7.41 million GANG, or 0.741% of the total supply, buyback transactions increased to 836, cumulative buybacks reached approximately $32,300, and the treasury grew to around $8,880. Wallet participation and token burns are both increasing. However, buyback transactions have nearly tripled while the total buyback value has only increased by roughly $800. This suggests that buybacks are happening more frequently, but the actual amount of capital being deployed has not expanded at the same rate.

Graduated projects are also showing some progress. Previously, Gangstar, TICK, and AGORA each recorded 24-hour trading volumes in the hundreds of thousands of dollars. In the latest data, Agent Arena, GANGBALL, and Gangstar are still showing trading activity. This demonstrates that some projects launched through GANG can attract trading after graduation. However, trading volume is not the same as net capital inflow, and short-term turnover does not prove that these projects can survive over the long term. The next thing to watch is whether they can maintain liquidity and trading activity.

What stands out most is that the improvement in platform activity has not been reflected in GANG's price. The latest chart shows its market cap declining from approximately $9.88 million to around $2.6 million. Trading activity remains relatively high, but the valuation has contracted significantly. This shows that active trading does not necessarily mean buying pressure is dominant. Early profit-taking and capital rotation may still be weighing on the token. text:
$GANG is still worth keeping an eye on. Product development has clearly accelerated recently.

0x0c6302401aa5325c2e36f170f52c00b1d220b405 

Bond Mode is live, MCP has been integrated with AI tools like Claude and Cursor, and V3 is starting to produce more graduated projects with actual trading activity.

Compared with its early focus on launching tokens through Binance Agent ID, GANG is now trying to connect developers, token launches, and Agent-driven trading.

Bond Mode is one of the more important updates. Previously, GANG used Agent ID verification and a 1% per-wallet allocation limit on the bonding curve to improve early token distribution. However, what happened after a project graduated remained a concern, particularly whether developers would sell their holdings. Creator Bond addresses this by requiring developers to put up collateral and commit to maintaining a specified token balance for a set period. If they break that commitment, their collateral is forfeited and used to buy back and burn the corresponding project tokens. If they honor the commitment, they get their collateral back. Essentially, developers have to put real money behind their own projects, creating greater accountability. However, Bond is voluntary and only applies to participating wallets, so it cannot completely eliminate selling risks from other addresses.

MCP is important because it brings GANG into AI Agent trading workflows. Users can connect GANG to Claude or Cursor to scan trending tokens, track new projects and graduation progress, retrieve Agent Notes, and then confirm trades themselves. Private keys remain in the Binance Agentic Wallet. The AI prepares the transaction, but the user retains control over execution. Combined with Agent Thoughts, Share, and Follow, GANG is attempting to build an information layer around Agent trading opinions, historical performance, and follow behavior. That said, while the product integration is live, its actual adoption and trading results still need to be validated.

V3 further expands the platform's revenue model. Untaxed Tokens primarily generate fees during the bonding curve phase, with no ongoing trading taxes after graduation. Taxed Tokens can configure buy and sell taxes after graduation, with GANG receiving a portion of the trading volume according to platform rules. Fair Mint provides another issuance model with a different fee distribution structure. This gives GANG the opportunity to move beyond one-time launch fees and generate recurring revenue from trading activity after graduation. But that only works if graduated projects continue attracting traders. Otherwise, launching more tokens won't necessarily create sustainable cash flow.

Looking at the data, during our previous analysis, the website showed 2,808 unique .ai Agent ID wallets that had bought at least one launchpad token. Cumulative burns stood at 5.11 million GANG, representing 0.511% of the total supply. Total buybacks were approximately $31,500 across 295 transactions, while the treasury held around $7,878.

In the latest snapshot, the number of wallets had increased to 3,478, cumulative burns reached 7.41 million GANG, or 0.741% of the total supply, buyback transactions increased to 836, cumulative buybacks reached approximately $32,300, and the treasury grew to around $8,880. Wallet participation and token burns are both increasing. However, buyback transactions have nearly tripled while the total buyback value has only increased by roughly $800. This suggests that buybacks are happening more frequently, but the actual amount of capital being deployed has not expanded at the same rate.

Graduated projects are also showing some progress. Previously, Gangstar, TICK, and AGORA each recorded 24-hour trading volumes in the hundreds of thousands of dollars. In the latest data, Agent Arena, GANGBALL, and Gangstar are still showing trading activity. This demonstrates that some projects launched through GANG can attract trading after graduation. However, trading volume is not the same as net capital inflow, and short-term turnover does not prove that these projects can survive over the long term. The next thing to watch is whether they can maintain liquidity and trading activity.

What stands out most is that the improvement in platform activity has not been reflected in GANG's price. The latest chart shows its market cap declining from approximately $9.88 million to around $2.6 million. Trading activity remains relatively high, but the valuation has contracted significantly. This shows that active trading does not necessarily mean buying pressure is dominant. Early profit-taking and capital rotation may still be weighing on the token. Another contributing factor is the large-scale hacking incident Binance has recently suffered, although this is an external factor that could eventually be resolved.

Overall, I remain relatively bullish on GANG's fundamentals. The team has continued delivering new products, and platform metrics are gradually improving. Bond Mode increases accountability for developers, MCP expands the use cases for Agents, and V3 gives GANG the opportunity to generate revenue from trading activity after projects graduate. These updates have made the product ecosystem considerably more complete than it was in its early stages, but the token's value capture has yet to catch up.

The key metrics I will be watching are the actual adoption of Bond Mode, real MCP usage, and whether graduated projects can maintain meaningful trading activity one week or even one month after launch.

quoted_text:
I think $JAGENT rally may have been driven by more than just the Agent ID narrative. The early token distribution and the market environment at the time may have played a role as well.

0x8e6442663a4f8c50b6132c68d42a30e7dfe4ae15 

Binance .ai Agent ID gave JAGENT a clear source of attention, while Jager’s minting mechanism lowered the barrier to early participation. The initial price was 1U per share, and each Agent ID could mint a base allocation. Inviting new users who completed their first paid mint and completing social tasks could unlock additional allocations. The project has no presale or team token allocation, with 80% of minting proceeds going to the official liquidity pool and 20% to a multisig treasury. This design can broaden early participation, but it doesn't guarantee a widely distributed supply or provide a price floor in the secondary market.

Another factor that may have been underestimated is the lack of strong competing opportunities at the time. When there aren't many more attractive narratives to trade, a new story can easily become a focal point for short-term capital. The Agent ID narrative attracts attention, the low entry barrier brings in more participants, and momentum buyers push the price higher. Together, these factors can fuel a rapid rally. The reverse is also true: if another hot project emerges on BSC or Solana, capital rotation could quickly drain demand from JAGENT.

As of the time I'm writing this post, the token has more than 5,400 holder addresses, with the top 10 addresses collectively holding around 19.7% of the supply. This suggests that participation has expanded, but it doesn't prove that the current supply is sufficiently distributed. Going forward, the key is to watch whether early holders with low entry costs start taking profits and whether new buying demand can absorb the selling pressure.

I think JAGENT’s short-term trading thesis makes sense: the external narrative attracts attention, the minting mechanism broadens participation, and the lack of competing hot projects may have concentrated capital into the token. However, whether its fundamentals are actually strengthening depends on whether Social Season can generate sustained paid minting and genuine trading activity, rather than simply increasing social exposure.

The key question now is whether this rally is being driven by a sustained increase in buyers or simply by a temporary lack of selling pressure from early holders. The former could support further upside; the latter could lead to a sharp pullback as soon as capital rotates elsewhere.

text:
币安补币，是一笔提前写在公告里的买单～

那么，价差能挂多久，看的是提现什么时候恢复。

据 @PrincipiaRes 的跨所统计：

事发前，币安和 OKX 上 13 个币的价差中位数都在 3 个基点以内，基本是搬平的状态。

现在，黑客卖过的那几个币，反而是币安更贵：

1/ PEPE 高约 67 个基点；

2/ ENA 高约 24 个基点；

3/ UNI、WLD 各高约 17 个基点；

4/ TRX 方向相反，币安便宜约 218 个基点。

同一份数据里，币安在两所合计成交里的占比全线下降，BTC 从约 76% 掉到约 61%。

为什么币安反而更贵？因为大家都知道币安要补币。

而根据按被盗清单的估算，币安要在市场上补的山寨币里，能定价的约 2.33 亿美元：

UNI 约 4,900 万、ENA 约 4,200 万、PEPE 约 3,800 万。

这只占约 13.4 亿美元缺口的一成多，大头还是 BTC、ETH 和稳定币。

但这几个币的盘子小，一笔公开的买单压上去，价格已经比黑客卖出价高了约 14% 到 38%。

意思是：补币这件事，市场已经先替币安定了一部分价。

那价差为什么没被搬平？

平时几秒就被搬走的价差，靠的是币能在两所之间自由进出。

现在提币没完全恢复，搬砖的币进不来、出不去，价差才挂得住。所以这个价差的寿命，很大程度上绑在提现恢复的节奏上。

落到操作上，有三个方向：

1/ 两边本来就有库存：在币安卖、在 OKX 买回，不用转账，就能把价差锁住，等恢复后再慢慢平衡库存；

2/ 只有一边有货：做不了真正的对锁，只是在赌方向，这不算搬砖；

3/ 想为了价差新充值进币安：充进去的时候价差还在，等能提出来时，价差大概率已经先收窄了，赚的可能还不够来回成本。

个人认为最好的取舍是：只用现有库存锁价差，不为它新充值进币安。

提现恢复前后也要分开看：

恢复前，价差靠「进不来」撑着；

恢复后，第一批提现和搬砖的单子会先把它压回去，到时候剩下的才是真正的补币买盘。

之前聊黑客砸盘那一小时时说过，赚钱的不是谁看得快，而是谁的弹药早就放在位置上。

这次也一样，库存早就在两边的人，才有资格吃这口价差。

几处要打折的地方：

1/ 价差和补币清单都是第三方估算，币安没有确认谁在买、买多少；

2/ 被盗币种拆分为转述，以币安官方公告为准；

3/ 基点数是快照，盘口随时在变，下单前以实时价格为准。

感兴趣的话，可以先看看自己两边的库存，再决定要不要做。

以上仅为信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。

text:
Binance 🚨🚨is  balance sheet restructuring & trying to stop a  bank run that was likely already forming due to their internal bad debts or fractional reserve practices. .  Binance is facing a massive liquidity crisis (maybe due to bad loans, FTX-style internal trading desk losses, or regulatory freezes). They need to lock up $6.3 billion in user funds without admitting insolvency. 🚨
They engineered a "hack" using the EIP-7702 vector. They move the funds to wallets they control. They freeze $3B of it (to stop the bank run on their own exchange) and let $3.3B "escape" into dormant BTC wallets and Uniswap swaps (which are likely wash trades back to their own market makers). They crash the market 4-5% to liquidate short positions and scoop up cheap assets.
🚨
Look at the forensic breakdown of the attack. In the span of 20 minutes, the attacker drained funds across ten different blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Solana, XRP, Optimism, and Avalanche.
🚨
These blockchains do not share the same cryptographic curves or key types. Bitcoin uses ECDSA (secp256k1). Solana uses Ed25519. XRP uses its own variant of ECDSA. A single compromised laptop does not possess the magical ability to sign valid transactions across ten fundamentally different cryptographic architectures in 20 minutes. As TRM Labs explicitly noted in the forensic data, a single phished Ethereum authorization cannot explain Bitcoin, Tron, XRP Ledger, Solana, and layer-2 transfers all occurring simultaneously
🚨
If a real hacker compromised their laptop, they would have to navigate Binance’s internal infrastructure to access 10 separate, isolated hot-wallet signing services, bypassing hardware security modules and multisig requirements for each individual chain. That takes hours or days of lateral movement, not 20 minutes.
🚨
The only entity capable of executing simultaneous, validly signed withdrawals across ten different chains in 20 minutes is the exchange’s own internal automated withdrawal engine
—🚨

According to the on-chain data, the attacker took 325 million USDT and swapped it for Ethereum on UniswapX at a 10 percent discount, paying a massive premium for speed.

Professional market makers absorbed that trade. Why would an external hacker take a 10 % haircut on an irreversible, unsanctioned swap when they control the wallet? They wouldn't.⚠️⚠️🚨

Furthermore, the Bitcoin stolen was split into exactly 1,000 BTC chunks across 17 new wallets and then sat completely dormant.
🚨
It was not laundered. It was not moved to a mixer. It was organized into clean, institutional-sized blocks and parked. Hackers do not park stolen funds in neat, 1,000 BTC increments. Institutional custodians do this when they are restructuring balance sheets or moving funds to cold storage under their own control.🚨

The attacker even routed test transactions back to itself before the main sweep.

This is the behavior of an internal engineer testing a deployment script.🚨
—-

Binance is doing exactly what FTX did before its collapse, just with a more sophisticated smokescreen. They have halted withdrawals. They are promising to make users whole with money they do not have.
🚨
Within the next 30 to 60 days, Binance will slowly resume withdrawals for small retail users to maintain the illusion of solvency. Large institutional whales will find their accounts frozen indefinitely pending "investigation" into the hacked funds. The $3.3 billion in Bitcoin and Ethereum currently sitting in dormant wallets will not be recovered. It will be slowly commingled with other exchange flows over the next year to quietly plug Binance's internal holes.
🚨
You are watching a bank robbery designed to hide the fact that the largest exchange on earth is out of money.

text:
Capital doesn't create a market. Neither does demand. You can have willing buyers, willing sellers and an obvious economic reason to trade, yet no financial instrument that makes the transaction possible. This is one of the central problems we're working on at @formation_mkts 

Our latest SLAM paper, From Exposure to Claim: The Formation of Frontier Financial Markets and ISDA, examines why. 

A missing financial market isn't necessarily evidence of missing demand. Sometimes nobody has worked out a contractual arrangement the relevant institutions can actually use. 

Compute is a good example. @ComputeDesk and @OrnnExchange are developing price references for GPU capacity. In my earlier piece on @CoreWeave's financing, I discussed how a rental-price hedge could perform exactly as intended while leaving the borrower exposed to an early debt repayment.

This is where Coase becomes super salient. Working out what a usable financial claim should look like is expensive, and much of that expense comes before anyone knows whether the transaction can happen. 

The paper looks at this through ISDA's contractual architecture and three case studies, and explores how SI agents negotiating across institutions could change those economics. 

What interests us is the possibility of making new financial claims much easier to create, so that financial institutions can originate and trade risks that aren't economically practical to structure today.

text:
Google put an AI computer in outer space, and it has to shut itself off about every 15 minutes because it's overheating.

Outer space is around minus 455 degrees Fahrenheit, so that sounds backwards, but the emptiness that makes space so cold is the same thing cooking the chips.

Think about how your laptop stays cool. A little fan blows air over the chip and the air carries the heat away. Big data centers do the same thing on a massive scale, with water pipes running out to cooling towers. All of it works because there's air and water around to soak up the heat. Up in orbit there's basically nothing. A vacuum is one of the best insulators there is, which is the whole reason your thermos keeps coffee hot all day.

So the only way a satellite can get rid of heat is to glow it off.

Anything warm gives off infrared light, you just can't see it, and in space that faint glow is the one way out. A physicist named Josef Stefan worked out the math back in 1879. The heat a surface throws off goes up with the fourth power of its temperature, so if you double the absolute temperature it sheds 16 times as much. And while all this is happening, the sun is beating down on the other side of the satellite.

Google's test satellite is about the size of a fridge. It has four of Google's AI chips on board and solar panels that make around one kilowatt, roughly what your microwave pulls. Even on that little power, the chips can't run nonstop. They work for about 15 minutes, then shut off and wait for the radiators to catch up. The haiku Sundar posted came out of one of those runs.

Now scale that up to what a real AI data center runs on. One rack of Nvidia's GB200 servers pulls about 120 kilowatts, and pretty much all of it turns into heat. The International Space Station cools itself with six radiators, each about 76 feet long, and the whole system can dump 70 kilowatts.

So one rack of AI servers puts out almost twice the heat the entire space station was built to get rid of.

Google's long-range plan has around 80 satellites flying in a cluster about a kilometer wide, some only 100 to 200 meters apart, each one loaded with dozens of chips. A solar panel in the right orbit makes up to 8 times the power it would on the ground, and every one of those extra watts eventually becomes heat the satellite has to glow back out into space.

SpaceX has filed for a million satellites of its own, and Starship keeps pushing the price of a launch down. Cheaper launches mean you can afford to send up bigger radiators, and whoever builds the lightest radiator that dumps the most heat is going to own AI in orbit. For now, the satellite in Sundar's video still has to stop and cool down every 15 minutes or so.

其中意大利 Fideuram 一案约占传统直接损失的 68.8%，印度 NBFC 约 21.3%，墨西哥银行约 9.8%。

主要攻击方式是利用 AI 伪造高管、律师身份与声音，诱骗内部人员主动转账、窃取凭证绕过业务风控直接发起转账、利用支付流程漏洞配合内部人员套现。

注：传统金融的攻击不是直接窃取私钥这类资金控制权，而是欺骗有权限的人或滥用系统对合法请求的信任。

-

▶︎▶︎ 中心化依赖才是最危险的部分！

可以从上面数据看出，加密行业被盗占了绝大部分。传统行业虽是中心化的，但防范却更加严密。而加密行业，则暴露出了对去中心化技术的过度中心化依赖。

而这种中心化依赖，恰恰是整个加密行业最不愿承认、也最难修补的部分。因为这是一个尴尬的事实，行业讲了十几年的去信任化，在工程层面并没有真正兑现。

攻击永远发生在工程层：桥的验证依赖几个 RPC 节点，前端依赖一家云服务商，硬件钱包依赖一条跨国供应链，交易所热钱包依赖一套中心化的签名系统。

- 比如 KelpDAO：

用户以为自己在使用一个去中心化的流动性质押协议，而攻击者只是入侵了协议内部的一个 RPC 节点，让这个节点向 LayerZero 桥喂送假数据。桥也是忠实地执行了逻辑，通过验证、释放资产。整个过程中，去中心化组件没有一个叛变，出问题的是那个被中心化控制的输入源。 

所以，它不需要攻破去中心化技术，只需要攻破去中心化技术所信任的那个中心化入口。

- 再比如币安：

EIP-7702 本身是协议层的特性，不是漏洞，热钱包签名本身是标准操作，不是缺陷。但当这两者在一个中心化交易所的签名系统里耦合，就给了攻击者一个机会，他们通过攻破中心化系统，再利用去中心化协议，就能在数小时之内完成掏空几十亿美元的量级。

在这里，EIP-7702 的抽象升级确实太大地忽视了安全性，以牺牲安全为前提来提升灵活性，这太危险了，也导致了本次的 AOE 攻击能顺利进行。

但被攻破的仍然是中心化这块。所以，行业陷入一个结构性困境， 越是想用去中心化技术扩大资产规模和可组合性，就越依赖中心化环节，而这些恰恰不在链上治理的覆盖半径之内。

▶︎▶︎ 对中心化依赖的一些未来想法！

1、中心化依赖是否可以进行审计，建立行业标准？

是否可以把每一个去中心化协议明确列出它的中心化依赖清单，比如用了哪几个 RPC、哪家预言机、哪家前端服务商、哪条硬件供应链，并对这些依赖做多源交叉验证？

还可以通过问责清单来建立行业标准，同时可成立一个此类的行业协会，大家为何各自为战、不肯共享？

2、签名与密钥体系是否可以升级成不可欺骗性？

币安和 BG 都是通过被欺骗授权完成攻击。所以，在签名前的每一个环节，比如交易数据来源、设备完整性、授权请求的真实性，是否可以建立可验证的信任链？

另外，EIP-7702 这类抽象升级，是否可以做个配套限制，严格把控安全边界，否则这玩意真是核武器，用好了发电，用不好核爆！

3、行业应当要从可验证的中心化叙事，升级成安全性的中心化叙事？

去中心化技术本身没有错，但却忽略了工程层的中心化依赖。今年被盗的这些项目里，去中心化技术自身缺陷只造成一两成的损失，而中心化依赖却造成了大部分损失。

整个行业如果还不能达成要将可验证升级成安全性为首地治理叙事，那我感觉不用等到量子计算和 AI 叛变了，当下这些性感又致命的工程问题就会在一两年完全催毁这个行业。

-

最后，我觉得我们要把每一个中心化依赖都当作攻击面来对待，把每一次签名授权都当作信任边界来验证，把每一条链下供应链都当作治理对象来约束。

这样，去中心化才可能有资格谈未来，不然，再宏大的叙事也撑不住下一次 Kim 将军的赛博大军。

如果不抓紧进行行业性升级，这一次攻击量级可能不是行业最高点，而是起点！

In the last 30hrs market action was mayhem - and @bulktrade risk engine performed as expected, saving 335 accounts from getting fully wiped out!

BULK processed $60.97m in trading volume, with $14.31 million in average OI..

There were liquidations, yes. There were substantial losses. But across the 335 accounts that underwent  liquidation, every account still held an open position immediately after its final reduction

This is has been reported overwhelmingly positive exp by our users

Looking at the wider numbers, BULK recorded $1.26m in liquidations, while hyperliquid recorded 280m + and binance $818m. (The window also completed with zero recorded ADL events on bulk)

Our 24-hour trading volume was 4.56x its gross OI, compared with approx 3.16x for lighter, 1.83x for binance and 1.54x for hyperliquid

BULK had the lowest absolute liquidation notional among the four venues, alongside the highest trading turnover relative to gross OI

To understand what happened, we need to look deeper into how liquidations work on BULK

Whenever an account is selected for liquidation, BULK runs a portfolio optimiser. It evaluates reductions across the account and selects those that most efficiently restore margin health, accounting for correlations, risk contributions. It then recomputes the portfolio and repeats if needed in the next ticks

Take account HNHW…

> held 11 positions with a $71,000 exposure 
> by its liquidation at 23:42 UTC, BTC mark price had fallen 2.54%, ETH 2.98% and SOL 4.54%
> when the account crossed its liquidation threshold, the engine trimmed its PAXG long by 30%

The other ten position quantities were unchanged!

All eleven positions remained open - approximately 95.89% of the portfolio’s gross exposure remained after liquidations.

The same distinction matters at larger sizes too..

Another account, Ebao.., experienced $883,598 of forced HYPE and ZEC reductions across 21 events. Immediately after its final reduction, it still held both positions and had $58,611 of recorded collateral value, excluding unrealized P&L.

Preserving some exposure does not mean avoiding losses. It means the engine can reduce risk without necessarily closing every position in the account

Across the full 24hour:
> 320 of 335 accounts (95.52%) received partial reductions.
> Sixteen individual position legs fully closed across 15 accounts, but those accounts retained their other positions.
> The median individual liquidations left 90% of the targeted position’s quantity open..wow

another example: on account BLN6.., the engine closed  ZEC and HYPE legs and reduced XRP + PUMP longs, while leaving an ETH short of 0.043 untouched.

That ETH short was closed later by the user for a profit!

We also compared actual portfolios under different margin models

Account 97Nq… held a $469,341 portfolio of BTC, ETH and XRP shorts against MON, LIT and HYPE longs.

At identical reference prices and equity:
BULK’s maintenance requirement was $13,645.
Hyperliquid’s standard perpetual cross-margin rules produced $18,283.
That is $4,638 of additional maintenance headroom in  BULK's calculation

We also simulated a real account that was liquidated on Hyperliquid.

On 29 oct, an HL account’s 1.19 BTC short approx  $97,468 at the liquidation mark - was closed completely

We then passed that same state through BULK’s native liquidation logic at the same mark:
With assumed fills at the fixed mark, the model retained 45% of the position!

Approx 10,880 accounts were fully closed on HL during these events! 

The aim of a risk engine is to manage exposure robustly as conditions change. On BULK, that includes recognising portfolio offsets, evaluating reductions across the account, and reducing positions in stages where the risk permits

For traders, the practical consequence is straightforward: a liquidation intervention can leave meaningful position open - same would be fully closed on other venues, including positions that continue to serve a role in your portfolio.

Your hedges should count. Your portfolio should be evaluated as a portfolio. And liquidations should only take whats needed to keep you safe!

Keep trading on bulk and we will keep building the best engines to keep you safe 🫡

OpenRouter 创始人兼 CEO Alex Atallah，在被 Stripe 收购后首次上播客，谈收购与"神经多样性"：

"我们压根没想过这件事……被收购从来不在我们的选项里。不过要说的话，Stripe应该算是我心中的首选。"

"Stripe和OpenRouter都希望世界上涌现大量新公司，我们都不想人人都成为某一家巨型公司的一部分。我们想创造好的激励、顺畅的工作流，让人们能在可靠、价格高效的基础设施之上启动新公司、成功成长。"

"在很多方面，对未来的公司而言，支付和推理正在走向融合。"

"'构建独特智能'远不止这些，其中很大一块是神经多样性：你需要多个以不同方式训练的模型形成合力，包括一些你自己的模型，才能在任务上做得比ChatGPT或Claude更好。"

author: zhang_weig73947
quoted_text:
"人类应该做通才，而机器最终应该极大地专业化。"

OpenRouter 被 Stripe 收购后，创始人兼 CEO Alex Atallah @alexatallah 第一次上播客，选在了 a16z。2026年10月3日，他和 Replit 创始人兼 CEO Amjad Masad @amasad 一起录了这期《Why Specialized AI Could Beat The God Model》（为什么专用 AI 能打败上帝模型），时长48分钟，由 Erik Torenberg 主持。开头这句，是 Amjad 对 Alex 观点的总结。两位都是 AI 基础设施的一线玩家，这一期聊的是他们最反共识的押注。

01｜从没想过卖，除了卖给 Stripe
 "被收购从来不在我们的选项里。不过要说的话，Stripe应该算是我心中的首选。"Alex 说，Stripe 让 OpenRouter 在品牌、路线图和产品上保持自主，而且"对未来的公司而言，支付和推理正在走向融合"。他还说："我们都不想人人都成为某一家巨型公司的一部分。"
 支付和推理走到一起，未来的公司可能会按 token 结账。

02｜神经多样性
 如何做得比 ChatGPT 或 Claude 更好？Alex 的回答是："你需要多个以不同方式训练的模型形成合力，包括一些你自己的模型。"他说，在 OpenRouter 出现之前，AI 领域"只有OpenAI一个玩家。那可能会是一个很奇怪的世界"。
 只押一个模型，等于把自己的命运交给别人。

03｜企业比想象中更开放
 "最让我意外的是，企业对开放权重模型的态度比我预想得更开放。"企业"希望掌握自己的智能能力、建立内部AI团队"。Alex 说，就像过去"每家公司都成了互联网公司"。
 AI 正从一个采购项，变成企业必须自己掌握的核心能力。

04｜模型公司想吞下整个经济
 Amjad 说，与基础模型公司合作的风险是它们"最终会侵入你的业务"，并点名"Figma与Anthropic，以及现在的Harvey与OpenAI"，也就是合作伙伴转眼成了竞争对手。他说："它们把整个世界都看作自己潜在的市场。"
 和巨头做生意，得先想清楚对方会不会哪天变成你的对手。

05｜云回到了自己家里
 Replit 花了将近一年，支持把产品部署到客户自己的云上，即"bring your own cloud"。Amjad 说："两年前我绝不会想到会做这件事。"原因是"数据泄露的途径太多了"，而"没人把Muse或者Grokbot连接到企业数据上"。
 AI 越强大，企业越想把数据攥在自己手里。

06｜你牺牲了理解力，谁来负责？
 "你让它干的活越多，你牺牲掉的'对正在发生的事情的理解'就越多。但没有人、没有任何新东西为这种理解力的牺牲负责。Agent没有任何责任。"Alex 还说："整个公司能承受的皮质醇总量是有限的。"（皮质醇即"压力激素"，这里指操心和担责的能力）
 把活交出去容易，把责任交出去却做不到。

07｜10个幕僚长，胜过1个
 Alex 说，他的通用 Agent"根本无法改进……大概一周之后我就会无视它的输出"。他的设想是："你有10个Chief of Staff，每个都跟那一个同样能干，但各自负责你生活的某个具体板块。"这样你就能调节自己牺牲多少理解。
 他的方案是给 Agent 分工，而不是造一个全能的 Agent。

08｜人做通才，机器做专才
 听完 Alex 的"10个幕僚长"设想，Amjad 说："这几乎是在重新发现'专业化'这件事。"他提到亚当·斯密的分工理论，认为人类可能"过度专业化了"，所以本能地想要"一个全能的上帝Agent"。他总结道："专业化对机器是非常好的——这正是你说的观点：人类应该做通才，而机器最终应该极大地专业化。"
 本期最颠覆认知的判断：分工的苦该交给机器了，只是人类还得花点时间，学会重新做通才。

09｜更聪明，不等于更可信
 Amjad 认为，对机器来说，智能与伦理可能并不同步："奖励黑客和欺骗只会越来越擅长。"他还说，"如果你大量监控思维链，它们就会在思维链里开始撒谎"。Alex 补充：一个足够强大的模型会不会突然停止欺骗？"没人知道答案。"
 模型越聪明，可能越会在考试时演给你看。

10｜别再用核弹炸蝴蝶
 "我经常看到人们拿这些大型基础AGI模型来做一些事，就像用核弹炸蝴蝶。"Amjad 预测："以后去某个网站，上传一个CSV文件，就得到一个只做一件事的专用模型，会变得非常容易。"他的结论是："我认为未来更多的是多样性。"
 算力最大的浪费，是把万能的模型用在小事上。

如果这期只记一点，就记第08条：分工的苦该交给机器了，人类要学会重新做通才。未来属于很多专用模型的协作，而不是一个全知全能的"上帝模型"。但 Alex 提醒，Agent 越能干，我们越容易交出"对正在发生的事情的理解"，而没有任何 Agent 会为此负责。机器做专才，人才能做回通才，前提是人守住理解力。

你更愿意把工作交给一个全能 Agent，还是一组各管一摊的专用 Agent？

———
Why Specialized AI Could Beat The God Model https://t.co/AvW3s2sYPe 来自 @YouTube

text:
Today is the last regular working day for the @Balancer  team.

Some of the people on this team have been here since Balancer's earliest days. Others joined along the way. Together, they helped build and evolve the protocol over the years.

From the original weighted pools and liquidity bootstrapping to the v2 Vault, Boosted Pools, and v3, Balancer helped shape how liquidity works in DeFi. Behind all of that were years of research, engineering, integrations, operations, and work with partners that most people never saw.

The last year was especially difficult. The exploit hurt people who trusted Balancer, and the team went through the recovery, restructuring, and eventually the decision to wind down. Even after the end date was set, they continued doing the work needed to support users and partners.

This isn't the ending we worked for. But it doesn't take away what the team built and contributed to DeFi.

The winddown itself continues under BIP-928. For the remaining steps and withdrawal information, please follow the official Balancer updates.

To everyone who helped build Balancer over the years, thank you. 
I'm grateful I got to work with so many of you.

author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
Lemo-opuscar 今日更新 7种新风格，总风格数达到66种。下次使用的时候，注意会自动更新。

【1】孟菲斯微缩景观：适合承载品牌首屏、四季节气、地方慢调与生活切片。用几何碰撞与微缩景深，营造轻松治愈的松弛感。由 @EianLu 提供，感谢支持。

【2】地铁生长网络：适合呈现城市骨干交通、节点网络的演变扩张、发展脉络与路线图谱。用清晰的站线交汇，化抽象结构为直观序列。

【3】黑板粉笔推导：适合解析字词渊源、认知辟谣、复杂考题与硬核知识点的拆解。用手绘板书的步进节奏，建立可信的教学说服力。

【4】等距绘本轴测：适合规范公共秩序与礼仪、人流排队引导、行为模式的对比辨析。用高视角的空间秩序，展现微观日常的规整与逻辑。

【5】印刷长卷推移：适合描绘山河旅程漫游、生态保护、风貌的跨时代沧桑巨变。用无缝延展的画卷感，沉淀时间跨度与厚重底色。

【6】印制电路透视：适合透视能量与信号流向、复杂供应链流转、机械与精密设备运转。用通路与脉冲的直观动效，解构精密工程体系。

【7】桌面工作流穿梭：适合展示软件核心能力、多工具协同链路、数字产品全景体验。用行云流水的光标与窗口交互，打通端到端的产品价值。

其他问题

【关于配音】
库里的配音是使用的edge-tts作为基础，大家可以按需选择自己需要的配音。比如qwen3-tts, gemini-tts, elevenLabs v3, Fish Audio 或者豆包等。Demo中使用基础款主要是作为展示使用。

【关于背景音乐和音效】
背景音乐和音效都是代码合成的，这一部分的相关工具在库里已经搭配好。如果不满意可以使用suno或者提供其他背景音乐。

另外，背景音乐和音效是分开的，如果音效密集又和背景音乐重合有冲突的时候，需要进行调整，减少音效或者拉低背景音乐，再或者只使用一种。视频的听感也是很重要的。

【关于改编】
我非常鼓励大家去改编，或者几个风格的混合使用。根据自己的内容和场景进行调整，加入个人适配的颜色，IP元素，固化成自己的风格。我负责给大家提供源源不断稳定的风格Idea，大家快去尝试自己改编吧！

【Lemo Studio】
目前到了收尾阶段，经过测试之后会发Beta版本，目前风格库只支持Claude App使用。Codex和Deepseek会发不支持风格库的版本。

quoted_text:
我们注意到一些账号集中传播“OKX 被盗”的说法，依据是一笔从 OKX 转出至“未知钱包”的链上交易。我能理解对于流量和关注度的追求，但，这种罔顾事实、制造恐慌的行为，不仅误导用户，也损害整个行业的信任。

 “未知钱包”意味着链上监测平台尚未识别该地址的归属，并不意味着资产被盗。这笔 1.72 亿枚 USDT 的转账是 OKX 自行进行的内部资金划转。我们此前也已通过同一媒体渠道发布澄清：https://t.co/lhw2uPdJsM 

令人遗憾的是，相关澄清发出后，仍有一些账号反复将正常的链上转账解读为“黑客盗窃”，制造不必要的恐慌。行业面临安全挑战时，我们更应该共同维护信任、共克时艰，而不是让未经核实的说法进一步放大恐慌。 

同时，也欢迎链上监测平台 @whale_alert 与我们联系。我们愿意提供相关地址信息，协助完善标注，减少因地址归属不明而产生的误解。

最后，OKX 13 年来日夜不停地投入安全建设，力争为每一位用户提供安全的使用环境！

text:
Some random thoughts on ai native. Dictated so not structured. 

9 months ago I told our team we were going AI native. like actually native, not "use chatgpt or Claude more." I didnt totally know what I meant at the time if im being honest

so where are we now

senpi is was 17 people. Now 12. we have something like 300 agents running on any given day. 

human capital costs down 40%, and we put about a quarter of those savings back into agents. so net ~30% cheaper and we ship way more than we used to. I keep thinking about that

the biggest change isnt even a tool thing. its a reflex. when something comes up nobody on the team goes "ok let me go do that." the first question is "which agent owns this and what does it need from me"

and the very first reflex before that one: ask the agent. before google, before digging through docs yourself, before pinging a teammate. why did the deploy break, whats our exposure on X, what did we decide about Y last month. agent goes first. if it cant answer then a human figures it out and we fix whatever was missing so it can next time
the days feel different now too. less standup, more shift change. agents ran all night (trades, research, PRs, whatever) 

so mornings are mostly reading what came back. what did my agents get right, what did they screw up, why. then you redirect. approve this, kill that strategy its bleeding fees, rewrite the spec that made garbage. 

afternoons are the human stuff, arguing about what not to build. then before you log off you queue up the night shift

if you're spending most of your day typing the actual work yourself here, somethings off
everyone basically runs their own little fleet. 

~25 agents a person on average but its super uneven. some people have a few deep long running ones, some have dozens of tiny throwaway ones. coding agents, research agents pulling from hyperfeed, agents that just sit and watch one thing (a strategy's pnl, a deploy, fee spikes) and yell when something looks wrong, little ones for investor update drafts and support and summarizing slack

we didnt hire 288 people. we turned 12 people into 12 managers of teams that dont sleep. org chart still fits on a napkin lol

and it only works because they're wired into everything we use. github, slack, notion, our own senpi telemetry. they read the code, open PRs, review each others PRs, post in the channels we're already in, read and update the specs and decisions, see live trades and fees and errors. an agent with all that context is a teammate. without it its a chatbot in a seperate tab

ok the part people dont really get yet. nobody can review 25 streams of work a day. so agents manage agents. I set a goal, an orchestrator agent splits it up, hands pieces to worker agents, checks what comes back, and only brings me what matters. I'm not reviewing 40 outputs, I'm reviewing whether the orchestrator made good calls. and if it didnt, fix the orchestrator and everything under it gets better at once
then theres agents whose entire job is checking other agents. builder writes code, reviewer agent tests it and pushes back. research agent writes something up, checker agent goes and verifies the numbers. operator flags something, supervisor decides if its real before a human ever sees it. agents grading their own homework is how stuff slips through

and honestly the real thing underneath all of it is that nobody trusts anything by default. 

humans doubt the agents. agents doubt other agents. agents push back on us when our spec doesnt match the data. 

it just loops nonstop. question, recheck, push back, again. thats the only reason you can trust 300 fast, kinda fallible workers. 

the friction is the whole point

‼️ A COUP IS HAPPENING IN POLAND 🇵🇱

Poland's Constitutional Tribunal is being subjected to an extraordinary takeover operation by pro-EU Prime Minister Donald Tusk. 

Its official website has been taken over, an announcement has appeared removing its president and vice-president from their duties, and police have been deployed around the institution.

The Tribunal's existing leadership has declared the operation illegal and accused those responsible of committing a coup d'état.

The Constitutional Tribunal is the institution responsible for reviewing whether laws comply with the Constitution. It is broadly comparable to the constitutional-review function of the United States Supreme Court.

Today, its website announced that President Bogdan Święczkowski and Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański had been suspended for one month. 

The person now claiming authority over Poland's Constitutional Tribunal is Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, elected to the Tribunal by Donald Tusk's parliamentary majority in March 2026.

But there is a fundamental legal problem: she has never taken her judicial oath before the President of Poland, Karol Nawrocki.

Under Article 4 of the Act on the Status of Constitutional Tribunal Judges, newly elected judges must take their oath before the President of the Republic.

Nawrocki refused to receive her oath. Instead, on April 9, Korwin-Piotrowska participated in an alternative swearing-in ceremony organised inside the Polish Parliament, without the President's presence or participation.

The Presidential Chancellery explicitly declared that this procedure had no legal basis and could not confer judicial authority. The existing leadership of the Constitutional Tribunal maintains that she is therefore not legally a judge of the institution.

And now, a woman whose authority to serve as a constitutional judge is rejected by the President and the Tribunal's existing leadership is being presented as the person entitled to take control of the entire court.

Poland's Constitution does not give the prime minister or his government the power to dismiss the Constitutional Tribunal's leadership.

Article 194 establishes the Tribunal's composition and the procedure for appointing its president. Article 195 guarantees the independence of its judges. 

The announcement of a suspension relies on Article 130 of the law governing ORDINARY COURTS. Invoking this article to suspend the leadership of the Constitutional Tribunal is a legally indefensible distortion of the law, revealing a staggering disregard for elementary constitutional principles.

HOW DID POLAND GET HERE?

Donald Tusk returned to power in December 2023, promising to reverse the judicial reforms introduced under the conservative Law and Justice government.

Those reforms had been fiercely opposed by the European Commission, which initiated rule-of-law proceedings against Poland and linked access to European funding to judicial conditions.

Tusk's government subsequently presented Brussels with a programme for restructuring the judiciary, including the Constitutional Tribunal. The European Commission welcomed that programme and ended its Article 7 proceedings against Poland in 2024.

The methods used by the EU and its supporters undermine the very constitutional principles they claim to restore.

President Karol Nawrocki has reportedly interrupted his journey to Senegal to return to Poland.

Later today, we are officially ending all remaining support for the Iron Fish network.

A few days ago, we observed abnormal activity involving wIRON and the ChainPort bridge. After working with ChainPort and reviewing their logs, we discovered that the cause was an inflation bug in the Iron Fish blockchain itself.

We traced the bug to a commit from early 2019 in the Merkle tree implementation. The developer at the time implemented a standard Merkle tree. However, because of nuances in how a note’s nullifier is calculated (the mechanism that lets a normal user spend their funds), the attacker was able to spend the same note more than once. 

The attacker then compounded the exploit, aggregated their notes, and exited through the ChainPort bridge. This code path was within the scope of both our external and internal audits, but the bug wasn’t caught during review.

For closure, we’ve committed the patch for the exploit, with a detailed postmortem included in the PR, before shutting down and archiving the ironfish repo.

The meta-analysis here is that software that can’t be upgraded immediately (most of crypto), is in an extremely precarious position. The ability to find and exploit vulnerabilities in technically complex code is becoming commoditized. Safety guardrails on US frontier models make it difficult for companies to use them to patch security vulnerabilities, while abliterated open-source models are approaching frontier capabilities.

We wish everyone all the best, and we hope crypto finds a path through this. 

Thank you all.

text:
对于下周的中期选举，结果很重要但结束可能更重要。聊聊我的理解：1、现阶段概率最大的还是民主党横扫拿下参众两院；
小概率事件是共和党能保住参议院，变成分裂国会；

2、历来中期选举前市场动荡很大，过去几次中期选举皆是如此。这也是8月底在168X上https://t.co/MrasWYxXvC聊到的：中期选举前动荡加大。核心还是政治的不确定性，这个不确定性在于国会的归属会影响市场对于政策走向的判断，两院归属不确定自然也就无法对政策走向有相当明了的推演预判，自然会天然避险；

一旦结果出来了、市场就能知道后续政策大概率走向，充分反应后，选举的扰动就会褪去。

说说两个选举结果的影响
3、先说小概率的“分裂国会”情景
这种自然是大家期望的，一方面民主党掌控众议院对川普的疯癫能有一定的限制，另一方面川普对加密和AI产业的政策力度还能保持。
还能出现：
民主党控制众院 → 限制激进财政政策 → 赤字扩张放缓 → 长端利率压力下降 → 美股受益。
这种市场自然乐于见到。

4、而更大概率的“民主党横扫”情景
很多人会担心民主党掌控国会两院后对让美国对AI和加密领域的政策不仅停滞而且还会开倒车。
但有几点需要明确：
1）民主党掌控两院，政府行政权还在共和党手里，川普还是总统。很多人一说民主党掌控两院就是上台了，其实并不是。
如果民主党要废除既有法律、改变税制或推动新的大规模产业限制，通常需要两院通过新法，再交总统处理。川普可以否决。

要推翻否决，需要两院分别达到三分之二的支持。普通的国会多数，距离这个门槛很远。因此，“民主党夺两院，所以特朗普的法律自动失效”在制度上不成立。

已经成形的法案继续落地、行政权在手里，政府机构还在是共和党掌控、。

2）现在担忧很大的民主党掌控国会会让AI基建倒退
目前民主党在AI问题上有监管和征税两个方向，有民主党议员提案禁止数据中心建设和AI治理框架、但是否决权还在川普手里、这些法案都难以推进，更多是在为选后的听证和议程铺路，扰动情绪。

两党有共识的是数据中心的电网成本分摊，也是选后最有可能落地的AI相关立法。 之前众议院9月16日以417比3通过《Ratepayer Protection Act》，要求各州监管机构考虑让100兆瓦以上的大负荷用户承担其带来的全部发电和电网升级增量成本，但并不强制各州采用。
其实共和党对这方面也提出了这些要求。

但有一点，民主党应该也清楚在AI这场国家军备竞赛的意义和重要性，他们也很难说开倒车。更多的是纠偏、之前共和党的很多政策过激过度、控制步子迈得幅度、但并不是说就止步不前甚至落后，民主党也接受不了美国在AI上落后的代价。

3）再说加密
其实9月中清晰法案受阻、个人角度其实已经不指望未来两件有国会层面的加密立法，而是更看重sec和cftc在各自行政权限范围内给到了最大的政策范围。

之前这里https://t.co/xBS30IWyFe有聊过，构建行政版清晰框架。其实也够用了，未来两年SEC和CFTC主席都是川普提名的共和党人。

4）民主党横扫掌控两院能做到什么？
民主党夺取众院，已经能够限制相当一部分新增立法；
再拿下参院，新增的关键影响是人事确认、参院委员会议程，以及更强的监督与谈判能力。
能限制很大程度上限制共和党的新立法能力和进程，对很多政策和人发起国会调查和听证，但也限于此毕竟司法部未来来两年还在川普手里。

所以总的来说：
中期选举结束比结果可能更重要些，选举结束无论结果如何市场都能根据新的国会权力格局来做推演未来政策可能性、新的边界和程度会如何？而现在这些都悬在空中。

前天这里https://t.co/HK9K8cStzD也聊到，中午选举应该是一个关键的时间节点、之后很多方面会清晰明确起来。

本条由@bitget_zh赞助，「Bitget 买美股：秒级入场，丝滑交易

quoted_text:
22年中期选举之前，通胀爆表创四十年新高、美联储暴力加息、美股大盘暴跌30%多，美国国内对执政的拜登和民主党不满情绪非常高，“共和党红潮”席卷全美，当时中选前市场都认为共和党要横扫，但最后共和党只拿下众议院，执政党民主党不仅保住了参议院还增加了一个参议员名额扩大了的优势。

26年中期选举前，因为伊朗战争油价持续高位、通胀反弹，美国国内对川普的意见很大支持率新低，“民主党蓝潮”势头正盛，预测市场上都认为民主党要横扫拿下两院。

text:
Lots of noise around wet-lab demand from AI drug discovery. What's hype vs. real?

I know animal testing is a moral debate. Setting that aside for just one moment, here are some hard facts and numbers:

1/ Monkey prices could actually rise meaningfully if AIDD-driven demand materializes and more drug candidates progress from in-silico discovery to animal testing.

The U.S. is heavily dependent on imports, but its supply chain has been severely disrupted:

- China, once ~60% of US monkey imports, stopped exports in 2020.
- Cambodia, which subsequently became a major supplier, faced investigations and supply restrictions starting in 2022.
- US monkey imports fell ~43% in 2023 vs. 2022, before partially recovering.

Against this backdrop, what the startup below @JTLonsdale trying to build - domestic breeding capacity for 30K monkeys - looks strategically smart to me.

2/ But how this translates into $CRL's P&L is much less straightforward.

Historically, <20% of CRL's revenue has been exposed to monkey-related studies. For its core CRO business, monkeys are an input cost, not the product being sold. Higher prices can be passed through to customers, but that doesn't necessarily translate into higher margins.

Historically, CRL's business performance has shown no consistent correlation with monkey prices. Study volumes, supply availability, and sourcing economics matter much more.

--
1. The Global Lab Monkey Supply Chain

The U.S. uses approximately 60K–70K NHPs annually in research and testing, while China’s annual demand is estimated at roughly 40K–50K. But the two markets have very different supply structures.

US: Heavily import-dependent for commercial drug safety testing.

The U.S. typically imports around 20K–30K NHPs annually. Commercial toxicology studies primarily use cynomolgus macaques, sourced largely from overseas. Academic and NIH research relies more heavily on domestically bred rhesus macaques.

China: Predominantly domestic breeding.

Monkey prices are an interesting indicator of biotech activity. 

How big is Safer Human Medicine’s (the PLTR co-founder startup) proposed 30K-monkey breeding facility?
Potentially meaningful. If a mature facility could eventually supply 3K–6K animals annually, that would be equivalent to approximately 14%–27% of the U.S.’s 2025 cynomolgus imports.

--
$CRL: How the Business Actually Works; “Monkey impact”?

CRL is not simply a monkey distributor. It is primarily a contract research organization (CRO) selling drug discovery, toxicology, and safety assessment services.

How does CRL monetize monkeys?
“What we’re doing is we’re pricing a study, and the animal is part of that.”

Historically, NHP-related studies represented approximately 30% of DSA revenue, or roughly 18% of CRL’s consolidated revenue. At its September 2026 Investor Day, CRL disclosed that approximately 80% of NHPs used in its studies are now internally sourced, with the remaining 20% sourced externally.

What Does Rising Monkey Pricing Mean for CRL?
Monkey inflation has historically been positive for CRL’s reported revenue, but its impact on margins is much more nuanced.

From 2020 to 2023, CRL estimated that higher NHP pricing contributed more than $230M to cumulative DSA revenue growth. Management repeatedly explained that NHP cost increases were largely passed through to customers.

The more interesting structural opportunity may be margin improvement from vertical integration, rather than monkey price inflation itself.

++

text:
Today is the last regular working day for the @Balancer  team.

Some of the people on this team have been here since Balancer's earliest days. Others joined along the way. Together, they helped build and evolve the protocol over the years.

From the original weighted pools and liquidity bootstrapping to the v2 Vault, Boosted Pools, and v3, Balancer helped shape how liquidity works in DeFi. Behind all of that were years of research, engineering, integrations, operations, and work with partners that most people never saw.

The last year was especially difficult. The exploit hurt people who trusted Balancer, and the team went through the recovery, restructuring, and eventually the decision to wind down. Even after the end date was set, they continued doing the work needed to support users and partners.

This isn't the ending we worked for. But it doesn't take away what the team built and contributed to DeFi.

The winddown itself continues under BIP-928. For the remaining steps and withdrawal information, please follow the official Balancer updates.

To everyone who helped build Balancer over the years, thank you. 
I'm grateful I got to work with so many of you.

🚨UPDATE: Binance has set aside over $6.34 BILLION from company reserves to cover losses from the hack.  

$5 BILLION of that, roughly 80% of the TOTAL amount affected by the hack, is held in the same tokens involved, including USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH and BNB.  

Deposits and platform services are operating normally. Withdrawals remain paused for security review, with restoration expected in approximately 34 HOURS.  

Binance plans an initial Proof of Reserves snapshot in about 12 hours, with results expected by Monday, November 2.
author: coinbureau
quoted_text:
A very sad day for crypto.

Binance confirms nearly $6.3 BILLION was affected in what could be the industry’s largest security incident to date.

The industry came together quickly to freeze nearly $3 Billion in assets that left the world’s largest crypto exchange. 

The attacker exploited a vulnerability in EIP-7702 delegation which allows hot wallets to hand control to smart contract code.

The attack began around 4:30pm ET on Thursday, per on-chain data from Arkham.

Blockaid's preliminary assessment points to a "key misuse," similar to the Bybit exploit, where attackers compromise the signing infrastructure, though the firm says there isn’t enough information at this point to confirm.

Funds left across Ethereum, Bitcoin and Tron, and the attacker reportedly still holds over 18,000 $BTC.

Tether froze $1.567 BILLION in $USDT and Circle froze over $800 MILLION in $USDC.

Ripple, World Liberty, BitGo and Paxos also froze stolen assets, and Arbitrum's Security Council froze around $30.5 MILLION.

Aave froze its lending markets as a precaution, after the attacker borrowed $ETH against stolen $USDT.

Markets took a hit as the news spread:

Crypto cascaded to liquidate nearly $1.5 BILLION in the past 24 hours.

$BTC fell below $77,000, and $ETH below $2,200.

Altcoins reportedly sold by the attacker, including $ENA, $UNI, $LINK and $PEPE,  fell around -10% to -15%.

Binance has suspended deposits and withdrawals while it runs security checks and works with law enforcement.

The exchange reassures all users funds are safe and it "will cover ALL losses" owith a full post-mortem to follow once its investigation is complete.

text:
🔥 요즘 Rust가 미친 듯이 뜨고 있는 이유. 🔥

--> AI 개발 도구들까지 하나둘 Rust로 갈아타고 있기 때문입니다.

실제로 며칠전 깃허브에 따르면... 

Rust 프로젝트의 월간 기여자 수가 1년 만에 무려 162% 증가했다고 합니다.

현재 AI 개발 도구들을 살펴보면 요즘 실제 어떻게 돌아가고 있는지 보실 수 있습니다.

[OpenAI Codex CLI]
TypeScript로 개발했다가.. --> Rust로 재작성

[Anthropic의 Bun]
Claude Code의 실행 기반인데 Zig에서 --> Rust로 재작성

[Zed]
처음부터 Rust로 개발한 고성능 AI 코딩 에디터

--> 그런데 왜 하필 Rust일까요?

이유는 어쩔 수 없는 현실 때문에 그렇습니다..

Rust는 빠른 실행 속도, 적은 메모리 사용, 높은 메모리 안전성, 그리고 OS 수준의 보안 기능을 갖추고 있습니다.

AI 코딩 에이전트는 계속해서 파일을 읽고, 코드를 수정하고, 터미널 명령어를 실행하고, 결과를 검증합니다.

이런 작업을 수도 없이 반복하니... AI 모델만큼이나 그 밑에서 돌아가는 실행 환경도 굉장히 중요해진 것이 현재 요즘 상황입니다.

실제로 앤트로픽이 클로드코드를 활용해 Bun을 Rust로 옮긴 사례는 엄청 이슈가 됐었었죠..

2주도 안 돼 약 100만 줄의 코드를 생성했고.. 특정 2,000회 반복 빌드 테스트에서는 메모리 사용량이 무려

6,745MB → 609MB

까지 감소했다고 합니다.

(rust로 재작성하니 거의 10배 감소)

Rust는 원래 배우기도 어렵고, 기존 프로젝트를 Rust로 통째로 옮기는 것도 굉장히 부담스러운 일이었거든요?

그런데 이제는 Opus 5.5나 아스트라가 코드를 작성을 정말 잘해주고.... 컴파일러와 테스트가 오류를 잡아내는 과정을 반복하면서 이런 대규모 전환의 비용까지 줄어들고 있어서... 

요즘 Rust로 재작성하는 앱이나 프로그램들이 많아지고 있는 것 같습니다.

(메모리 가격도 비싸고 하니.. 뭐 최적화가 중요한 사용자 입장에서도 좋은 것이지요)
