text: The story behind videos that “pop.”
author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
Your iPhone is lying to you about how bright your screen is.

Every time a certain kind of video plays, your phone secretly darkens everything else on the screen so that one clip can glow. You probably just watched it happen with this guy biking past a cliffside cathedral.

Here's what's going on. When that clip slides into view, your phone cranks the real panel brightness way up, past where your brightness slider says it is. At the exact same moment, it quietly turns down every other pixel in the app by the same amount, so your tweets and profile pics look totally normal. The only thing left getting all that extra light is the video. That's why it looks like it's shining at you from somewhere behind the glass.

Apple calls this EDR. According to its own display engineers, iPhones can push highlights up to 8x brighter than the white on a normal post. Pretty much everything people upload tops out at that white and stays there. A video has to be specially graded in HDR to even ask for more, and almost nothing on your timeline ever does.

It gets more intense the darker your room is, too. Apple gives HDR the most room to work with when your brightness is turned way down, which is how most of us scroll in bed at night. So it hits hardest right when your eyes are least ready for it.

Instagram learned this the hard way. Once one post can glow, everything around it looks gray, and being the brightest thing on the screen is about the oldest trick in advertising. Instagram ended up adding a setting to turn off HDR video entirely, then later tied Reels brightness to your phone's light sensor to calm things down. A Chrome engineer even proposed a new piece of web code back in 2023 just so feeds could cap how bright HDR is allowed to get.

X stayed out of all this for a long time. As recently as late September, guides on posting HDR to social media still said X flattens every video to standard range. X did start letting HDR images glow around last December, which is where those flashbang profile pics came from. Now HDR video seems to be getting through too, and I couldn't find any announcement about it.

The guy who made this used Midjourney for the stills, animated them with MiniMax's H3 model, and did the final color grade in HDR in DaVinci Resolve. Lots of people have access to the same AI tools. The grade at the end is the part your phone actually reacts to, and you don't get it from typing a prompt.

I'd bet the first brands to grade their ads like this on X get a few good weeks of free attention before somebody builds a brake.

I pointed out in my speech that the Muslim Brotherhood’s antipathy for modernity is a dramatic departure from Islam’s historical affinity for science and learning. During the Muslim Golden Age, spanning the eighth through the fifteenth centuries, Muslim leaders dignified Islam’s wealth and power by promoting a brilliant flowering of innovation and scholarship in science, mathematics, philosophy, art, literature, astronomy, pharmacology, psychology, engineering, architecture, medicine, and navigation that continues to enrich the world today. Arab leaders fostered an intellectual ferment unmatched by any other in human history. A long line of enlightened caliphs assembled—and abundantly rewarded—an unparalleled galaxy of jurists, scientists, physicians, philosophers, musicians, artists, poets, and wits. Muslim rulers elevated the role of reason and tolerance, cultivating a milieu of religious and intellectual freedom—where Jews and Christians also flourished—and encouraged sages of various faiths and ethnicities to collaborate and freely exchange ideas.

For five centuries, Arabic was the world’s most learned and literary tongue and the lingua franca of science and scholarship. Most mosques had libraries (Córdoba hosted 600!). Muslim princes in the tenth century often had more books in their personal collections than existed in all of Europe. Baghdad had 100 bookstores in AD 891. England would have to wait another 420 years until 1309 to see paper for the first time.

Islam’s second Golden Age during the Ottoman Empire (1299–1922) birthed a cosmopolitan and pluralistic civilization centered in Constantinople that yielded additional bonanzas in poetry, music, art, and a tsunami of scientific innovation from coffee to water pumps, steam engines, gears, surgical scalpels and clamps, the first smallpox vaccine, and the cannons that allowed the Ottomans to dominate Europe to the gates of Vienna.

In 1928, six years after the Ottoman Empire collapsed, the Muslim Brotherhood began to spread its dark strain of violent fundamentalism from Egypt to Palestine and across the Muslim world. Islamism’s contagious proliferation ended the dialogue between Islam and the intellectual classes and demoted the role of reason in Islamic life. The Muslim Brotherhood’s principal philosopher, Sayyid Qutb, was contemptuous toward public education in science, math, and philosophy, believing that the only source of truth is the Koran. For Qutb, the purpose of education was not to celebrate life, or to nourish the intellect, but to indoctrinate children in the art of war, the glorification of death, and a blind obedience to an autocratic caliph.

Qutb railed against reason, which he considered the seed of apostasy. He sought to silence the humanities and viewed science as a sinister displacement of religion. He derided pluralism, rationalism, innovation, and tolerance. In doing so, he deprived Islam of its modern potential and its own greatest inheritance: the confidence to learn from the world, preserve its wisdom, and surpass it.

In his obituary for Muslim culture, The Closing of the Muslim Mind (2010), Robert R. Reilly recognizes that Qutb’s outlook dooms his followers to inertia. A religion that values obedience over initiative, that seeks to obviate independent reason, is a religion of violence. Where there is no framework for rational mediation, all disputes must be settled by force.

It didn’t worry Qutb that discouraging education in physics, mathematics, medicine, or engineering would atrophy intellectual and economic development in the Muslim world. Qutb explained that Muslim countries were so far behind the West in the sciences and technology that there was no hope to catch up. Muslims, he preached, should do what they do best—study the Koran and embrace martyrdom as the path for achieving global dominion: “The Muslim community today is neither capable of nor required to present before mankind great genius in material inventions, which would make the world bow its head before its supremacy.”

Qutb’s diatribe against Muslims competing in science and technology was nothing less than civilizational malpractice—especially given that he wrote it in 1964. Had Japan, Singapore, or South Korea accepted Qutb’s logic in 1964, they would have opted out of modernity. Instead, they chose to accept the challenge of competition. Their decision to engage has yielded stunning achievements that transformed their nations into economic and technological superpowers and enriched all of humanity.

The anti-intellectualism of Islamism—the rejection of evidence and the scientific method, the hostility toward objectivity, the suppression of contrary information, the deification of dogma, the embrace of pseudoscience, the contempt for reason as the path for discerning objective truth, and Islamism’s association of science with immorality—has helped close off the Islamic mind. The staggering metrics of intellectual and scholastic enfeeblement in Muslim nations attest to Islamism’s systematic squandering of human capital including the creative potential among the world’s two billion Muslims.

Korea issued 260,000 patents in 2024, while nine Arab countries, including Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, issued fewer than 10,000 in total, with 8,000 of these coming from a single nation—Saudi Arabia—which has made herculean efforts in recent years to de-Islamize its society. Japan, which represents about 1.5% of the world’s population and is practically devoid of natural resources, granted 306,855 patents in 2024 alone. There are 127 million Japanese, compared to 500 million Arabs.

According to Hillel Ofek’s 2011 analysis, there were a mere nine scientists, engineers, and technicians per thousand citizens in Islamic nations. The global average was forty-one. Among the 1,800 universities in Muslim nations, only 312 housed scholars who had published articles in journals.

Muslims represent 26% of the world’s population, and Muslim countries control half the world’s crude oil resources and 40% of natural gas resources. And yet the 53 Muslim countries combined publish only 5% of the world’s scientific literature. Hillel Ofek points to a 1989 study showing that in a single year, the United States published 10,481 frequently cited scientific papers, but during that same year, Arab countries published just four. A 2002 analysis of Arab science in Nature magazine identified only three scientific areas of excellence from Islamic countries: desalination, falconry, and camel reproduction. According to Nobel laureate physicist Steven Weinberg in 2011, “for forty years I have not seen a single paper by a physicist or astronomer working in a Muslim country that was worth reading.”

Contrast the Arabs’ dismal record of intellectual achievement in modern times with that of their closest cousins, the Jews, nearly all of whom live in democratic societies with laws that separate religion and politics.

Keep in mind that Jews, who number 15.8 million worldwide, represent a mere 0.2% of the world population. As of 2025, no Muslim has ever received the Nobel Prize in medicine or economics, and only four Muslim scientists—all living in Western democracies—have received the Nobel Prize in chemistry or physics. In contrast, some 200 Jews have received Nobel Prizes in science. About 26% of Nobel Prizes in math and science, 28% in medicine, 40% in economics, and 39% in chemistry have gone to Jews. Since 1901, some 22% of Nobel Prizes in all categories have gone to Jews.

Genocidal hatred against ALL Jews and Christians and other minorities is foundational to Islamism. Only in the West does Jew hatred pretend to require the alibi of Palestine or hide behind anti-Zionism. Muslim Brotherhood cosmology describes the universe as a cosmic, existential war between Islam and Jews that began with Muhammad and which only one side can survive. “Since Islam subdued them [in Medina],” Qutb warned, “they are unforgiving and fight furiously through conspiracies, intrigues, and also through proxies [the United States] who act in the darkness against all what Islam incorporates.” Islamist utopia will only emerge when every Jew is exterminated. Jews in Qutb’s theology are not just political adversaries, but perpetual and metaphysical evil. “The Jews,” he said, “are behind materialism, animal sexuality, the destruction of family, and the desolation of society.”

And Jewish genocide, for Islamism, is more than a theoretical aspiration. In 1948, the world’s 22 Arab nations were host to 750,000 Jews living in communities that predated Muhammad by 1,000 years. Today, there are virtually no Jews in those nations: Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Libya, Algeria, Yemen, Mauritania, Somalia, Sudan, Jordan, Gaza, or the PA-governed areas of the West Bank; in Nazi terminology, they are Judenrein: Jew-free. There are fewer than 1,000 Jews in Tunisia, down from 105,000. In 1948, Christian populations represented 20% of those nations; today they represent 4%. These are the real ongoing genocides of the Mideast.

Adolf Hitler’s Nazi regime bonded with early Islamists over their shared Jew hatred. The Nazis became the principal funder of the Muslim Brotherhood in the 1930s, and the Muslim Brotherhood operated propaganda, espionage, and sabotage operations for the Nazis during World War II. Joseph Goebbels and an army of Nazi and ex-Nazi propagandists built the Muslim Brotherhood’s powerful propaganda machine in the 1930s, ’40s, and ’50s. The massive influx of money from Iran and the Gulf States starting in the 1990s turned this operation into an amplifier of unmatched power that makes Goebbels look like a piker. A global propaganda barrage by this outfit has distracted Hamas’s Western dupes from Islamism’s authentic genocides by persuading them that Israel committed a genocide in Gaza, even though, according to the CIA Factbook, Gaza’s population has actually increased since October 7, 2023.

Islamism is genocidal against Christians and Jews, but among its most pitiful victims are the Arab societies that suffer the misfortune of living under its rule. Despite all their petroleum wealth, Muslim countries have slipped behind Asia and Latin America in virtually every metric of political freedom, technological progress, and social well-being. Islamism’s merger of politics and religion has robbed Islam of its intellectual vigor and doomed most Muslim populations to living in stifling tyrannies with little freedom to elucidate their thoughts and speech or fulfill their creative potential. Those countries are predictably stagnant, unable to evolve in the modern world. The dark shadow of fundamentalism over scholarship and progress has proven toxic to the Muslims’ transition to modernity. The very civilization that practiced tolerance and celebrated pluralism and dialogue, filled a thousand libraries with its books, gave the world observatories and universities, and stunning innovations in science, has become closed, aggrieved, and violent, and averse to reason, curiosity, freedom of inquiry, and scholarship.

All 22 Arab nations in the Mideast and North Africa are autocratic dictatorships. Almost all are apartheid states that legally restrict the rights of minorities. Gays in many of the nations are put to death. Under sharia law, women have little more rights than cattle. They live stunted lives behind veiled faces, enduring systematic servitude, legalized domestic violence, child marriage, chattel slavery, and public stoning for adultery, which is legal for their husbands. In September 2021, the Taliban made it illegal for girls to attend school after age 12. The Taliban’s Vice and Virtue law forbids women from speaking aloud in public.

If you want to understand the Muslim Brotherhood’s vision for society, look no further than Gaza. Hamas, which rules Gaza, is the Palestine branch of the Muslim Brotherhood. Palestinians have received over 4X per capita in international aid than Europeans received under the Marshall Plan. (See Clawson 2002.) Europe used its money to rebuild 17 nations. Palestinians couldn’t build themselves even one. Under Hamas’s iron fist, Gaza squandered its share on bombs, weapons, extravagant salaries for its billionaire kingpins, and a billion-dollar bunker and tunnel system built for its warriors—but off-limits to its citizens. Gaza remains a stunted and stagnant, impoverished society under tyrannical oppression, with no free speech or other basic freedoms. Hamas governs through force, including brutal crackdowns on discourse, public executions of dissenters and collaborators, tight controls on humanitarian aid distribution, and onerous taxes on almost every activity. No elections have occurred since Hamas took over in 2007. Instead of building a nation, Hamas has transformed Gaza into a death cult wallowing in victimhood, nursing aggrievements, addicted to violence, resentments, and yearning for a seventh-century miasma. Hamas nurses Palestinian infants from birth on genocidal hatred of ALL Jews—not just Zionists—and indoctrinates children in the savagery and unspeakable barbarism that the world witnessed on October 7. Hamas shows its contempt for the Palestinian people by deploying them as child soldiers and civilian shields, and placing rocket launchers and ammo dumps in schools and hospitals. Hamas’s greatest strengths are its propaganda operation and its willingness to impose unlimited pain on its own population to achieve its ideological goals.

Islamist governments like Iran, Hamas, and Hezbollah distract their populations from their misery by blaming the myriad social ills and the predictable government failures on scapegoats: Jews, Zionists, and America. They’ll have us believe that all their derelictions are the result of the evil Zionists, the “Little Satan” Israel, and the “Great Satan,” the U.S. And just as victimhood is paralyzing to personal growth, it deprives Islamist nations of national success by robbing its practitioners of agency. Islamism’s cult of victimhood and its coterminous abolition of self-criticism have stagnated global Islam and locked it in hatred, violence, brooding resentment, and isolationism. Referring to the Arab world, Fouad Ajami described this as “a political tradition of belligerent self-pity.”

Contrast Gaza’s failures with the successes of its closest neighbor, Israel, a tiny sliver of swamp and desert 1/600th the size of its Arab neighbors, that blossomed into an agricultural juggernaut and a global economic and technological superpower. Jews took one of the few places in the Mideast with no oil, gas, or other resources, and despite being surrounded by enemies, they nevertheless turned the barren landscape into a vibrant, pluralistic democracy where Jews and Arabs vote as they please; worship according to their convictions; serve beside each other in the judiciary, the army, and political leadership; and enjoy equal rights. Women and gays in Israel have all the rights of men, and Israel’s biggest annual celebration is the Pride parade in Tel Aviv. As the only democracy in the Mideast, Israel is a robust and heroic outpost for freedom and Western values.

And Israel is merely a nugget among the bounties bestowed by Jews on Western civilization. There is no ethnic or religious group that has contributed more than Jews to the welfare of humanity or to the advancement of liberal democracy. Jewish traditions of ethics and thinking have shaped Western civilization and global progress through foundational moral concepts, including our monotheistic Christian belief system with its roots in Judaism, milestone scientific breakthroughs, medical innovation, and innumerable cultural achievements in art, literature, education, health, and entertainment. Relative to their proportion of the population, the astonishing contributions by Jews have been breathtaking. An abbreviated list would include medical advances like the polio vaccine (Jonas Salk, Albert Sabin), chemotherapy and immunology (Paul Ehrlich), streptomycin and the age of antibiotics (Selman Waksman), penicillin (Ernest Chain), pacemakers (Paul Zoll), and blood typing (Karl Landsteiner).

In sciences, a short list of Jewish luminaries would include Albert Einstein (theory of relativity), Niels Bohr (quantum mechanics), and Paul Berg (first recombinant DNA molecule).

Jewish contributions to business and technology include Google (Sergey Brin), Meta (Mark Zuckerberg), Oracle (Larry Ellison), Salesforce (Marc Benioff), Intel (Andrew Grove), and Dell Technologies (Michael Dell).

Jews virtually created the American entertainment industry, including founding six of the eight major Hollywood studios responsible for 75% of the classic Golden Age movies. They also revolutionized laughter. A 1978 TIME magazine survey found that 80% of professional comedians were Jewish.

The major figures of twentieth-century Western thought—Jesus Christ, Sigmund Freud, Albert Einstein, and Karl Marx—were all Jewish. Twenty percent of philanthropic giving in the United States comes from Jews. Jews compose twenty-five percent of America’s most generous givers. They are overrepresented on lists of secular organizations that benefit human rights, social security, higher education, personal freedom, and constitutional rights. They represent 14% of doctors and 29% of psychiatrists. Their contributions to America’s global economic leadership include Salomon Brothers, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, Blackstone, Wells Fargo, and Vanguard. In a rational universe, wouldn’t non-Jews be expected to celebrate these contributions with gratitude?

Now, here are some things that Jews don’t do: suicide bombings, rape gangs, beheading people, killing gay people, aspiring to kill all non-Muslims, forcing young girls to wed older men, lynching women for wearing makeup or showing hair, female mutilation, religious dictatorship, Christian genocide, polygamy, rioting and burning down cities, applying the death penalty for leaving Islam, cooking babies in ovens, hijacking airliners (and driving them into buildings), bombing buses and crowded restaurants, disfiguring girls with acid for failing to wear the hijab, operating modern slave markets where hereditary Black slaves are bought and sold by Arabs, advocating global jihad, and committing 90% of the terrorist acts globally.

These are the gifts that Islamism has bestowed on the world, along with closed minds, poverty, starvation, ignorance, oppression, and violence. This comparison begs the question, “Why does the world hate Jews and embrace Islamists?

The answer, of course, is a sophisticated mass propaganda campaign that ignores evidence and inverts reality to make Israel a global villain.

Looking at Islamism’s track record, seven nations with substantial Muslim populations—Egypt, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Jordan, Syria, and Russia—have outlawed the Muslim Brotherhood, branding it as a terrorist organization. Kenya and Argentina have also banned the Brotherhood for fear of its impacts on their societies. The Brotherhood today sees its best opportunities for expansion as Western nations that are unequipped to deal with its tactics.

In 2004, the FBI discovered the U.S. Brotherhood’s archives in a Virginia basement, including a 1991 “Explanatory Memorandum” characterizing the Brotherhood’s work in America as “a kind of gradual Jihad in eliminating and destroying the Western civilization from within.” Muslim Brotherhood documents describe this process of gradual infiltration as “gradualism,” “entryism,” or “Da’awa.”

In a 1995 speech in Toledo, Ohio, the Brotherhood’s leading cleric, Yusuf al-Waradawi, told his audience: “We will conquer Europe, we will conquer America! Not through sword but through Da’awa.” As a board member and outreach chair of a Muslim Brotherhood front group, Abdul El-Sayed ran a high-school recruitment program entitled “How to do effective Da’awa.”

The Muslim Brotherhood’s explicit written strategy for taking over Western nations is to broaden its appeal through a “red–green alliance” by adopting Leftist rhetoric and allying itself with liberals, socialists, and communists. This was the strategy first initiated by Yasser Arafat in the 1960s and then implemented by Muslim Brotherhood acolyte Ayatollah Khomeini during his 1979 Iranian Revolution, and later by Muslim Brother Mohammed Morsi during his 2011 color revolution in Egypt. After they gained power, the Leftists, in each case, learned that they were not actually Islamism’s partners, but only its useful idiots. Khomeini hunted down, jailed, and murdered his former Leftist and communist allies. Morsi sidelined his. A 2012 Arabic-language statement bearing Abdul Al-Sayed’s name backed Morsi’s presidency and urged him to “purge” the media and police.

Anyone wondering what America’s future looks like if the Muslim Brotherhood gets its way has only to look at France, where Islamist mobs of the red–green alliance, following the Muslim Brotherhood playbook, chant communist phrases, wave Palestinian flags, and vent their destructive hostility toward the West by destroying the iconic monuments of our shared civilizations.

Abdul El-Sayed mocks his critics as Islamophobic or anti-Arab racists when they inquire about his continued loyalties to the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed said nothing about the Brotherhood itself, its ideology, or the Muslim Brotherhood front organizations he works with. A disavowal that names nothing and condemns nothing is a disavowal in name only.

Why can’t El-Sayed give us a full-throated and detailed condemnation of this terror group, and disavow also its poisonous ideology without ambiguity? text:
Bill Ackman reveals Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft are now about a third of his portfolio, each bought when the stock fell, and says it’s interesting when a company announces "enormous demand" and its stock goes down

“I would say every business today is either AI related or should be or is going to be disrupted by AI. So I think that’s the assessment that you have to do."

"You know, we purchased Amazon after Trump announced liberation tariffs. We acquired Meta after they disappointed people by committing a large amount of money to capex. And the same with Microsoft."

"You know, it’s sort of an interesting environment when you have a company come out publicly and say, ‘We have enormous demand for our service. Therefore, we have to invest well in excess of what we expected in capex just to try to meet the demand from our product.’ And then stock price goes down."

"And that’s what led to an investment in Microsoft. But it’s probably, those names represent about a third of our portfolio today.”
author: firesidealpha
quoted_text:
Bill Ackman says Elon Musk might have to borrow a trillion dollars to open gigawatts of data centers, keeping rates persistently high, and that neoclouds are like levered real estate developers sensitive to the cost of capital

“So, I think it is sustainable because, you know, intelligence is again an enormously valuable asset. And I think the demand therefore for the compute that enables intelligence, I think, is going to be sustained."

"And, you know, the companies that are, you know, the hyperscalers that are building out a lot of this infrastructure have the financial resources, the creditworthiness in order to access the capital."

"I worry more about the pure play neocloud companies that are a bit like highly levered real estate developers playing a theme. I think they’re much more at risk. They’re much more sensitive to the cost of capital."

"But you have, I mean, SpaceX, Elon on the earnings call gave some projections for how many gigawatts of data centers he was going to open. If he meets his objective, he might have to borrow a trillion dollars of capital."

"So, you have companies competing at sovereign levels for debt. And the result is, you know, this massive, you know, more and more supply of debt. So, I don’t see a world in which, you know, there’s a dramatic, you know, there’s a lot of demand for capital and a finite supply. So, I think that makes rates persistently high.”

text:
Ex-Tower Research HFT trader Annanay Kapila (@annanay) on adverse selection, the hidden cost of market making:

"The problem with market making is there is a concept called adverse selection."

"It basically says you're way more likely to trade when your estimate of the fair value is wrong."

"Those people are more likely to trade against you than the so-called random trader, or just an investor who wants to buy and sell in the market, who is kind of equally likely to trade at all times."

"If I think the fair price is $100.5 and it's actually $99.9, there's still no free money in this market. But as soon as I put a bid over here, I am on average losing $0.10 for every share that I do."

"I'm way more likely to trade when I have that bid at $100, just because arbitrageurs are generally smart, and they'll trade very quickly if they think your pricing is wrong."
author: ethanrkho
quoted_text:
"Greed makes markets."

Annanay Kapila (@annanay) spent years as an HFT quant at Flow Traders and Tower Research before founding QFEX (@QFEX), a perpetual futures exchange for equities, commodities & FX. Cambridge Maths.

At his last job, the desk traded $10B+ of volume a day, run almost entirely by algorithms.

In this lecture, he builds market making from first principles:

- The map of systematic trading: prop money vs. other people's money, HFT vs. mid-frequency, and why every strategy lives in one quadrant
- Why prop firms can return 50-100% a year while hedge funds can't: HFT never leaves you holding a big position
- The order book from scratch: bids, offers, limit orders, and why the first order on a price level gets the trade
- No free lunch: how arbitrageurs force every order book to reveal a fair price without anyone trying to
- The entire strategy in one line: bid below fair value, offer above it, collect the difference forever
- Market making is "time-spreading risk," warehousing positions between a seller who shows up now and a buyer who shows up later
- Adverse selection: you're most likely to get filled precisely when your price is most wrong
- Why market makers are completely self-serving, and why that's exactly what makes markets work
- The competitive race that compresses spreads: greed among market makers means lower costs for everyone else
- Thick books vs. thin books, and the vicious loop that keeps illiquid markets illiquid

I Lost $30K on Polymarket to a Manipulated Oil Spike Nobody Else Saw

I bet about $30,000 on @Polymarket that oil (WTI) would not hit $105.

It was a simple trade. All week, oil kept failing just under $105. On Friday it dropped to around $103 heading into the close. So I bet "No".

Then this happened.

At 5:00 PM ET the main US oil market (NYMEX) closed for the weekend. Five minutes later, the price feed Polymarket uses (@PythNetwork) suddenly showed oil at $105.11.

Over the next 17 minutes it "hit" $105 six times, each time snapping back to $103 within a minute. By 5:30 PM it showed $102.90, lower than before.

But oil never actually went there.

On ICE, the real exchange named in the rules, oil traded at $102.50
On Hyperliquid, a huge oil market, the highest price was $102.91.

Only Polymarket's price feed moved. Real oil didn't.

Why it smells like manipulation:

It started right after the main market closed, when it's cheapest to push a price.
The exact same fake high, $105.307, showed up three times.
It was just enough to cross $105 and wipe out every "No" bet.

Polymarket doesn't protect you from this

Polymarket's rules say the feed's price counts "exactly as published". There's nothing about manipulation or fake prices. So a few minutes of bad data can decide markets worth tens of thousands of dollars.

Compare that with @Kalshi: it's regulated and has strict rules against insider trading and market manipulation. On Polymarket, nothing in these market rules protects users from a fake price.

@Polymarket @PythNetwork @UMAprotocol: please review the 5:05–5:22 PM ET prices before these markets resolve. Oil never hit $105.

Charts: Pyth's spikes vs Hyperliquid's flat line over the same minutes.

Either one of those numbers is wrong, or these races are tied together much tighter than they look

Democrats have 47 seats counting two independents, and need 4 net, because Vance breaks a 50-50 tie
The state markets have them favored in five Republican seats:

＞ North Carolina 98¢
＞ Ohio 73.5¢
＞ Alaska 71.5¢
＞ Texas 70.5¢
＞ Maine 69¢

Kansas is a coin flip at 51.5¢, Iowa sits at 44.5¢

Run every race on its own at today's prices
Democrats net 4 or more in 85% of outcomes, and about 5 on average

The math only gets down to 71.5¢ if the races move very closely together
That is a real risk, since a national polling miss can hit every state at once

For 71.5¢ to be fair, Ohio, Alaska, Texas and Maine have to swing mostly as a pack on the same night

That is a lot to assume about four very different states
If they move even a bit less together, Senate control is cheap at 71.5¢ or the state markets are too rich

text:
Lightberry wants to charge $20,000 a year for software running on a $39,990 humanoid robot. That's $40,000 for the robot and another $40,000 in software fees over the following two years.

Breakdown #002: @lightberry

The San Francisco startup, founded by @aliattar and @sadkoeni, is betting that businesses will pay a substantial recurring fee to make humanoid robots better at interacting with people.

Their first robot, Lumi, is a 1.3-meter humanoid built on Unitree's G1 platform.

Lightberry replaces the onboard computer, adds its own cameras and microphones, and runs its software on NVIDIA's Jetson Thor.

The robot handles perception and movement locally, while cloud-based AI models take care of conversations and planning.

Lightberry doesn't train its own foundation models. Its software focuses on how robots behave around people.

That includes deciding when to speak, when to listen, and when to remain silent.

Think about a robot working at a hotel reception, guiding visitors through an exhibition, or interacting with customers at a trade show.

It needs to understand who's talking to it, handle interruptions, and respond without making every conversation painfully awkward.

Lightberry has already demonstrated its software on several humanoid platforms, including Unitree, Fourier and Booster.

The company also says it generates revenue from enterprise customers running its software on third-party hardware.

With Lumi, Lightberry is now selling the complete product.

The first 100 Founder Edition units are priced at $39,990, including one year of software and support. The reported annual software fee after that is $20,000.

On October 30, Lightberry also announced that Lumi had received a conditional exemption from US restrictions on foreign-produced advanced robots.

According to the company, the approval requires shifting manufacturing to the US.

That's a significant development for a robot currently based on Chinese hardware.

But the economics are what I'm watching.
ㅤ
At $20,000 per year, a company operating ten Lumi robots would spend $200,000 annually on software alone.

That's before maintenance, cloud usage, and the people needed to operate them.

And Unitree is developing its own software ecosystem.

Lightberry will have to demonstrate that its interaction software delivers enough additional value to justify those recurring fees.

There are no publicly confirmed Lumi deliveries yet, and the company hasn't disclosed how many enterprise customers are paying for its software.

I'd like to see what happens after the first year, when customers have to decide whether Lumi is worth another $20,000.

Especially in markets like hospitality and events, where customers have plenty of alternatives for that money.

随着AI数据中心对内存的需求不断增加，涨价已经传导到了我们日常使用的电脑内存。

根据 DRAMeXchange 的数据，常用于电脑内存的DDR4 8Gb芯片，10月份合约均价从9月份的26美元涨到27.5美元，环比上涨5.77%，再次创下该型号有记录以来的新高。

AI服务器使用的内存和我们电脑里的内存条并不相同，但它们都需要存储芯片厂商的产能。现在三星、SK海力士等厂商将更多资源转向服务器内存，普通PC内存的供应受到挤压，电脑厂商和内存条厂商采购芯片的成本也跟着上升。

PC Gamer追踪的一款32GB DDR5-6000内存套装，在2024年和2025年的大部分时间里，美国亚马逊售价大约是80至100美元，到2026年10月报道时已经涨到553美元。

说人话就是，现在 AI 的建设已经开始影响到正常消费者的使用，比如我们现在买显卡或者是买内存的价格就提升了很多，而提升的原因就是因为 AI 需要大量的内存挤占了民用生产的空间。

其实我们都在为 AI 买单，不论是我们否愿意。

quoted_text:
海力士和三星财报都创新高，但股价为什么还在跌？

最近很久没有聊海力士和半导体了，尤其是在 Token 2049 以后忙的没有时间做空 ADR 以后就几乎没有看半导体了，最近正好有小伙伴来，而且一直在投资海力士，就赶紧捡起来重新看看。

也巧了最近两天海力士和三星也是公布 2026年 第三季度的财报，从整体的数据来看 AI 数据中心对存储芯片的需求仍然很强，两家公司的收入和利润都创下了季度新高。尤其是海力士的财报更好。

海力士三季度营收达到 104.62 万亿韩元，营业利润达到 83.33 万亿韩元，比市场预期的 76.96 万亿韩元高出约 8.3%。三星电子的营收达到 195.3 万亿韩元，营业利润达到 107.4 万亿韩元，其中半导体部门贡献了 106.5 万亿韩元的营业利润。

从业务来看，这一轮增长不只是 AI 芯片需要的 HBM 在推动。海力士三季度开始大规模出货 HBM4，服务器 DDR5 出货量比上季度增长超过 40%，企业级 SSD 的销售也在扩大。三星同样增加了 HBM4 和服务器 SSD 的销售，公司表示存储业务的收入和利润都创下了季度新高。

海力士三季度 DRAM 的平均售价环比上涨了 20% 多，NAND 平均售价也上涨了 20% 多。

海力士预计受 AI 数据中心建设和新工厂投产周期影响，存储市场供不应求的情况可能持续到 2030 年。公司已经与 14 家主要客户签订长期协议，覆盖 2027 年和 2028 年超过一半的产能。三星也认为，2027 年 AI 相关存储需求的增长将超过行业供给增长。

到这里我要吐槽一下，本来还想等 2027年 看看内存的价格是不是能回落一些，但从目前的情况来看有点难了。现在买内存反而成了理财产品。

从股票价格走势来看，海力士的财报超过预期，10月28 日公布财报当天股价上涨了 10.89%，第二天也继续上涨。三星 10月29日 公布详细财报后股价下跌了 4.13%，主要原因是半导体部门的营业利润略低于分析师预期。

到了今天，两家股价都出现下跌。前一天 Alphabet（Google） 的营收低于市场预期，AI 投资增加也让现金流受到关注，股价下跌了 12.64%。

市场担心的是科技公司持续投入这么多钱建设 AI 数据中心，未来能不能产生足够的回报。如果客户为了控制支出而放慢扩建，海力士和三星未来的存储订单也可能受到影响。也就是我经常说的资本开支太高了。

所以总的来说，AI 对 HBM、服务器内存和 SSD 的需求仍然很强，海力士和三星两家公司的存储业务也确实在赚钱。但投资者对于 AI 资本开支的担心已经蔓延到了下游的产业链，可以说只要这把悬挂在 AI 头上的达摩克里斯之剑没有被挪走市场总会担心三星和海力士的业绩就可能会变成井中月。

THE BINANCE CRISIS JUST EXPOSED ETHEREUM'S BIGGEST ADVANTAGE

Billions moved from Binance hot wallets. Stablecoin issuers raced to freeze the suspected stolen funds.

But something extraordinary happened onchain.

🔹 $823M in USDC frozen by Circle
🔹 $1.567B in USDT frozen by Tether
🔹 444,766 ETH worth $1.01B in Arkham tracked wallets

Over $2.39 BILLION in stablecoins frozen, while native ETH remained beyond any issuer's ability to blacklist.

And here's the part that deserves far more attention.

Both types of assets can operate on Ethereum.

Wall Street can issue regulated stablecoins and tokenized securities with compliance controls, while native ETH remains permissionless, without a central issuer or freeze switch.

That's a powerful combination for the future of finance.

Institutions get the safeguards they require. The network preserves an open financial system that no single company controls.

The suspected Binance attack exposed the risks of that freedom, too.

But it also revealed something fundamental about Ethereum's architecture: regulated finance and permissionless money can coexist on the same infrastructure.

And that could become enormously important as trillions in financial assets move onchain.

In the case of Lighter:

1. All data is verifiable - you don't have to trust the operator.  Withdraw your funds via escape hatch if Lighter stops operating. There are CLOBs for other products like spot/options where realtime settlement makes a difference, and it is synergistic via portfolio margin

2. Lighter can trivially offer privacy to traders by encrypting data (with the trader's public key) before it's posted to Ethereum. This does not affect the escape hatch. Position level privacy can be mandatory, opt-in, or opt-out. Trades, volume and open interest can remain public, verifiable info while individual trader positions remain hidden

3. No priority fees on Lighter. 

4. Combining onshore/offshore orderbooks is technically possible but that's up to the regulators.

5. Lighter matching engine is centralized and highly performant. There is no tradeoff between speed and security. If there is inefficiency, it is the cost of generating and publishing proofs of correct execution, which is low and continuing to drop quickly.

text:
In 2018, Elon Musk tweeted that he would fund the replacement of lead contaminated water pipes in Flint, Michigan for any home that still had unsafe water. He said to just tell him which houses needed help and he would fix them. The response from Flint's officials was near silence.

The offer was genuine. Elon followed up. He donated $480,000 to install UV filtration systems in Flint schools. He offered to continue funding until every household had clean water. Local officials thanked him publicly and then largely stopped responding. The project stalled not because of money but because of bureaucracy, local politics, and the same institutional inertia that had allowed the crisis to happen in the first place.

The detail that makes this story devastating is not the donation. It is the disconnect between the speed at which Elon operates and the speed at which a municipal government can accept help. He offered. He funded. He followed up. The system he was trying to help could not process the help at the speed it was offered. The man who can build a factory in 6 months could not get a city to accept pipe replacements because the approval process, the contractor bids, the environmental reviews, and the political negotiations moved at a pace that made SpaceX look like light speed by comparison.

He has described the Flint experience as one of the most frustrating of his career. Not because the problem was hard. Because the problem was easy and the system designed to solve easy problems was broken. The water needed clean pipes. The pipes needed money. The money was offered. And the space between offered and installed was filled with a bureaucracy that moved at the speed of government while children drank contaminated water.

The man who solves engineering problems for a living encountered a problem that was not engineering. It was institutional. The pipes were simple. The politics were not. The money was present. The will was present. The system that was supposed to connect money and will to pipes could not function at the speed the crisis demanded.

He fixed the schools. The broader offer faded. The city eventually replaced most of its pipes through federal and state funding years later. The man who offered to fix it in months watched it take years. The frustration of the man who moves fast encountering a world that doesn't is the frustration that defines his relationship with every institution he touches. The rockets are faster because they don't require a city council vote.

text:
A very sad day for crypto.

Binance confirms nearly $6.3 BILLION was affected in what could be the industry’s largest security incident to date.

The industry came together quickly to freeze nearly $3 Billion in assets that left the world’s largest crypto exchange. 

The attacker exploited a vulnerability in EIP-7702 delegation which allows hot wallets to hand control to smart contract code.

The attack began around 4:30pm ET on Thursday, per on-chain data from Arkham.

Blockaid's preliminary assessment points to a "key misuse," similar to the Bybit exploit, where attackers compromise the signing infrastructure, though the firm says there isn’t enough information at this point to confirm.

Funds left across Ethereum, Bitcoin and Tron, and the attacker reportedly still holds over 18,000 $BTC.

Tether froze $1.567 BILLION in $USDT and Circle froze over $800 MILLION in $USDC.

Ripple, World Liberty, BitGo and Paxos also froze stolen assets, and Arbitrum's Security Council froze around $30.5 MILLION.

Aave froze its lending markets as a precaution, after the attacker borrowed $ETH against stolen $USDT.

Markets took a hit as the news spread:

Crypto cascaded to liquidate nearly $1.5 BILLION in the past 24 hours.

$BTC fell below $77,000, and $ETH below $2,200.

Altcoins reportedly sold by the attacker, including $ENA, $UNI, $LINK and $PEPE,  fell around -10% to -15%.

Binance has suspended deposits and withdrawals while it runs security checks and works with law enforcement.

The exchange reassures all users funds are safe and it "will cover ALL losses" owith a full post-mortem to follow once its investigation is complete.

text: UP 面临的最大考验，不是它的机制设计有多聪明，而是 TapeUP 能否将这些机制真正转化为一个持续运转的经济体系。👍
author: iruletrenches
quoted_text:
关于 $UP – TapeUP 的个人观点：值得关注的核心在哪里？

在了解 UP 的经济机制之后，我认为 TapeUP 正在尝试构建一种具有不少亮点的经济模型。不过，除了这些积极的设计之外，也有一些问题仍需要时间来验证。

以下是我的几点个人看法：

1. PoB——一种不同于传统代币发行的思路

将购买预算分为即时买入部分和 25 天线性释放部分。
这种方式可以延长买入过程，而不是将全部买入需求集中在初始阶段。
项目因此能够获得更多时间来开发产品、积累用户和建设社区。
但需要明确的是，按照时间表释放买入资金，并不意味着市场产生了新的真实需求。这两者不能混为一谈。

2. Builder Code——让协作成为经济机制的一部分

用户可以使用彼此的 Builder Code，加速 UP 的购买过程。
双方分别使用自己的待释放资金，实现等额加速。
加速行为会被记录为权重，并参与 UP 建设奖励池的分配。
积极的一面是，这套机制能够鼓励参与者之间建立联系与协作。
但值得观察的是，社区究竟是在真正建设产品，还是主要为了优化奖励而参与。

3. UP 与 BEM 的关系——形成明确的角色分工

BEM 作为交易结算资产和手续费收取资产。
UP 作为交易标的和建设奖励资产。
交易手续费将分配给质押、UP 回购以及其他相关用途。
如果交易活动持续增长，这两种代币有机会形成更加紧密的经济联系。
但前提仍然是：必须存在真实的交易需求和实际收入。

4. UP 回购机制——需要关注真实数据

根据设计，协议将部分交易手续费预算用于回购 UP。
这可能为 UP 带来来自协议活动的额外买入需求。
但计划用于回购的预算，不等于已经实际完成的回购数量。
真正值得关注的是回购交易记录、实际回购数量，以及这些数据能否通过链上记录验证。

5. 2100 万枚总供应量——稀缺性不等于价值

UP 的总供应量设定为 2100 万枚。
根据资料，初始供应量的 100% 进入交易流动性。
整体供应结构相对清晰。
但总量较低并不意味着代币一定具有较高价值。
长期价值仍取决于市场需求、实际使用场景以及代币流动性。

6. 1000 万美元市值门槛——一个值得关注的里程碑

当 UP 市值达到这一门槛时，协议计划开放全链账本 UP 与 BNB Chain 上 BEP20 UP 之间的双向兑换。
根据设计，这一转换不会增加 UP 的 2100 万枚总供应量。
这将是扩大资产可访问性的重要一步。
不过，实际执行方式、跨链稳定性以及开放后的流动性，仍需要进一步观察。

7. 我最关注的事情：TapeUP 能否创造真实价值？

在我看来，这才是决定 UP 未来表现的关键：

有多少用户真正使用 TapeUP 的产品？
有多少 Builder 正在创造新的应用和服务？
协议收入是否来自真实需求，并保持持续增长？
交易手续费和回购活动是否公开透明、可以通过链上数据验证？
当激励奖励减少时，用户是否仍然愿意持有和使用 UP？

结语

我认为，UP 的经济设计值得关注，尤其是 PoB、Builder Code 与手续费分配机制之间的组合。

但我们也需要认识到：一个拥有良好 Tokenomics 设计的系统，并不一定就能发展成为成功的生态。

PoB 可以制定买入释放计划，但无法自动创造市场需求。
Builder Code 可以激励协作，但无法保证产生高质量产品。
回购机制可以增加一种潜在需求，但其效果取决于实际协议收入。
有限的代币供应可以形成稀缺性，但不能单独决定代币价值。

在我看来，UP 面临的最大考验，不是它的机制设计有多聪明，而是 TapeUP 能否将这些机制真正转化为一个持续运转的经济体系。

这才是值得整个社区持续关注和验证的事情。

text:
I've been working for some time on a game https://t.co/eg7aTFJNXL that would include mechanics that I remembered and loved from all Civilization series games, from 1 to 7. Each of them had something I liked and something I didn't. I never kinda seemed to get the set of features I wanted. So a few weeks ago I sat down with claude code and codex and made a pretty fun game I actually liked.
In short the game can be summarized as Civilization with borders and a deep internal struggle mechanic: civil wars, coups, revolutions. You can think about it as a mix of Civilization and Crusader Kings, but not exactly because the game never descends down to the level of individuals: because of the timeframes represented this wouldn't make any sense. The actors on the political scene are families, or gentes if you will: they become rulers, governors, units are recruited from the members of the families. This expands on ethnicity mechanic from Civilization 3 where each population unit, the so called citizen (although in reality it represents some unspecified large group of people which grows larger as the game progresses, from 10 000 to a few million) had a distinct ethnicity that had some minor gameplay effect, mostly reduced contentment of the population.

In Atlas of Ages, however, in addition to ethnicity each citizen has family. Each family has 4 traits affecting gameplay: dwelling (e.g. Plains Dwellers), profession (e.g. Woodcutters), character (power-hungry, fearful, ambitious) and feat (such as Great Builders). Each trait gives various gameplay bonuses and/or penalties. Grassland dwellers for example, earn one additional production when they are assigned to a grassland, and unit of a family with the Warriors trait get higher strength in battle. Families break up over time, losing old traits and gaining new ones, they have their own opinion about the ruling family and have their preferred type of government, they can stage coups and rebellions to e.g. change Monarchy to Republic, or to just take power in a Monarchy for themselves following the breakup of a ruling family (a simulated succession crisis). One family can rule for a long time, but if they rule too long other families start getting unhappy just because of that and eventually they'll stage a rebellion. Although it IS possible to avoid rebellions, there are ways to calm rival families down, it's not always practical. For example, you might have an entrenched family that has been ruling for half a game that already results in a high grievance, in addition to that it might have gained a negative character trait, such as corrupt which reduces gold income of the whole country plus increases grievance of other families even more. Once civil war starts you can pick either the Government or the rebels. The best idea is to always pick the winning side, although sometimes is hard to say which one will win. Take into account traits of the new family and how hard it would be to win to make your decision. Although you as a player generally should be able to outsmart the automated opponent, if the difference in strength is too large, there's nothing you can do
Types of government is another big feature of the game. What I really hated in Civilization is that types of government basically don't mean much. They give you some economic bonuses but that's about it. Democracy plays just the same as Despotism. That's the problem I wanted to address, and, as far as I know, I am the first to try it, of all developers of Civilization-like games.

Despotism plays exactly like normal Civilization game. Your control everything like a despot. You have one ruling family which is also the founding family in the beginning. You select what to build in cities, where to move units, everything you control personally.

Once you research Code of Laws you can switch to Monarchy or Republic. And both play different from each other.

Lighter is building toward becoming regulated financial infrastructure with its own DCM + DCO structure in the US.

The US futures market alone represents roughly $31T in annual notional volume.

And we already have a glimpse of what distribution can do.

Robinhood alone generated $17.85B in volume in Q3.

I think the market is still trying to figure out what $LIT is.

The bigger question is what Lighter can become.

text:
This is one of the better litmus tests for whether you’re pushing your use of AI enough or not. 

Up until maybe six months ago probably the best you could do with AI was pull off something you already would produce, but just doing it a little faster. But now we’re entering a point where the output of working with AI can and should dramatically exceed what you would been able to do before, in a fraction of the time.

The product prototype should not only be fully functional and interactive, but it should probably have meaningfully better features than it would have had before. The engineering architecture should be able to deliver performance gains that you wouldn’t have been able to go after otherwise. 

The research for a project should consume every single fact on the subject across every dimension of analysis possible. The business process you implement with AI should operate entirely differently and learn from all its past failures in a way no human could. 

We’re unquestionably entering a period where AI will be smarter than us on most axes. Perhaps not on every dimension that matters (intelligence is still very jagged), but at least on enough dimensions that when we combine it with what we’re good at, you get qualitatively different outcomes.

So the simple test is: if you could have done what you’re doing before AI, you’re likely not pushing it enough.

text:
New post on Eth Research!

PropAMM fills on Ethereum mainnet and PropAMM support for TEMBRI (toolbox): same-block quotes, a small spread, and flow taken from lagging AMMs

By:
- DanGuo

🔗 https://t.co/tXrWkXQ1Jv

Highlights:
- Across 30 days the author decoded 92,627 fills on nine Ethereum PropAMM venues (69,827 WETH/stablecoin fills) and benchmarked execution quality using Binance 1-second trades as the external reference price.
- Several venues enforce quote freshness at the smart-contract level: for El Zorro, bopAMM, and Kipseli, the registry is read with minTimestamp=maxTimestamp=block.timestamp, so fills can only execute against maker updates from the same block (Tempest allows a small timestamp window).
- Execution costs are small and stable: takers lose about 0.45 bp at the fill on every day, and average markouts do not improve over the next 5 minutes for any taker class—showing no evidence of adverse selection against takers.
- After short-term CEX moves (>0.5 bp in the prior 12 seconds), 78.5% of fills trade against the move; PropAMM quotes adjust in the same block while Uniswap lags, so arbitrageurs/routers commonly use PropAMMs as the “fresh” leg versus “stale” AMMs.
- Most PropAMM fills are privately submitted (only 2.9% seen in a public mempool archive on a measured day), no PropAMM leg was sandwiched over 30 days, and sandwiching risk mainly appears on the AMM legs of public, routed transactions rather than on PropAMM pools themselves.

ELI5:
Some crypto trading pools on Ethereum (PropAMMs) let one market-maker set the price by posting an on-chain “quote” each block. When someone trades, the trade uses that posted quote. This study shows those quotes are forced to be very fresh (often from the same block), traders consistently pay a tiny fee-like spread (~0.45 basis points), and many trades are actually part of arbitrage where bots use the PropAMM as the up-to-date price and trade against slower pools like Uniswap that haven’t caught up yet.

text:
If you’re planning to buy Air Fryer, here’s the only checklist that actually matters:

1. Capacity:
2–3L = bachelor/couple
4–6L = family
8L+ = serious meal prep

2. Wattage:

1600–1800W cooks faster and more evenly.
Anything lower struggles with crisping.

3. Basket Quality
Go for ceramic or stainless steel if possible.

If you’re buying non stick, make sure it’s detachable, thick and easy to clean.

4. Controls:

Digital > manual. Presets help but not mandatory.

5. Shape:

Oven-style if you bake, roast, or cook in batches.
Bucket-style if you want compact size and quick use.

6. Noise & Heat:
Cheaper models get loud + hot on the outside.

I’ve personally used two air fryers till now: Agaro and Philips.

Both worked well, but Philips had better consistency and build quality over time.

The instinct when a tariff or energy price shock lands is to wait for clarity. Clarity costs time, and time is what countermeasures require.

A finance director sees a tariff announcement ripple across news and economic sources. InekIA runs a shock simulation, tracing how the move reaches costs, revenue and margin across scenarios built from the team's own figures and sourced facts.

The output is not a forecast. It is a ranked set of countermeasures on pricing, hedging and sourcing, evaluated before the budget review, while there is still room to act rather than react.

text:
In the case of Lighter:

1. All data is verifiable - you don't have to trust the operator.  Withdraw your funds via escape hatch if Lighter stops operating. There are CLOBs for other products like spot/options where realtime settlement makes a difference, and it is synergistic via portfolio margin

2. Lighter can trivially offer privacy to traders by encrypting data (with the trader's public key) before it's posted to Ethereum. This does not affect the escape hatch. Position level privacy can be mandatory, opt-in, or opt-out. Trades, volume and open interest can remain public, verifiable info while individual trader positions remain hidden

3. No priority fees on Lighter. 

4. Combining onshore/offshore orderbooks is technically possible but that's up to the regulators.

5. Lighter matching engine is centralized and highly performant. There is no tradeoff between speed and security. If there is inefficiency, it is the cost of generating and publishing proofs of correct execution, which is low and continuing to drop quickly.

Further to my post about @NYSE working to bring @HyperliquidX onshore, major credit to @ChairmanSelig and the Trump administration for making all of this experimentation possible. 

There’s only one way of finding out if something is useful to the marketplace and I’m excited for us to find out. I do have some questions:

1. What is the benefit of trading perps on-chain on a regulated exchange? Isn’t the main benefit of trading on-chain to operate in a trustless (aka non-kyc’d) environment in order to minimize friction, and/or to be able to enter into atomic transactions in order to receive what you are buying in realtime? Since a perp is not an asset, that obviously isn’t helpful. 

2. @standuquesne - are you aware that if you trade on Hyperliquid, the world will be able to track your positions and trades in real time? Do you see that as a benefit?

3. Hyperliquid has priority fees - a mechanism that enables market participants to pay to see information first, or even prioritize orders in front of the queue. Is this consistent with CFTC core principles?

4. Will it be possible to combine the liquidity of the offshore order-book with the onshore order-book?

5. If not, wouldn’t it be better to list perps in a traditional (centralized) order-book on a regulated exchange and not have the inefficiencies that on-chain matching introduces?

BREAKING: Inside Starcloud, the $2.3B Startup Putting Data Centers in Space

FACTORY TOUR - Redmond, WA

Primes quoted them $75M-$100M to build their first data center in space. They did it for $2.5M.

In just 21 months, Starcloud is one of the fastest companies to go from founding to orbit.

With $450M in total funding from Manhattan West, Nvidia, Cisco, Benchmark & EQT, the team walks me through their mission for AI in space.

I toured the new HQ w/ CEO @PhilipJohnston + co-founders @EzraFeilden & @AdiOltean

AI compute on Earth is limited by power & permitting. @Starcloud_ is moving it to orbit, where solar power is nearly constant. Philip says the dawn-dusk orbit alone could fit about 10 TW of compute, roughly 20x the entire US power grid. Once launch costs fall below $500/kg, he says compute in space will be cheaper than on the ground.

From Starcloud 1, Starcloud 2, to Starcloud 3, we saw: 

Tracking Starcloud 1 live in orbit, circling Earth every 90 minutes at 17,000 mph with the first Nvidia H100 in space.

Co-Founder & Chief Engineer Adi Oltean walks through Starcloud 2 as the team fires the latches that deploy its 120 ft solar wingspan. It launches in January with 100x the power of Starcloud 1. 

Co-Founder & CTO Ezra Feilden shows the 16-ton secondhand vibe table. The team bought it for $200K, instead of paying $1.5M & waiting 2 years for a new one, they rebuilt it over a weekend.

Engineering Manager Bailey Montaño leak checks the ion thruster after vibe. Bailey designed the radiators, which have 10x less mass & cost 500x less per watt than the ISS’s. 

In the fab shop, Ezra shows the Starcloud 3 demonstrator, a 2-ton, 235 kW vehicle that fits 50 to a Starship. 

Camilo Lopez cuts stainless on the laser cutter. 

Engineering Operations Lead Miguel Rivera, formerly of Helion Energy, teaches me to MIG weld.

The tour ends in the new campus, about 100,000 sqft built to produce 100 satellites a week toward an 88,000-satellite constellation.

In the case of Lighter:

1. All data is verifiable - you don't have to trust the operator.  Withdraw your funds via escape hatch if Lighter stops operating. There are CLOBs for other products like spot/options where realtime settlement makes a difference, and it is synergistic via portfolio margin

2. Lighter can trivially offer privacy to traders by encrypting data (with the trader's public key) before it's posted to Ethereum. This does not affect the escape hatch. Position level privacy can be mandatory, opt-in, or opt-out. Trades, volume and open interest can remain public, verifiable info while individual trader positions remain hidden

3. No priority fees on Lighter. 

4. Combining onshore/offshore orderbooks is technically possible but that's up to the regulators.

5. Lighter matching engine is centralized and highly performant. There is no tradeoff between speed and security. If there is inefficiency, it is the cost of generating and publishing proofs of correct execution, which is low and continuing to drop quickly.

Further to my post about @NYSE working to bring @HyperliquidX onshore, major credit to @ChairmanSelig and the Trump administration for making all of this experimentation possible. 

There’s only one way of finding out if something is useful to the marketplace and I’m excited for us to find out. I do have some questions:

1. What is the benefit of trading perps on-chain on a regulated exchange? Isn’t the main benefit of trading on-chain to operate in a trustless (aka non-kyc’d) environment in order to minimize friction, and/or to be able to enter into atomic transactions in order to receive what you are buying in realtime? Since a perp is not an asset, that obviously isn’t helpful. 

2. @standuquesne - are you aware that if you trade on Hyperliquid, the world will be able to track your positions and trades in real time? Do you see that as a benefit?

3. Hyperliquid has priority fees - a mechanism that enables market participants to pay to see information first, or even prioritize orders in front of the queue. Is this consistent with CFTC core principles?

4. Will it be possible to combine the liquidity of the offshore order-book with the onshore order-book?

5. If not, wouldn’t it be better to list perps in a traditional (centralized) order-book on a regulated exchange and not have the inefficiencies that on-chain matching introduces?

text:
最近一直在想一个问题下一轮 Crypto 的新叙事，到底会是什么？

DeFi、Meme、铭文，这几轮玩法基本都走过了。早期确实出现过很多倍数，但现在再想从这些成熟赛道里找机会，难度已经越来越高。

我最近反而在关注一种新的资产发行方式

AI Agent + Fair Mint

为什么会想到这个 ，因为我觉得现在 AI 的发展阶段，有点像当年铭文刚出来的时候。

铭文当时最吸引人的地方，不是资产本身有多复杂，而是发行方式变了。大家按照同一套规则参与 Mint，不需要提前找庄家拿筹码，也不用一开始就面对内盘大户的成本优势。

如果把这个逻辑放到 AI Agent 上，会不会出现一种新的玩法？

通过 AI Agent 完成资产 Mint，让参与者在相对公平的规则下获取筹码，同时限制内盘预留和大户提前囤积，尽可能拉平早期参与者的成本。

这样发行出来的资产，至少在起跑线上，不会一开始就出现特别夸张的成本差距。

当然，Fair Mint 不代表一定能涨，也不代表后面没有庄家。

真正决定一个资产能走多远的，还是后面的共识、持币地址增长、筹码分布，以及有没有机会进入更大的交易市场。

如果这套模式真的跑通，后面的玩法可能也不会陌生   ，早期 Fair Mint，后续做任务、刷 Discord、拿白名单，再到生态项目不断出现。

这套路径是不是有点像当年的铭文？我觉得现在 AI 的发展阶段，确实给这种新发行模式提供了很好的土壤。

下一轮机会未必是再发明一种新资产，而是重新设计一次资产发行的规则。

しかもRedditは自分の投稿データをGoogleにAIの学習用として売っていたから、自分で育てたAIに客を取られたというなんとも惨い結果になってしまってる。

そこからRedditが考えて出した答えが「ログインしないと中身を見せない」という仕組み。
これがインターネットの次の段階で、情報だけ抜いて人を送り返してもらえないなら、中身を開けておく理由がない。だからもうシャットアウトすることになった。
Redditが閉めたら、同じ状況のサイトは全部後に続いて閉めていくに決まっている。

そうなると不都合が生じるのは誰が考えてもわかると思う。しかも困るのはAIだ。AIが出す答えの元ネタは人間が開かれたネットに書いた文章。そのネットをAI自身が閉じるように動いている。自分の餌場を自分で潰している構造とそっくりなんだよな。

このニュースはRedditの株が落ちたって話じゃなくて「人の為に書いて人が来る、それで食っていける」っていう、ネットが30年回してきた仕組みが壊れたって話なんだよね。将来は誰にも分からないが、既存のネットの仕組みは崩壊が近づいている。

感の良い人はもうそれを予測して、既に動いているのかもしれない。

好TM格局！这次Polymarket的处理，我是真的服了。

昨天我还在吐槽，自己在Poly上的两个仓位被黑客强行卖掉，余额被全部转走。

当时我就在想，钱被盗了可以赔，那些被黑客低价卖掉的仓位，额外造成的损失怎么算？

没想到今天官方就给出了答案。

不仅全额赔付被盗资金，连强制卖仓产生的滑点、暂停交易期间造成的部分损失，也一起补了。

我刚看了下自己的账户，好像还比原来多了一点。

这次Poly总共拿出390万美元赔偿用户，其中270万用于弥补被盗损失，另外120万用于覆盖相关交易损失。

而且不需要用户自己提交申请，官方直接根据链上和交易记录识别受害账户，自动赔付。

反正这次Poly的善后，给个五星好评不为过。
author: Mulight
quoted_text:
昨晚Poly被盗的不用担心了，官方已经明确会全额赔付

一万美金以下的会在今天之前到账，超过一万美金的需要通过邮件签署一个表单。

速度还是挺快的，刚看了下我的已经到账了，可以正常提现和交易，千万记得要把2FA设置好

下面再次梳理下Poly被盗全过程

今天凌晨，我也成了 @Polymarket  被盗的受害者之一。

原本还在正常交易的两个仓位，突然被人卖掉，随后账户里的U被全部提走，我用的是Google登录，

一开始还以为是自己的账号出了问题。直到顺着链上记录追查，才发现是被黑客入侵了，并且Polymarket 这次出事的规模远比想象中大。

目前到底损失了多少钱？

据Bubblemaps后续统计，超过700名用户受到影响，涉及资金约 346 万美元。

其中约270万美元被换成 POL转出，另外约75万美元仍留在 Polymarket。

这还不是官方公布的最终损失数字。

黑客到底是怎么做到的？

目前的调查指向第三方网站监控服务DebugBear。

安全研究人员发现，攻击者通过被入侵的第三方脚本，利用用户已经登录的 Polymarket 会话，尝试自动卖出仓位、转换资产，再通过 Relay 把钱转走。

即使 Google 账号本身没有被盗，只要打开了加载恶意脚本的页面，已有的交易权限就可能被利用。

现在平台已经恢复了交易，并承诺全额赔偿所有受影响用户。

庆幸的是，官方没有回避这次安全事件，也明确作出了赔付承诺。

但还有一个问题

除了被提走的余额，那些被黑客低价卖掉的仓位，造成的额外损失又该怎么算？

希望Polymarket后续公布详细的赔付方案，包括受影响用户如何确认资格、赔付金额如何计算，以及具体的到账时间。

我的金额不大，但是被盗真的比亏钱还难受

也希望这次所有真正受到影响的用户，都能顺利拿回自己的钱，另外做好安全防护，年底了，保护好自己的钱包

text:
Never take out crypto-backed loans. Not even against Bitcoin. Here's my story from the October 10, 2025 crash.

Two months before the crash, I borrowed against 5 bitcoin:native  (~$600K at the time) through Coinbase's Morpho lending service.

BTC was trading around $120K. My liquidation price was ~$100K. I figured I'd have plenty of time to add collateral or repay the loan if BTC started falling.

I couldn't have been more wrong.

On October 10, BTC plunged from $120K to $115K, $110K, then $102K within an hour.

I had enough USDC sitting on Coinbase to repay my entire loan. But Morpho stopped working. Repayment attempts failed.

I even tried liquidating other holdings and transferring additional funds. Nothing worked. 10 attempt to pay off the loan and all in vain.

At $103K, I genuinely thought my 5 BTC were gone. I was sitting at my desk contemplating how I would recover from this.

Fortunately, BTC rebounded near $102K. Once the platform stabilized, I repaid everything and withdrew my Bitcoin.

The lesson? Liquidation risk isn't your only enemy. Platform failure during extreme volatility can wipe you out EVEN WHEN YOU HAVE THE FUNDS TO SAVE YOURSELF.

Never again. No leverage. No crypto-backed loans. Not even Bitcoin.

And here's the part most people still don't understand:

Your BTC is used to mint cbBTC out of thin air, which gets pushed onto @Morpho. If Morpho gets hacked or the cbBTC disappears, Coinbase loses none of the collateralized BTC.

You do.

Coinbase keeps the real BTC.

So the borrower gets:

• Morpho risk
• Wrapped BTC risk

...AND now gets to pay 2x to 3x higher interest for that risk.

感谢近期大家 Peer 的关注。下面简单说明 Peer 怎么运作，以及使用协议时需要了解的事项。

Peer 是非托管 P2P 消息协议：由一组智能合约和验证节点（attestor）组成。Peer 目前支持 12 种支付方式。任何开发者都可以接入新的支付方式，把协议集成进自己的应用，或者为 https://t.co/UzX8D8UEQn 做一个替代前端。

协议如何运行：卖家把 USDC 挂进合约，买家用自己的支付宝直接付给卖家本人账户。付款在 TEE（隔离硬件环境）里核验通过后，合约自动放币。Peer 不碰法币，也不托管你的 USDC。

验证不用支付宝或其他支付平台的开发者 API。用户用自己的登录会话发起验证，会话加密进 TEE；TEE 确认付款、出证明，合约直接校验，中间没有 Peer 代收代付。
协议文档：https://t.co/wLsLQHQ6eS

对用户来说：
Peer 直接沿用各支付平台已完成的身份验证，前端按行业标准做钱包地址筛查。建议用户对交易对手再做一层核实。

卖家可以在智能合约里给订单加风控：买家白名单、额外 KYC、限额、价格下限、最长 T+14 延迟结算、链上争议。

协议无需许可，这些控制内置在协议里。这些技术功能和控制不能凌驾于适用法律之上，也不保证账户不会被限制或冻结。用户须对使用协议的方式负责，包括遵守适用于自己的法律和平台条款。

quoted_text:
Appreciate everyone taking an interest in Peer and our recent announcement. Here is an explainer on how Peer works and what users should be aware of using the protocol:

Peer is a noncustodial messaging protocol comprised of a set of smart contracts and attestors. Peer currently supports 12 payment methods with the most recent one being Alipay. Any developer can create a payment method integration, integrate the protocol into their app, or create an alternative interface to https://t.co/00wnZZ53BK

How the protocol works:
A seller posts a USDC listing into a smart contract, a buyer pays the seller directly, and the contract releases the USDC automatically once the payment is verified in a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE). As an onchain and permissionless protocol, Peer never holds or transmits users' fiat and never takes custody of their USDC.

Verification uses no developer APIs from Alipay or from other existing supported platforms. Instead, users initiate verification using their own session encrypted to the TEE, which confirms the payment and signs an attestation that the contract verifies without Peer or anyone in the middle.

Read our protocol docs: https://t.co/T1taTx27fD

For users:
Peer directly inherits verified identity from the integrated payment platforms, and our interface follows industry standard wallet address screening. Users are encouraged to do additional vetting for their counterparties.

Peer gives sellers controls in the smart contract for managing risk for their own ads. This includes tools for whitelisting buyers, requiring additional KYC, and controls such as order limits, price floors, up to T+14 deferred settlement, and onchain dispute resolution.

The protocol is permissionless, with these controls built in. These technical features and controls do not override applicable law or guarantee protection against account restrictions or freezes. Users are responsible for how they use the protocol, including complying with the laws and platform terms that apply to them.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. 

Get started now at https://t.co/00wnZZ53BK

最近 Anthropic 有一笔账，被日本博主 pal9999 算得很扎心。
他的数字是这样的。Anthropic手上现金约 1100 亿美元，11 月 IPO 预计再融 1000 亿左右，加起来 2100 亿。

可按他从招股书里整理的设备投资，2027 年要 1000 到 1200 亿，2028 年 1350 到 1600 亿，2029 年 1500 到 1700 亿。照这个速度，两年出头现金就花完。

缺口只能借。问题在评级。FT 报道，Blackstone 已经提醒投资人，Anthropic IPO 后的信用评级大概率是「高垃圾级」，原本以为能拿投资级。垃圾级意味着银行、养老金这类钱很难进来，借钱成本也更高。

收入涨得是真快，这点股票市场看得很清楚。但债券市场看的是还钱的时间表，算力要电、要地，涨不了那么快。

评级给垃圾级，是在提醒大家，这家公司的故事是靠持续融资撑着跑的。估值和评级这么拧着，接下来谁来接这笔桥接融资，比下一个模型发布更值得盯。

quoted_text:
ちとアンソロピックの話するよー

まずアンソロピックが現在もってる現金が１１００億ドル。

１１月のIPOで調達できる金額がおよそ１０００億ドル。

併せて手持ちの現金２１００億ドル。

一方でアンソロピックに必要な設備投資費用は

2027年1000〜1200億ドル
2028年1350〜1600億ドル
2029年1500〜1700億ドル

となってる。中身はMS、google、amazon、ネオクラウド、spaceX、AMDとの契約。S-1が出所。

S-1だけみても、２年で手持ちの現金が尽きる計算になる。

2027年に売り上げが１０００億を超えてると予測してるけど帳簿上はトントンになる。だが現金は減る。他にも費用あるから。

問題は固定費である。現在はAIの訓練費用に年120億ドルだが、訓練の費用は指数関数的にあがる。

2027年には訓練費だけで400〜800億ドル、その後も上がり続ける。これは指数関数的に上がる。AIはそういう風に出来ている。

2027年に1000億、2028年に1500億という売り上げ予測もあるが、「計算能力が指数で増え、売上もそれに付いてくる」って前提で組んである。

だが現実は計算能力は電力と立地という物理で線形にしか伸びず、売上も市場の限界で線形にしか増えない。

つまり支払いは指数で組まれていて、計算能力と売り上げは線形なんだ。これが噛み合わないと支払い分が固定費として残る。

この固定費分はどこからファイナンスするしかない。そこで問題なのが「投資適格格付け」なんだけど、これがなんとジャンク級と格付け会社から判断されたのさ。これだと市場から金を借りるのが難しい。

正直言って、これは意外だった。ブラックストーンと格付け会社がグルになってIPOの為に無理やり通すと思っていたので。

このまま行くとアンソロピックは「2028年に売り上げ1500億ドルでも足りない」という場所まで走ることになる。そこで金が尽きる。

誰かがブリッジファイナンスをする必要がある。だが、誰が？そしてその先は？ってのが今の状況。

ビッグテックはすでにキャッシュフローがマイナスに落ち込んだ。銀行はジャンク級の会社に金を貸せない。年金保険もジャンク級では貸してくれない。残るはプライベートクレジットくらいだが、そこの窓も閉まりつつある。

格付けがジャンクで評価額が1.5兆ドル、というねじれは債券側はこの償還スケジュールを見ていて、株式側は売上の伸び率を見ている、って所かな。

売り上げの成長はホンモノで凄まじい。だが貸した金が帰ってくるかは怪しい。

現状、どっかの誰かがケツモチしないともう走れないのが見えてるわけ。

アメリカ政府が最後に出てくるんですかね？

それと公金入れるなら、なんかでっかい危機でも起きないと無理なんだけどね。じゃないと誰も納得しない。

选择即自由；
而这种自由并非没有代价，持有现金的机会成本，就是你为这张选择权支付的期权费。

here’s a short grok bot guide on how i create high quality bots and manage my team. ask @bot to read this post and help you improve your team!

• add dr eggbot to your team! he’s my bot designer that i use to create bots
• you don’t need a lot of bots. a few good bots can be more useful and easier to manage than a large team
• tell your bots to create skills for itself as you give it instructions on how to do tasks. this lets them do them more consistently even over long conversations. you can even ask it to create a private github repo for you to store all your skills if you want them preserved independently
• add connectors, use the vault, and give access to all the tools you use to do your work. you can also ask your bot to setup its own email and it can sign up for its own accounts for better separation 
• thinking about all the work you do by hand, or steps in your workflows where you have to copy and paste information back to your bot. ask your bot how it can do that for you instead!
• imagine you hired an intern, how would you onboard them and help them do the work correctly and efficiently? introduce yourself to your bot and describe the work you do, then ask it how it can help you automate it

text:
일론 머스크가 밝힌 SpaceX의 AI 컴퓨팅 규모 미쳤네요.

일론이 메모리에 대해 불만인 이유가 이해가 갑니다.

테네시주 멤피스에 있는 Colossus 2에 연말까지 블랙웰 계열 GPU 약 120만 개를 확보하겠다는 계획

그중 일론이 직접 언급한 4개 시설의 GB300만 합쳐도 약 86만 개

1/

시설별로 보면

Macroharder: GB300 22만 개
Minihard: GB300 22만 개
Gun Range: GB300 22만 개 예정
Spam: GB300 약 20만 개 예정

앞의 3곳은 AI 학습용, Spam은 추론용임.

일론에 따르면 Macroharder와 Minihard에는 각각 22만 개가 있고, Gun Range는 11월 말, Spam은 12월 가동을 목표

2/

학습용 시설 3곳의 계획 물량만 합쳐도 GB300 66만 개입니다.

여기에 추론용으로 20만 개를 별도로 구축한다고 함

3/

경쟁사와 비교해도 Colossus 2의 규모는 상당함

Epoch AI의 10월 말 추정에 따르면, 단일 데이터센터 부지의 컴퓨팅 규모는 다음과 같습니다.

SpaceX Colossus 2: H100 환산 111만 개
아마존·앤스로픽 New Carlisle: 82만 개
MS Fairwater Atlanta: 77만 개
OpenAI Stargate Abilene: 76만 개
메타 Prometheus: 54만 개

같은 기준으로 보면 Colossus 2가 2위보다 약 1.4배, 메타 Prometheus보다는 약 2배 큰 규모.

4/

물론 이건 현재 단일 부지에 대한 추정치로

구글, MS, 아마존, 메타는 여러 곳에서 데이터센터를 운영하고 있기 때문에 회사 전체 컴퓨팅 자원을 비교한 순위는 아님..

메타도 Prometheus를 향후 약 100만 GPU 규모로 확장하겠다고 밝힌 만큼 바뀔 수도 있음.

5/

Spam 같은 경우 일론은 이 시설에 GB300 약 20만 개를 넣되, 학습이 아닌 추론용으로 사용하겠다고 밝힘.

AI 모델을 학습시키는 데만 막대한 GPU가 필요한 게 아닙니다. 이용자가 늘고, AI가 답변을 위해 더 오래 생각하고, 에이전트가 상시 작업하게 되면 추론을 위한 컴퓨팅 수요도 계속 커지게 됨.

6/

엄청난 HBM이 필요할 것.

GB300 NVL72는 GPU당 HBM3E 288GB를 탑재합니다. 일론이 말한 GB300 86만 개가 모두 이 GPU 기준이라면, 단순 계산상 HBM 용량만 약 248PB.

quoted_text:
I am for an AI pause, meaning a pause to training frontier models.

I think the AI models we have now are amazing. They save an incredible amount of human labor and can help drive science and technology forward and accelerate them enormously. I reckon it would take a decade to even disseminate current AI capabilities through society and make full use of them.

Driving the frontier forward from here will massively increase the risks. If we value human life, we should try to keep things at timescale that humans can react. The risks of things  happening that most of us find abhorrent will increase a lot otherwise. This will mean not getting some of the benefits of AI, but on balance, I think the risks are now getting too high.

Practical ways to implement this pause are:
 - USA to ban training of new frontier models in a suitable way
 - USA and China making a treaty and encouraging more countries to join
 - Enforcement can be via limits on hardware or large data centers, probably both

I don't think that this pause should be forever. The goal is to slow down the frontier, let society catch up, and make it more resilient (better resistance to cyber and biological threats, individuals managing more of their life with AI , democratic resilience). In a few years time, we can be in a better place to take the next steps. The goal is not to stop AI and its benefits forever, it's preserving and improving human life through it, and that's only possible by slowing it down to human timescales for now.

author: hnshah
quoted_text:
I'm now building an "improvements" feature into all of my personal vibecoded applications: a freeform text input that's hooked up to an agent that yolo implements whatever is submitted.

It's an interesting experience -- the activation energy barrier to sanding any rough edge or implementing any new feature becomes extremely low. Someone else who uses one of the applications I created has already implemented 150 improvements over the course of a few days. This pattern feels like a new kind of tool -- liquid software? -- and every application that doesn't have this feature now has a slightly rigid and anachronistic flavor. Why can't I just tell it how I want it to be different?

Now, it's not obvious to me how this pattern can or should scale. Does it become unmaintainable after a while? (Maybe model intelligence improvement outstrips my feature appetite such that it's fine?) How does collaborative software work in this model? Can software designed this way be secure and reliable?

Whatever the larger questions about broader deployment, it definitely works great in a personal context. It reminds me a little of the visions of Lisp/Lisp machines, Smalltalk, and HyperCard -- systems that the user can take control of and modify. Those visions never quite worked, though: the vast majority of software today is not end-user modifiable in any useful way. So, while this "liquid" affordance is a very small touch, the way it changes one's relation to the software feels a bit transgressive and empowering in a Lickliderian and Engelbartian way.

text:
Over the past two weeks iPhones have been publicly jailbroken more than once, and most people treated it as a bit of tech drama and scrolled on. I want to use it to talk about something that matters more to people in crypto: wiping an old iPhone, putting it in airplane mode and using it only to hold your seed phrase is not as safe as most people think. If it's an iPhone 11 or older, the problem lives in the chip, and no iOS update will fix it.

Quick recap of what happened. On October 16 at Hexacon in Paris, the Calif team jailbroke an iPhone 18 Pro running iOS 27.0.1 live on stage. The jailbreak survived a reboot, they had root, and they got past MIE, the hardware memory protection Apple added starting with the A19 specifically to stop spyware. In the same session they showed attacks that get in through a single click in Signal or iMessage. A week later, on the day iPhone Duo went on sale, they jailbroke that too. Apple shipped iOS 27.2 on October 26, and Calif says most of the bugs they used are now fixed. Then on October 30, Ikotas Labs, the Japanese team that just won Pwn2Own, posted that they had jailbroken 27.2 as well. Their video only shows swapped icons and the version number, though, so I'm treating it as unconfirmed for now.

For most people on a recent phone who keep it updated, none of this is a reason to panic. Before chains like these get patched, they usually sit with spyware vendors and forensics companies, and the odds of an ordinary person being specifically targeted are low. Update to 27.2 and you've done what you need to.

The people I actually want to warn are those using an old iPhone as a cold wallet. iPhone 4S through iPhone X have checkm8 in the BootROM, made public in 2019. This June, usbliter8 went public, covering the iPhone XS, XR, the 11 series and the 2nd-gen SE. The BootROM is boot code burned into the chip at the factory. Apple can't patch it with a software update, so these devices will carry the hole for as long as they exist. Exploiting it doesn't need a network either. Once someone has your phone in hand, they put it into DFU mode and plug in a custom USB board (the public research used a $5 Raspberry Pi Pico 2), and they can run their own code before iOS even boots. Airplane mode makes no difference here.

I don't want to overstate it. On models like the XS and 11, the BootROM bug alone won't hand over your seed phrase, because your passcode and the Secure Enclave are still in the way. The trouble is that these remaining layers are exactly where people tend to cut corners: a 6-digit passcode, an iOS version years out of date with a pile of public n-days, a short wallet app password. On some older models, forensic tools use bugs like this to brute-force the passcode. And if your wallet app encrypts the seed with nothing but a short password, once that encrypted file is copied off, the attacker can take it home and keep guessing offline, with no attempt limit. Old iOS versions also have a charging port problem. ChoiceJacking, published in 2025, lets a malicious charger pose as a keyboard and approve the data-access prompt for you. Apple only closed that in iOS 18.4.

One more thing about this kind of attack: when you get your phone back, nothing looks off. In security circles it's called an evil maid attack. A hotel room, a security check, lending your phone to someone to charge — any time it's out of your hands for a while, there's an opening. A lot of people only find out their phone was touched after their assets are already gone.

My advice:

1. Check which iPhone holds your seed phrase (Settings → General → About). If it's an iPhone 11 or older, move to a newer model before storing a seed on it.

2. If you've already stored one there, no need to panic. When you get a chance, generate a brand-new seed phrase in an environment you trust and move your assets over. It has to be a whole new seed. A fresh address under the old seed won't help.

3. If your phone has ever been out of your hands for a while, say held for inspection at a border, don't wait. Migrate as in step 2 as soon as you can.

4. Update your daily iPhone to iOS 27.2 (Settings → General → Software Update). If you haven't moved to 27 yet, install at least 26.7.2.

5. Switch to a long alphanumeric passcode (Settings → Face ID & Passcode → Change Passcode → Passcode Options). A 6-digit PIN has only a million possible combinations. Make your wallet app password longer too.

6. Carry your own charger. Don't use public USB ports, random power banks or cables you don't know.

7. If you hold a lot or are likely to be targeted, consider turning on Lockdown Mode (Settings → Privacy & Security → Lockdown Mode). It blocks wired connections while the phone is locked.

8. Any "iOS 27 jailbreak download," or any tutorial asking you to install a certificate or configuration profile, is a scam or malware. Neither Calif nor Ikotas has released any tools.

If you like using an iPhone as a cold wallet, go with a newer model and keep it on the latest iOS. There's no public BootROM exploit for the iPhone 12 or later, and if something does turn up, Apple can still fix it with an update. With really old devices, the risk sits in the chip itself, and updating iOS won't get you around it.
