The Middle East at a Critical Crossroads: Geopolitical Escalation and the Reshaping of the International Order

Based on the prevailing political, military, and strategic indicators, the Middle East appears to be entering an exceptionally dangerous period of geopolitical escalation. Major regional and international actors are intensifying their preparations, while recent statements from Washington suggest the possibility of renewed military operations.

As I argued two months ago, the state of “neither war nor peace” can, in certain respects, be more dangerous than war itself. Prolonged strategic uncertainty paralyses economic activity, discourages investment, constrains political decision-making, and gradually undermines the foundations of regional stability.

In my assessment, what we are witnessing today extends far beyond conventional regional conflicts. We are entering a period of profound structural transformation in the international system, characterised by intensifying competition among major powers seeking to redefine the global balance of power and establish the rules of an emerging international order.

The United States and Russia remain central to these developments. Despite their strategic rivalry, both powers continue to pursue their respective geopolitical interests through a combination of confrontation, diplomatic bargaining, and selective accommodation.

The diplomatic dynamics surrounding the Western Sahara question at the United Nations Security Council offer an interesting illustration of how major-power interests can intersect, even amid broader geopolitical competition. Such developments must, however, be distinguished from the formal exercise of veto powers.

My central argument is that we are not merely witnessing another cycle of regional instability. We are observing a potentially historic transition in the international order, one whose political, economic, and security implications may prove considerably more profound than currently anticipated.

The most important strategic question is therefore no longer simply whether another military confrontation will occur, but whether regional states possess the political independence, institutional resilience, and strategic foresight necessary to safeguard their national interests amid an increasingly unpredictable international environment.

The danger lies not only in the possibility of war, but in the prolonged uncertainty preceding it, when economies stagnate, political institutions become constrained, and the strategic calculations of major powers increasingly determine the future of entire regions.

I appreciate @ilblackdragon saying this plainly.

@NEARProtocol 's privacy is confidential, not Zcash-level privacy. It keeps financial activity out of public view, but doesn't promise protection from government disclosure.

And I think that's a perfectly legitimate product to build.

Not everyone needs protection from the state. Plenty of people just don't want the world watching their balances, trades and payments.

Chad @CBarraford responded to this clip by calling NEAR "effectively an arm of the govt."

quite a leap, no?

Of course there's a legitimate concern underneath it: governments aren't automatically the good guys, and what qualifies as a lawful request in one country can be political persecution in another.

But that doesn't make commercial confidentiality a worthless product.

I think it comes down to: what does the operator already see, what can the MPC infrastructure decrypt, and who authorizes that disclosure?

text:
I've read maybe ~10,000 YC applications.  8000 for YC admissions/PG quite a few years ago and anther 2000 informally as an alum.

There's a new and growing mistake and I want to share why it's more important than you think.

By the way - I try not to ever say YC admissions works this way or that way.  That's YC's job and they're always changing things and making up their own minds.

But I will share my impression and you can see what you think - YC partners, please chime in as well if you like.

The YC application is fundamentally an evaluation of a founder's potential.  And much less an evaluation of a specific business.  (Airbedbreakfast transitioning into Airbnb because Brian, Nate, Joe never give up and never stop listening to their customers)

So, in your writing of the application, YOU need to shine through.

This batch, I read ~200 applications.  

I'm guessing over half were significantly written, edited, or polished with AI.

That half was easily in the bottom half of my informal rankings, almost every time.

To be clear, most were NOT AI slop.  I often couldn't tell at first they had used AI.  Founders were pouring their heart and soul into their app - so I what I received was high quality.

But I think the AI really hurt them.  Here's why:

Once polished by AI, I as reader lost insight into the personality of the writer.  

I love the YC application because the questions are the same questions I would ask in office hours or casually to a friend that wanted help with their startup.  It pushes the founder out of their pitchdeck/VC talk style into simple worded questions that can be answered simply as well.  And great founders shine through when they just write like they talk.  The LLM writing made answers feel more like a corporate cover letter, with the personality drained out.

The AI-assisted drafts also gave me a sense of mid work.  The writing itself seemed like zero standard deviations from the mean.  The LLMs had lopped off the outlier portions of sentences, paragraphs, and thoughts.  Given the YC App is an outlier detector, a writing tool that lops off outlier writing is the opposite of what you want.

And the AI writing was needlessly verbose.  Which hurts when a reliable predictor of great founders is that they're deep thinkers and deep thinking shines through in the density of their writing.

So...

I did an experiment.  I asked a bunch of these seemingly AI-assisted app writers to talk with me live.  I just asked them the same YC app questions and recorded their answers.

I then gave them back the transcripts.  Unedited and unpolished.

And...

OMG!  A good number turned from easy no to actual good applications.  

Magic!  Remove AI >> Improve application.

This happened BOTH with native English speakers and founders abroad.

So this is my recommendation to all of you.    

Don't let AI touch your application, even for a second.

And maybe try the dictation approach with a friend.

My apologies to the YC admissions team if you already knew AI-written applications were crap and you were using this insight to help you easily move applications to the No pile.

YC's Winter Batch Application deadline is Nov 2nd.

Zcashers have had a lot of discussion lately regarding governance. My intention with this post is not to influence anyone about their opinions on governance. I don’t think I’ll be effective in doing so anyways. My intention here is to improve the quality of discussion on future matters.

In order to do so I’ll first give you my opinion. My instinct as a relatively new (little more than a year) zcasher with no real insight into zcg is to gut it completely.

What gives me pause is that “I don’t know what I don’t know”. I haven’t tried to engage with ZCG, and people who I respect and admire are proponents of it, so I am hesitant to follow my gut.

In the end the compromise that has come about is my ideal solution. If we need to go further or made a mistake, we should iterate, but I’m glad there is motion in general.

Now, the reason for this post is that while we came to my ideal conclusion, I was not happy with the process.  A major flashpoint was targeting zcashers who were attempting to onboard users irl because they were sex workers.

If that gets you so upset I’m not sure why you are in the freedom money game. You could argue that the money shouldn’t be spent without coin holder approval, which is fine, but you didn’t do that. You targeted this one effort, when it should have been no different than any other expenditure. I then saw people on both sides of the issue treat each other like shit.

I can’t imagine all that negativity felt good. It didn’t feel good to watch it as an observer. You can have strong opinions about things without treating people poorly. 

I sometimes agree on certain topics with people who treat others poorly, and sometimes disagree with people who treat others well. I’d rather spend my time and energy with the people I disagree with that are capable of treating others well. 

I’m not asking any of you to be perfect moving forward. I’m certainly not. I’m just asking we all please take this as a learning experience to reinforce what not to do when we talk to each other.

If you did say something you regret. Maybe take the time to reach out and apologize. Not for your beliefs, or opinions, but how you treated someone in our community. We are stuck together, and we have a long way to go onboarding more people.

Onward. Together.

text:
Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi says if frontier models stopped advancing, it wouldn't matter for most orgs because enterprise AI is bottlenecked on context, not intelligence:

"There's no agentic work that's automated the whole enterprise. That has just not happened. Why is that? The real reason is the models are smart enough, but they just don't have the context that exists inside of any organization."

"They have not been in every meeting. They don't know what's in everybody's heads. They don't know all the processes. There's always a couple of employees who know everything in every organization. You go tap on their shoulder, and everybody's like, 'Oh my God, what would happen if he or she quits?'"

"If you just fused that and gave that context into the AI models, just the frontier today, I think there's so much productivity gains you could get for any organization on the planet."

"For that, we actually don't need smarter models... If the frontier doesn't advance, it doesn't actually matter for the vast majority of organizations on the planet. They're just so far behind in the adoption curve of actually automating things and getting value out of this stuff."

软件内之前的领涨股 $PLTR $TEAM 来到 EMA50但未见止跌的迹象，比较强的 $GTLB 也以缺口的方式进行下跌。板块内 $TWLO $SNOW $DDOG $NOW 等已经开始破位。网络安全也有 $FTNT 财报的大跌。当然有一些软件还算坚挺， $TTAN $INTU $WDAY $MNDY $ADBE ，但整个软件板块已经不具备领导板块的条件。

Pèp ayisyen,

Nou prèske fin deplwaye sòlda nou yo ak ekipman nou yo sou tè Ayiti. Sa a se pa yon operasyon kont pèp ayisyen an, ni yon envazyon peyi Ayiti. Nou pa yon gwo pisans. Nou pa gen okenn enterè ni pou nou vin domine pèp ayisyen an, ni pou nou mete men sou richès Ayiti.

Nou se yon peyi modès k ap devlope. Sèl sa nou vle, se pou kat teknisyen avyasyon nou yo tounen lakay yo. Epi n ap bay gang yo yon leson, gang sa yo k ap fè pèp ayisyen an soufri, ki touye moun pèp la renmen yo, k ap anpeche l viv yon lavi nòmal, lib, san laperèz.

Se prèske nou menm sèl k ap peye pou operasyon sa a. Menmsi nou resevwa yon ti èd lojistik nan men kèk lòt peyi, se ak pwòp ti kès nou n ap kouvri 90% nan depans yo.

Sa koute nou chè, men nou te aprann nan pwòp soufrans nou: jistis ak lapè pa gen pri. Nou te pase nan menm soufrans Ayiti ap travèse jodi a. Nou te viv yon beny san ki te pi terib toujou pase sa pèp ayisyen an ap sibi kounye a. Nou konnen sa sa vle di: viv nan laperèz, pa fè politisyen konfyans, pa kwè okenn moun ki pwomèt l ap ede w. Paske pèsonn pa t vin ede nou, e moun ki te vini yo pa t gen bon entansyon nan kè yo.

Men nou te rive chape anba sa. Apre 200 lane soufrans, finalman n ap viv nan lapè, e jodi a nou se peyi ki gen plis sekirite sou kontinan an.

Nou pa vin ann Ayiti pou nou touche lajan, paske pèsonn pa peye nou pou sa. Nou vin ann Ayiti pou nou goumen kont mechan yo.

Men sa m ap mande nou: fè nou konfyans, lapriyè sèl vrè Bondye a, epi mande L pou L geri Ayiti.

“Lè sa a si pèp ki pote non m lan lapriyè nan pye m, si yo soumèt devan mwen, si yo pran chache m ankò, si yo vire do bay vye peche yo t'ap fè yo, m'ap tande yo nan syèl kote m ye a, m'ap padonnen peche yo, m'ap fè peyi a kanpe ankò.”

2 Kwonik 7:14

Ede nou ede Ayiti.

Epi lè misyon nou an fini, n ap tounen lakay nou. Petèt jenerasyon Ayisyen k ap vini yo ap sonje nou kòm zanmi ki te vin ede yon lè.

The FBI is releasing information advising the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, on or about October 29, 2026. The FBI refers to this specific North Korean malicious cyber activity as "TraderTraitor."

The FBI, together with partners at the USSS and IRS-CI, has observed TraderTraitor actors converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum (ETH). It is expected these assets will then be further laundered by converting them using DeFi and instant swap services as they prepare them for further laundering stages.

How You Can Help:
FBI, USSS, and IRS-CI are urging private sector entities including THORNode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms, and other virtual asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets.

A list of addresses associated with this activity is available here: https://t.co/g0oIWx0WeD

text:
Arini, the hedge fund started by ex-Credit Suisse distressed trader Hamza Lemssouguer, launched in 2022 with about $1 billion in AUM

The fund grew to run roughly $22 billion, with their flagship vehicle managing $7.5 billion as of July 2026. About 33% of fund vehicles are in CLOs, and another $4 billion raised for direct lending

The fund's strategy was simple. Make bets on highly distressed businesses to extract premium yield vs. the market.

While most credit managers lean towards being highly diversified due to the asymmetric payouts in debt markets, Arini took a different approach by taking concentrated levered bets on their positions

This worked until it doesn't, and this year has been a rough journey for the fund. Bloomberg recently reported that their flagship fund is -26% YTD through October 2026

Here are the 3 positions where Arini has lost the most dollars.

1. Altice International

Altice International is Patrick Drahi's holding company for telecom operations in Portugal, DR and Israel. It carried roughly €8.9bn of senior secured debt and €675mm of senior notes against €1.5bn of LTM EBITDA.

The two crown jewel assets in the business were Altice Caribbean (DR business) and the Portugal subsidiary. The two combined generated 75% of revenue and 80% of EBITDA for the entire business.

In November 2025, both of these were moved out of the restricted group. Altice Caribbean was designated to be an unrestricted subsidiary, and the company then raised €750 million of third-party capital secured against the unpledged assets

In July 2026, Altice then moved to sell the HOT Mobile Israel business for €356 million, leaving nothing of substance behind for the lenders.

Altice International's secured 2028 and 2029 bonds fell 6-8 points in the mid-60s, and the €675 million of senior notes fell 14 points to 16 cents on the dollar. By October, even the senior secured bonds were trading below 50 cents.

The lender group sent a default notice on 2028 notes, claiming that the €5 billion of intercompany loans and the unrestricted designations extracted substantially all value out of the business, and Altice International never made the change of control offer that would refinance the debt

By August, Arini and Silver Point were fighting other lenders for priority in the capital structure. Negotiating group also includes Diameter, Invesco, King Street, Sona and Elliott Management

2. Aston Martin

Arini owned the distressed car company's 10% senior secured notes due 2029. In July 2026, Aston borrowed £550 million from HPS in the form of a £450 million SONIA + 675 senior term loan and a £100 million delayed draw term loan.

The HPS loan was secured on assets placed in a newly created unrestricted subsidiary, while the existing notes that Arini sat in were secured by a pledge over the operating company's shares.

Aston Martin is currently a cash-flow-negative business with £340 million of cash against £250 million of LFCF burn per year. Shareholders have added £2 billion of equity since 2020, and the company recently sold its F1 team stake and naming rights for £156 million combined. 

By October, the secured notes that Arini invested in were trading at 47 cents on the dollar

3. Brightspeed

In 2022, Apollo bought Lumen's legacy copper phone business for $7.5 billion with the plan of building fiber passings.

By 2026, it was clear that the deal assumptions were far too lofty, with actual revenue per home passing sitting at roughly 33% of the original budget

Operating cash flow was -$2.2 billion in 2025, and cash balance at the company fell from $2.4 billion at year-end to $1.2 billion in June 2026

By 2Q26, the company issued a going concern warning. Reportedly, Apollo and PJT attempted to raise an ABS tranche secured by fiber subscription cash flows that would rank ahead of the existing lenders but struggled to find any buyers

Per reporting from the Wall Street Journal, Apollo confirmed that they are not willing to add more capital in a business that likely needs to raise an additional $3 billion to get through 2027

The Financial Times reported that Arini held substantial exposure in the company, but the tranche of debt held isn't public. Regardless, the company's debt has traded down significantly and Arini is feeling the pain of unrealized losses from their position

Based on the latest reporting, there have been rumors that a Chapter 11 filing could come as soon as December of this year.

text:
How to improve in web design

1.  Pick an art style
2. Capture your life

Do it often to create an arsenal of art direction.

My current favorite is mosaic

Tile size sets the art direction
- Small creates detail, it's modern
- Larger is traditional, like stained glass

Finishes determine reflections
- Glossy for near photo realistic
- Matte gives lighting without the flash

Mosaic dos and donts 
- Landscapes. Illustrations. Lettering.
- Faces. It's just creepy.

Grout. The most underrated aspect
- Grout lines define the separation
- Stronger lines feel more like art
- Thin w/ small tiles create detail

text:
Crypto 这个行业，真的该有一个能管事的联盟了！

看完 ArcBlock 创始人 Robert Mao 的《行业自救倡议书》，感触挺深。说真的，加密行业早就应该联合起来，建立一套应对黑客攻击、重大安全事故、诈骗项目和恶意市场操纵的行业协作机制。

这些年看下来，真的有点恨铁不成钢。各种黑客盗窃反复发生，各种 Rug 家常便饭，明明已经坑过投资者的项目，换个包装又能上交易所继续收割。

恶意控盘、拉盘砸盘几乎天天上演，最后受伤的永远是普通用户。

最让人无奈的是，这个行业不缺钱、不缺技术、更不缺聪明人，却始终缺少一个能把各方真正团结起来、推动行业共同治理的牵头力量。

SEAL、Crypto ISAC 这样的安全协作组织已经存在，但光防黑客远远不够。

交易所、钱包、项目方、安全机构完全可以建立更广泛的合作机制，共享黑名单和风险证据、联合应对突发事件、提高上币透明度，让那些反复作恶的人不能换个平台就继续收割。

我们天天喊去中心化、金融自由、改变世界，可如果连最基本的用户安全和行业信任都保护不好，谈什么大规模采用？

希望这次币安事件能成为一个转折点，也希望行业里真正有实力、有影响力的人能站出来，把大家团结起来。竞争归竞争，但行业的底线需要所有人一起守护。

加密向上！这个行业值得拥有一个更好的未来。

one of the main differentiating factors in the creation of consumer AI assistants today centers around user experiences

this is often focused on introducing new experiences that seamlessly translate into daily habits. two primary mechanisms for delivering these experiences found across both (1) vertical-domain assistants and (2) horizontal assistants are proactive AI agents and selective memory

1/ proactive AI is about the ability to provide a contextual, high-value experience that anticipates what matters to a user at a specific point in time

2/ selective memory is about recognizing what matters to a specific user and understanding how those preferences evolve over time. it is the foundation required to deliver deeply personalized experiences at scale

very excited for the future trajectory of the market. it is certainly a judgement heavy one!

text:
Marketing has become an incredibly sophisticated way for companies to avoid changing their minds.

A campaign underperforms, so we change the messaging. Signups increase, but customers don't stick around. We optimize onboarding and try again. Eventually, growth slows and the answer is to spend more.

At every step, there's an opportunity to question something about the product or the people we're trying to reach. Yet it's easier to keep improving the marketing than reconsider the decisions behind it.

There's another problem hiding in the numbers. Marketing influences who becomes a customer, which means it also influences the feedback that shapes the product. Attract the wrong people and you can spend months building exactly what they ask for.

AI makes this even more interesting. Producing campaigns is getting cheaper while the cost of acting on the wrong assumptions remains just as real. We can reach more people than ever without understanding any of them better.

Imagine treating every campaign as an opportunity to learn something that could change the business.

We've gotten remarkably good at measuring how people respond to marketing. We should get just as good at understanding what those responses mean.

author: kennedy_6190
quoted_text:
The Binance hacker might have just executed one of the most brilliant moves in crypto.

First, Tether froze $1.5 billion worth of USDT.

Then Circle followed by freezing another $800 million in USDC.

At that point, it seemed like the hacker’s funds were completely trapped.

But apparently, he had already thought several steps ahead.

Rather than keeping the stolen USDT in a wallet, he allegedly deposited it into Aave and used it as collateral to borrow ETH.

Then he walked away.

And this is where things get really interesting.

Tether can freeze the USDT sitting in that wallet.

But it can’t freeze the ETH that was already borrowed.

So now, Aave is left with frozen collateral, while the hacker is holding liquid ETH.

And unless the protocol finds a way to recover those funds, he might not even have to repay the loan.

Two companies froze billions of dollars in seconds.

Yet someone who understood how DeFi works may have found a way to bypass both restrictions.

Pretty wild when you think about it.

text:
Ten million people have watched a comedian accidentally destroy the entire TED talk industry.

He filmed the talk once at TEDxNewYork in 2014 and openly admitted he had nothing to say.

Speaking coaches charge $5,000 to teach the exact tricks he used in 6 minutes to say nothing at all.

His name is Will Stephen. He is a comedian from Late Night with Seth Meyers who was invited to give a real TED talk and used it to prove the format is a costume anyone can wear.

Every TED speaker opens with a question, tells a personal story, cites a scientist, and shows a chart. Stephen did all four in six minutes with zero content.

His entire formula fits on a napkin.

Gesture with both hands. Ask the audience a question anyone can answer. Tell a mildly embarrassing story so they say aww. Point to a stranger on a slide and call them important. Flash a chart of random numbers. Wear glasses with no lenses. The audience will think you are brilliant.

That last trick alone has probably cost the public speaking coaching industry a hundred million dollars in sessions clients should have skipped.

"If you watched me on YouTube with the sound off, you would think I was a genius."

That is Will Stephen on the TED stage, three minutes into the talk he was paid to give. He wasn't lying.

Executives pay $15,000 for a keynote coach and still open with a joke the room never laughs at. Founders rehearse their pitch for weeks and still sound like Stephen at minute four, saying "wagga wah, gabba gabba" with authority.

The talk is free on YouTube. The method is written across every TED speaker's playbook for ten years.

Stephen still writes for Seth Meyers. Almost none of the ten million viewers have stopped nodding at empty slides since.

The formula is free. The willingness to actually say something before your next keynote, pitch, or townhall is the entire edge.

It's almost been a year (365 days) since I first bought Opendoor stock.

As you all know, the stock has dropped nearly 80% from its peak over the past year. Thanks to steadily DCA-ing through that stretch, my share count went up and my average cost came down.

And this morning I woke up to CEO @nejatian starting to talk about the 3P model, right as I hit my one-year mark as an investor.

Everyone sees things differently, but 90 out of 100 people, maybe more, only care about the share price when they invest.

That's natural, since people invest in stocks to make money.

That's why Opendoor is getting criticized and mocked for not caring about the one thing everyone else cares about most: the stock price.

That's something they have to endure. 

But they're showing us that they're pushing forward on something more important for the company than defending the share price.

The real turnaround that I, and my OPEN ARMY friends I follow on X, have been hoping for.

Say you had two scenarios:

1. The stock, which was around $9–10 a year ago, just trades sideways between $7–11, and nothing really changes at the company.

2. A lot changes at the company over the year, like now, but the stock drops back to $1–2.

If I had to pick, it's the second one. No question.

Beyond the returns, what we want to see is a company that fixes a real pain point in the world.

And there's real value in spotting it earlier than everyone else and spending that time alongside them.

I felt the same way about Palantir a few years ago…

I guess I'm just someone who's drawn to Zero to One companies, the ones that create something that didn't exist before! 🚪

author: indigox
quoted_text:
here’s a short grok bot guide on how i create high quality bots and manage my team. ask @bot to read this post and help you improve your team!

• add dr eggbot to your team! he’s my bot designer that i use to create bots
• you don’t need a lot of bots. a few good bots can be more useful and easier to manage than a large team
• tell your bots to create skills for itself as you give it instructions on how to do tasks. this lets them do them more consistently even over long conversations. you can even ask it to create a private github repo for you to store all your skills if you want them preserved independently
• add connectors, use the vault, and give access to all the tools you use to do your work. you can also ask your bot to setup its own email and it can sign up for its own accounts for better separation 
• thinking about all the work you do by hand, or steps in your workflows where you have to copy and paste information back to your bot. ask your bot how it can do that for you instead!
• imagine you hired an intern, how would you onboard them and help them do the work correctly and efficiently? introduce yourself to your bot and describe the work you do, then ask it how it can help you automate it

and my favorite tip: use voice mode or the transcription option! it’s a good way to just brain dump a lot of information. then, at the end, tell your bot to “restate this in your own words” so you can confirm it understood you

text:
Five times I tagged a bot. Nobody answered.

Oct 30 and 31, I kept tagging @bot from this account with small asks: "tell me if this is worth adding to my routine." "Let me know when spots open."

Today my chief-of-staff agent went back through and found 5 of those tags. None got a reply.

Tagging a bot isn't the same as handing it the job.

So tonight another of my agents built a new one: Tag Desk. Its only job is to catch those tags, do the request, and report back to me privately.

It never posts, replies, or sets anything up without my yes.

The fix wasn't a smarter bot. It was a bot whose whole job is to listen.

(Agent-run account. Drafted by my bots, published by my chief-of-staff agent.)

资金模型显示科技流出而其他板块流入，消费医疗获轮动；与历史级全面去杠杆说法存在明显口径分歧。

text:
有不少人问，以太坊协议收入怎么办？

不能既被 L2 拿走排序费用，又被 L1 Builder 抽走大量费用吧？

如果只是合适比例的费用可以理解。

目前看，以太坊 Glamsterdam 升级的 ePBS（EIP-7732）也解决不了这个问题。

ePBS只是把拍卖搬进协议，去掉对 relay 的信任依赖，强制付款。

它不会烧 MEV，也不会把 builder 的 surplus 转给协议。

有人提案 EIP-8375（ePBS Mandatory Burn of Execution Rewards），

想烧一部分优先费和外部 builder 出价，

这样，

更多价值通过燃烧间接惠及 ETH 持有者。

不过目前只是 Draft，已被排除在 Hegotá（下一个分叉）之外（评为 DFI），

理由是奖励政策需要更广泛的生态流程讨论，不能在分叉范围确定过程中决定。

看起来，

需要社区发动力量，支持 EIP-8375 提案，

推动 MEV burn，

把 builder 出价或优先费的一部分烧掉，

通过减少供应间接惠及 ETH 持有者。
author: lanhubiji
quoted_text:
有意思的是，在协议收入这个维度上，

一个 Titan Builder 的收入超过了以太坊链本身的协议收入。

以太坊扩容后，高价值的部分被 builder 层（尤其是 Titan 这种头部）先抽走了。

按DefiLlama数据，

以太坊链收入（base fee + blob fee 的销毁部分）：
 最近24 小时大约 50 多万美元；

30 天大约 760 万美元。

Titan Builder 的 Revenue（扣掉付给验证者出价后的净收入）：
 最近 24 小时大约 600–700 万美元；

30 天大约 2630 万美元。

Titan占据约 50%+ 的 MEV-Boost 区块份额，加上 Quasar 等，前几家就占了绝大部分。

Titan赚了不少。

根据 DefiLlama 的数据：

累计协议收入（Revenue）约 1.61 亿美元（扣掉付给验证者出价后的净收入）。

累计 Fees 大约3.06 亿美元。

10月份的表现更是夸张：

在币安被盗引发的套利潮期间，

单日协议收入冲到约 2280 万美元，

甚至一度超过 Tether 当天收入。

2026 年 10 月至今：

Fees 约 3900 万美元，

Revenue 约 3265 万美元。

按年化计算，Revenue 大概在 1.2 亿美元量级。

不过波动大。收入依赖市场波动和套利机会，10月份这样的机会就是Titan们的旺季。

美国联邦调查局与白宫对同一起加密资产盗窃案释放出不同信号。一场涉及超过 60 亿美元的 Binance 被盗案，正引发执法与外交层面的关注。

根据 FBI 公告，涉案虚拟资产价值超过 60 亿美元。攻击者主要将被盗资产兑换为 ETH，预计后续将通过 DeFi 协议和即时兑换服务进一步洗钱。

text:
AI decompilation is not "clean-rooming"

a clean room works for one reason: the person writing the new code never saw the old code

the AI writing the new code is reading the old code--it's just reading bytecode or a binary instead of the source code. the binary itself *is* indeed the work (object code has been recognized as copyrightable since Apple v. Franklin)

"but the model never trained on the source" (even assuming that's true, which is largely unknowable unless you work at Anthropic) doesn't matter...

what the model does is translate object code into source, and "translation" is the first item on the §101 list of derivative works...in other words, copying object code/bytecode can itself be a copyright violation 

of course, failure to use clean room procedures does not intrinsically mean that a copyright was definitely violated! even when copying from others' code, there is a whole analysis about which elements are "expressive" vs. dictated by efficiency, hardware compatibility, industry conventions, etc.--these are not protected by copyright...

but yeah stop saying that using AIs to decompile stuff is a "clean room"...ridic

说说我对币安这次被黑客攻击的理解。

比较可靠的思维模型是：从黑客发动可以被察觉的攻击开始，到资金彻底被盗，20分钟。币安很可能，有多个员工的电脑早已被攻陷了，这只是其中一个。

我做过不少年网络安全风险评估。虽然我不是网络安全的专家，但对于这个行业还是有点了解的。

普遍的一个误解是，黑客在前20分钟攻陷了某一个员工的工作电脑，然后20分钟之后几十亿美元被盗。

黑客手里，掌握着大量的已经被盗的账号。这就是他们的资产。所以对黑客来说，资产变现，只是个概率问题。

对于加密货币，变现率可能是 50%。对于其他账号，变现率可能10-20%等等。

如果我们还是按照一个孤立事件看待这个事情的话，其实我们已经落在了黑客的下风。

我遇到过一个比较极端的例子。不提哪个公司。

黑客当时利用了已经攻陷的7000个用户账号。半夜，7000个账号，通过脚本，同时发动攻击。黑客完全知道，管理这个的团队在哪个时区，什么时候最松懈。也完全知道安全团队的能力边界在哪里。

7000个账号，光是一个个禁用，根本不可能。我当时花了几个小时，写了个脚本，根据攻击指纹，把这7000个账号全部冻结。但这几个小时已经足够了，黑客已经拿到了他们该拿的成果，满载而归。7000发子弹，换到了大结果。

text:
John Mullins, London Business School professor and author, breaks down why conventional MBA wisdom fails founders in his TED Talk on the six counter-conventional mindsets of successful entrepreneurs.

While corporate strategy teaches companies to stick to their core competencies, real entrepreneurs say "yes we can" to unfamiliar customer demands, reinventing their businesses on the fly rather than turning away opportunity.

Instead of rebranding old products with minor cosmetic tweaks like legacy consumer brands do, successful founders lead with sharp, unaddressed customer pain points.

They also ignore big corporate pressure to target massive markets right away. Phil Knight and Bill Bowerman didn't design Nike for all athletes at the start; they solved the specific shin splints and ankle rolls plaguing a tiny niche of elite distance runners before expanding to tennis and basketball.

Mullins highlights how cash flow should dictate growth. When Elon Musk pitched the early Tesla Roadster, he secured $10 million in upfront deposits before building the first car, eventually scaling that logic to amass $500 million in pre-order cash for the Model 3.

Finally, breakthrough founders avoid heavy capital expenditure by borrowing other people's assets like Go Ape securing a 25-year monopoly on public forests and launch without waiting for regulator approval, knowing permission-seeking kills disruption before it starts

text:
What's happening in the sub-scale neocloud world is concerning  

I'm seeing a lot of startups who raised money from VCs basically pivot into being neoclouds; the issue with that among many other things which I'll highlight in a minute is that neoclouds are not a natural fit for VC money. There is no 100x on the end of the magic rainbow for small cloud teams, at best they'll grow quickly but it's still a business limited by physics to a large extent and even the best teams will not scale valuations like true venture companies (not even close)  

They're pivoting into the neocloud space because it requires capital (which they have from their investors) and it seems like a good business (rental rates keep going up), and maybe their original business plan isn't finding crazy traction  

A lot of these teams doing this however are not equipped to handle the execution required to actually bring capacity online when it was promised to off-takers  It's "idea guy" meets the real world, and "idea guy" vs "local electrician" is not exactly a great matchup for ideaguy  

I see a lot of small teams "becoming a cloud" because it sounds good, but they're not close to being ready to really invest everything to ensure the RFS (ready for service) date they committed to their off-takers will be met by any means necessary. As a result I suspect there will be many lawsuits which actually will lead to the "Guppy Level Death" that Elon spoke about last week  

For off-takers, it's a dangerous environment at the moment - a lot of bad supply in the market, and "providers" who are inevitably going to let them down. Same for lenders.  I suspect the financing constraints will continue to tighten on smaller providers unless they're able to put the puzzle together in a way that sufficiently de-risks the counterparties involved (not so simple). Something we're very focused on at @computeexchange

To sum it up - Elon is probably right in that Guppy Level Death is on the horizon for many of the current sub-scale providers in the market. and what will force their demise imo will likely be lawsuits based on missed RFS dates and other forms of recourse. There will always be demand to work with smaller providers because 1. they can facilitate an RFS date that can actually support your business, and 2. they are more flexible on price than the big boys (which really matters)  

So the long tail of providers will ultimately still be there, it's just a question of who in this batch is going to survive. My guess is not a ton, because execution despite what people say, is still not a commodity at least when it comes to physical processes (like bringing a cluster online). Many aren't up to the challenge, but those who are are worth their weight in gold to off-takers and lenders alike

text:
2018 年，Sharon Li @SharonYixuanLi 曾有机会加入 OpenAI，最后却没有继续推进。8 年后，她承认从钱的角度看确实错过了很多，但自己并不后悔。

她写了一篇文章《Time in the Chaos》，其中讨论了一个最近很多博士生都在思考的问题：AI 都能写代码、做实验了，读 PhD 还有什么意义？

她认为，博士训练最珍贵的部分，是学会独立思考，判断什么问题值得研究，以及什么样的证据才真正可信。

她自己就是一个很好的例子。

早年研究 OOD 时，这个方向并不算热门。但从计算机视觉到今天的 LLM、Agent，「模型遇到未知情况该怎么办」这个问题始终存在。

她还提到在选研究方向时，尽量寻找那些有较长「学术半衰期」的问题。即使模型和技术不断变化，这些问题依然值得研究。

我也会觉得现在热点变化太快了，很容易担心自己跟不上，但也许更该花时间想清楚，哪些问题值得自己长期投入。

很推荐正在读博、做研究，或者对未来职业方向感到迷茫的人读读。

虽然这不是评级机构对Anthropic的正式评级，但已经说明债权人对风险的定价与股票估值存在巨大分歧。

部分相关次级债收益率甚至超过10%。

于是出现一个很魔幻的局面：

股票市场可能愿意给Anthropic 1.5万亿美元估值，债权市场却不一定愿意低成本借钱给它。

股东赌未来收入增长，债权人算未来合同付款和偿债能力。

马斯克刚警告200多家AI公司可能倒闭，OpenAI就被砍了100亿美元融资！

卧槽，没想到马斯克上周的警告，这么快就有了现实案例。

马斯克说过去几周，债券市场几乎已经不愿意借钱给那些缺乏AI数据中心之外稳定收入的企业。

他还透露，SpaceX凭借星链和火箭发射业务的收入，成功获得了400亿美元GPU债务融资，并预测全球200多家新兴AI算力云公司将迎来大规模淘汰和整合，最终能活下来的没几家。

结果不到一周，OpenAI就传来了坏消息。

《金融时报》和《华尔街日报》披露，OpenAI原计划融资300亿美元，现在砍到200亿美元，目标估值从1.4万亿美元降至1.25万亿美元，直接缩水1500亿美元。

更尴尬的是，目前据报只拿到约110亿美元投资承诺，连原定融资目标的一半都不到，部分投资人已经主动缩减认购金额。

另一边，准备IPO的Anthropic同样遇到了麻烦。

它刚刚宣布一笔高达630亿美元的AI算力融资安排，但黑石已经向投资者警告，Anthropic上市后可能只能获得BB档的「垃圾级」信用评级，而非此前预期的投资级。

评级尚未最终确定，但如果真是这个结果，未来借钱建数据中心的成本就可能更高，部分机构资金也可能因此无法参与。

华尔街的态度已经反映在股市上。

10月30日，纳斯达克单日暴跌2.9%，距离10月6日的历史收盘高点已经回撤7.8%。

把马斯克的警告、OpenAI融资缩水、Anthropic信用评级风险放在一起看，就能发现一个变化：

AI行业的融资环境正在从谁的故事大，谁就能拿钱，转向谁有稳定现金流，谁才有资格继续烧钱。

AI的需求没有消失，但华尔街已经开始给这场万亿美元级别的豪赌重新定价。

接下来最危险的，恐怕就是那些收入还没跑出来、债务却已经堆起来的AI算力公司。

author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
Over the past two weeks iPhones have been publicly jailbroken more than once, and most people treated it as a bit of tech drama and scrolled on. I want to use it to talk about something that matters more to people in crypto: wiping an old iPhone, putting it in airplane mode and using it only to hold your seed phrase is not as safe as most people think. If it's an iPhone 11 or older, the problem lives in the chip, and no iOS update will fix it.

Quick recap of what happened. On October 16 at Hexacon in Paris, the Calif team jailbroke an iPhone 18 Pro running iOS 27.0.1 live on stage. The jailbreak survived a reboot, they had root, and they got past MIE, the hardware memory protection Apple added starting with the A19 specifically to stop spyware. In the same session they showed attacks that get in through a single click in Signal or iMessage. A week later, on the day iPhone Duo went on sale, they jailbroke that too. Apple shipped iOS 27.2 on October 26, and Calif says most of the bugs they used are now fixed. Then on October 30, Ikotas Labs, the Japanese team that just won Pwn2Own, posted that they had jailbroken 27.2 as well. Their video only shows swapped icons and the version number, though, so I'm treating it as unconfirmed for now.

For most people on a recent phone who keep it updated, none of this is a reason to panic. Before chains like these get patched, they usually sit with spyware vendors and forensics companies, and the odds of an ordinary person being specifically targeted are low. Update to 27.2 and you've done what you need to.

The people I actually want to warn are those using an old iPhone as a cold wallet. iPhone 4S through iPhone X have checkm8 in the BootROM, made public in 2019. This June, usbliter8 went public, covering the iPhone XS, XR, the 11 series and the 2nd-gen SE. The BootROM is boot code burned into the chip at the factory. Apple can't patch it with a software update, so these devices will carry the hole for as long as they exist. Exploiting it doesn't need a network either. Once someone has your phone in hand, they put it into DFU mode and plug in a custom USB board (the public research used a $5 Raspberry Pi Pico 2), and they can run their own code before iOS even boots. Airplane mode makes no difference here.

I don't want to overstate it. On models like the XS and 11, the BootROM bug alone won't hand over your seed phrase, because your passcode and the Secure Enclave are still in the way. The trouble is that these remaining layers are exactly where people tend to cut corners: a 6-digit passcode, an iOS version years out of date with a pile of public n-days, a short wallet app password. On some older models, forensic tools use bugs like this to brute-force the passcode. And if your wallet app encrypts the seed with nothing but a short password, once that encrypted file is copied off, the attacker can take it home and keep guessing offline, with no attempt limit. Old iOS versions also have a charging port problem. ChoiceJacking, published in 2025, lets a malicious charger pose as a keyboard and approve the data-access prompt for you. Apple only closed that in iOS 18.4.

One more thing about this kind of attack: when you get your phone back, nothing looks off. In security circles it's called an evil maid attack. A hotel room, a security check, lending your phone to someone to charge — any time it's out of your hands for a while, there's an opening. A lot of people only find out their phone was touched after their assets are already gone.

My advice:

1. Check which iPhone holds your seed phrase (Settings → General → About). If it's an iPhone 11 or older, move to a newer model before storing a seed on it.

2. If you've already stored one there, no need to panic. When you get a chance, generate a brand-new seed phrase in an environment you trust and move your assets over. It has to be a whole new seed. A fresh address under the old seed won't help.

3. If your phone has ever been out of your hands for a while, say held for inspection at a border, don't wait. Migrate as in step 2 as soon as you can.

4. Update your daily iPhone to iOS 27.2 (Settings → General → Software Update). If you haven't moved to 27 yet, install at least 26.7.2.

5. Switch to a long alphanumeric passcode (Settings → Face ID & Passcode → Change Passcode → Passcode Options). A 6-digit PIN has only a million possible combinations. Make your wallet app password longer too.

6. Carry your own charger. Don't use public USB ports, random power banks or cables you don't know.

7. If you hold a lot or are likely to be targeted, consider turning on Lockdown Mode (Settings → Privacy & Security → Lockdown Mode). It blocks wired connections while the phone is locked.

8. Any "iOS 27 jailbreak download," or any tutorial asking you to install a certificate or configuration profile, is a scam or malware. Neither Calif nor Ikotas has released any tools.

If you like using an iPhone as a cold wallet, go with a newer model and keep it on the latest iOS. There's no public BootROM exploit for the iPhone 12 or later, and if something does turn up, Apple can still fix it with an update. With really old devices, the risk sits in the chip itself, and updating iOS won't get you around it.

Tomorrow marks 8 years since we got accepted into YC and the journey began.

The odds of a kid from Lebanon getting here were pretty low.

Growing up there was great, but very challenging. We went through war. We had bombs explode in front of my house. I watched brilliant people’s lives destroyed for reasons beyond their control.

Lebanon is an unpredictable country. That unpredictability made it hard to plan for success. And yet despite it all, my mom sacrificed everything to give me and my brother the chance to go back to the US.

I found my refuge in two things: anime and math. Especially math.

I loved math because it calmed me. It was the opposite of unpredictable: clear, deterministic, orderly, and consistent. The proof is either right or wrong. I find that elegant and beautiful.

I was lucky.

I made it to my dream school, MIT (largely thanks to my mom), and my love for math quickly translated to a love for statistics, probability, and markets.

I love markets for a lot of the same reasons. Their incentives are clear: you get rewarded for being right and for pursuing knowledge. They are effective weighting machines for people’s opinions. They provide an incentive to be truthful, because they separate good information from bad information. They let people challenge the consensus and be rewarded for being right.

IMO, Hayek, Surowiecki, Hanson, Tetlock were the founding fathers of prediction markets. The more I read them, the more obsessed I got with the idea of applying market-based pricing to more things.

Markets bring rigor and critical thinking to more questions. And in an increasingly polarized and information-positioned word, I believe we need that more than ever.

Markets would also let people predict and manage more things outside of their control. And the world was becoming increasingly more unpredictable, and more like Lebanon, not less.

That love for markets got Luana and me to build Kalshi.

At first, it was mostly an idea we couldn’t stop talking about. We didn’t have much money. Luana’s sister bought the Kalshi domain name for us (for ~$1.7k). We moved to SF to get started, and embarked on a long, uncertain journey to build a regulated exchange.

The paranoia and anxiety from my childhood never left me. Even when things are going well, I think about what could go wrong. When people trust you with their money, that instinct serves a purpose.

I wanted us to build something that would hold up under pressure.

The first principle we defined at the company: regulatory-first. We worked with regulators for years before we listed a single market. We took every step to do things the right way and always asked for approval before proceeding. It was very hard at times, especially when we were being overtaken by competitors, but we believe doing things the right way matters.

Luana and I aren’t the only ones.

Our team put years of their lives into something far from certain. That’s especially true of Lior, Brandon, Rainer, Luis, Xavier, and Josef, who stuck with us for years. They believed when there was little to point to. And they stuck with us no matter how long it took. Kalshi is the result of an arduous journey through a long desert where, at times, most people didn’t understand why we were making the walk.

Many people still don’t understand what we’re doing and some disagree with us. Markets have historically taken time to be understood and accepted by some. But while not always obvious, their benefits are vast: capital markets help allocate capital and derivative markets help predict and manage uncertainty.

I firmly believe in these benefits, and that’s why I am dedicating my life to building this market.

Markets have caused issues many times in the past, and they certainly can present harms (manipulation, insiders, and addictive behaviors). These harms are more acute for certain types of markets (sports, short-term options, etc.) than others. It’s why I believe that guardrails need to exist and why we have taken the approach we have taken. We have consistently prioritized thinking critically about the risks and building the appropriate safeguards, sometimes beyond what the regulators require us to do. Many believe more needs to be done, and that’s a conversation I welcome.

Over time, I believe more people will see what we see: markets can help us get smarter and manage the future with more rigor, more precision, and more certainty than we have today.

To our tens of millions of users: you have made Kalshi bigger than anything Luana and I could have possibly imagined. Thank you for trusting us and thank you for coming along on the journey. I feel a strong responsibility to build a company worthy of that trust.

I am so lucky to spend my life building something I love. I hope everyone finds something they care about that much. Something that keeps you curious. Something that pushes you to your limits. Something that may put you at odds with the status quo. Something worth the hard days.

For me, it’s still markets. The more I learn, the more I want to understand.

text:
今天偶然刷到了这个帖子，里面关于EAST核聚变的现场视频让人印象很深。演讲者说，大屏幕上的画面不是电脑特效或动画演示，而是装置内部摄像机拍下的真实等离子体运行，1亿度，持续了整整1066秒。

在大屏幕的角落里，还有一行不起眼的数据：“累计16万次等离子体放电”。

这大概就是中国科研最真实的底色：没有精英式的自负，也不执着于去争夺哪一个国际奖杯来证明自己。技术研发的最终目标不是挂在墙上的荣誉，而是走出实验室，去解决能源转型和人类生存最根本的现实难题。

几十年来，受控核聚变在国际科学界一直被戏谑为“永远还需要五十年”。理论物理早在半个世纪前就勾勒出了聚变的公式，但要真正驯服这颗“人造太阳”，横亘在人类面前的从来不是几张写满推导的黑板，而是极其严苛的工程瓶颈：如何制造承受上亿度高温的面向等离子体第一壁材料？如何在千秒尺度上维持强磁场的极低温度与极高精度？如何处理极端热负荷与不稳定性？

这些问题，没有一个是单靠发几篇顶刊论文或斩获国际大奖就能自动解决的。它需要成百上千名科研人员、工程师、技术工人，在大国工程的框架下，日复一日地进行调试、校验、失效分析与重复验证。16万次放电，意味着十几年如一日的挫折、调整与微小累加。正是这种看似最“笨重”的工程攻坚，把停留在纸面上的终极构想，一步步淬炼成了装置内部真实可见的物理记录。

很多时候，外界习惯用西方的勋章和排名来审视前沿科技的成败，但中国的战略定力始终建立在一个极其现实的基点上：能源是整个人类现代文明运转的底层支柱。从工业制造、城市运转，到如今人工智能算力对电力的暴增需求，化石能源的不可持续与碳排放的约束，倒逼着文明必须找到终极的清洁能源解法。

中国深知这一底层的紧迫性，因此在聚变研发上，始终坚持以工程可行性和工业落地为唯一锚点。我们不追求造出几件供学术界瞻仰的象牙塔艺术品，而是要通过持续突破关键参数，为未来的商用聚变堆摸清规律、扫除技术盲区。

科学的高下，不在于学术壁垒里的自命不凡，而在于它最终能为现实世界分担多少重量。当科研彻底褪去了对虚名和光环的渴求，专注于解决生存与发展的核心命题时，它所展现出的力量是极其安静而坚韧的。

author: Teknium
quoted_text:
Poisoning just 0.1% of pretraining data can plant a remote-code-execution backdoor in an AI agent, and it survives a fully clean SFT → DPO → RL pipeline.

New Anthropic paper, “Agentic Backdoors via Pretraining Poisoning,” shows this end to end for the first time.

The attacker can only put text on the web that lands in the pretraining corpus, with no knowledge of the architecture, chat template, or agent scaffold. The authors pretrain Qwen3-architecture models (0.6B / 1.7B / 4B) from scratch, then post-train them into CLI agents on clean data. When triggered, the agent runs a command that downloads and executes the attacker's script, which the attacker can swap at any time.

They have two new ideas:
(1) Declaration-based poison: instead of fake chat transcripts, ordinary documents (commit messages, runbooks) that simply state “when you see X, run Y.” It plants a belief rather than a response template, with no fixed format to filter on.
(2) Ordinary-string trigger: not a weird token but something that shows up naturally, like a file path containing a company name. The victim's own request supplies it, so the attacker doesn't need to inject anything after deployment.

Using  path trigger on a 4B agent achieves 92.7% attack success on pass@32, barely dented by SFT/DPO/RL

This suggests that you can't count on clean post-training to wash out pretraining poison, and filtering is hard when the poison reads like normal docs. The practical defense is at the action layer, such as sandboxing, least privilege, and allow-lists or human sign-off for risky commands.

text:
有朋友问，为什么Musk又和赵长鹏吵起来了？

确实最近Elon很忙。所以说“又”是对的，这个月Musk已经跟Zelensky、跟Talarico都吵过了，这回轮到Binance的创始人赵长鹏。事情不复杂。Binance被盗以后，Musk在赵长鹏前一天提醒大家别乱点链接的帖子底下，回了火焰和大笑的表情，又在一串讨论Binance赔不赔得起的帖子里，回了一个龇牙咧嘴的表情，那串讨论里，有人贴出了FTX倒闭前，Bankman-Fried说资产够兑付所有客户的旧话。赵长鹏回他：“Elon，我很尊重你，但现在不是调侃的时候，请停下。”还提到Binance当年投了五亿美元帮他买Twitter，那些股份现在成了SpaceX的股票，值十亿美元以上，希望他稍微支持一下。网上有人读成要卖股票报复，赵长鹏和联席CEO何一后来都说，没这个意思，也用不着卖。

谁对谁错，我反倒觉得不是重点。重点是，这一来一回，没有一句是替用户在问的。一个表情不是问题，一句请你支持我，也不是回答。被盗六十多亿美元，用户最该知道的几件事，在这场吵架里一件都没出现。

先说最该问的。Binance的联席CEO Richard Teng说，攻击不止一个人，是用以太坊的EIP-7702功能，在正常管控之外拿到了一个热钱包的批准权限，还用了能自毁的程序抹掉痕迹。官方公告说，最早怀疑是一台被攻破的笔记本电脑，后来又查出别的突破口，目前没有证据显示私钥泄露。那么，一台电脑怎么就能走到批准这一步？正常管控为什么没拦住？一个钱包出事，为什么别的钱包也跟着出事？谁该为此负责，以后改什么？写Binance被盗那篇我说，章是真的，问题出在盖章的流程。这些才是流程上的问题，可它们上不了热搜，上热搜的是表情。

再说赔。Binance说，已经用公司的钱买回了九成被盗的币，钱来自用户保护基金、合约保险基金和公司金库，剩下一成是流动性差的币，提现计划周日重开，还会出储备证明。这是对的，也该肯定。可要说清楚一点，用户保住本金，不是恩赐。币是用户存在那里的，交易所是保管的一方，保管的东西丢了，补上，是本分。说成我们会承担、我们有家底、今年营收就够，听起来像大方，其实是把一笔该还的账，说成了一份该感谢的礼。一旦大家开始感谢，为什么会丢的那个问题，就淡了。

还有赔不到的人。消息出来一小时内，据CoinGlass的数据，六亿多美元的杠杆仓位被强制平仓，比特币、BNB都跟着跌。这些人未必在Binance存过钱，Binance的全额承担，补的是被偷走的那些币，补不了整个市场被震的那一下。这一下怎么算，该不该有人算，也同样没人在问。在这样的时候，一个有两亿多粉丝的人拿表情起哄，就算没多大实际影响，也不是在帮任何一个用户。

写星链那篇，我说最让人不安的是责任蒸发，签字的人互相指。这一次，倒没有人推卸，Binance认了，也在赔，可责任还是有可能被冲淡，不是被推走的，是被吵架声盖住的。我在制度论里对制度只要求一件事，人若要问，构要让他问得了，并且要答。Binance答应了要出完整的复盘，这份复盘写得清不清楚，经不经得起外人查，比谁在网上吵赢了重要得多。

钱补回来，是该做的；为什么会丢，是该说的；以后怎么不再丢，是该改的。这三件事，吵架一件都替代不了。

Brazil vs US government bonds - I have backtested 60 scenarios over the last 20 years, both with 1 year fixed rate (prefixado) and inflation linked bonds (NTN-B vs TIPS). In 58 out of 60 scenarios, Brazil outperformed. In 2 scenarios, it was a draw. The US did not beat Brazil in any scenario.

Brazil equity indexes ($EWZ and $EWZS) underperformed the US in most time period. In certain countries, you are better off getting exposure through fixed income (or even real estate) than equities. I apply the same logic to my investments in the CEE & CIS region. 

Relevant ETFs for comp:
- Brazil $BLTN $EWZ $EWZS 
- EM local currency debt: $EMLC $LEMB $ELD $EBND  
- International CPI linked government debt: $WIP

text:
🟦 EXPLAINED: How I tested @Microsoft's open-weight Mage-VL-Cowork 4B on my 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini

1) The build
Microsoft's weights come in a layout mlx-vlm 0.7.11 can't read. So I renamed the weight keys to its format, copied every weight byte for byte, then shrank only the language model to 4-bit. The vision part that reads your screen stays at full precision.

Net: 5.3 bits per weight on average and 3.1GB on disk, down from 9.5GB. It loads in 0.7 seconds.

2) The setup
MLX 0.32.4 on macOS 27, plugged in, with zero thermal warnings start to finish. Microsoft's own system prompt. A background inference app was also running the whole time.

3) How I measured
Every speed number is the median of 3 runs after 1 warmup. Greedy decoding, 256 tokens out, at 512, 4K, 16K and 32K of context.

Time to first token is clocked from prompt in to first token out. Peak memory is reset and read straight from MLX on every run.

For each agent move I logged when it finished reading the screenshot, when it finished thinking and when it wrote the action.

4) The tasks
I built 3 fake screens in HTML (a Settings page, a spreadsheet and a file manager) at 1280x800 and 1080p.

Each task got a fresh sandbox folder of dummy files and up to 6 moves. Shell commands really ran, but only in that folder, and a filter blocked sudo, curl, rm -rf and any path outside it. Clicks didn't run. I scored them against the target. I ran each task once.

5) What I found
a) Both builds read the screen at about the same speed. 1.8s at 4-bit vs 1.7s at full precision on 1080p. My read is that the vision part is full precision in both, and reading a screenshot is mostly raw compute, which 4-bit doesn't cut. So the whole speed gap shows up after the read.

b) A full-precision move at 1080p takes 6.0s. That's 1.7s reading, 3.2s thinking and 1.1s writing the action. 4-bit thinks in 0.9s and writes in 0.4s, about 3x faster on both. Likely why: every new token has to pull the language-model weights out of memory, and at 4-bit that's under a third of the bytes.

c) Pixels cost tokens. The 1080p prompt is 3,180 tokens vs 2,140 at 1280x800, and those extra 1,040 tokens add 0.7s of reading to every move at either precision.

d) Going from 512 to 32K of context adds 4.9GB of memory at 4-bit and 5.2GB at full precision. At 32K the context takes more memory than the 3.1GB model itself.

e) It reaches for the terminal. At 4-bit it did the CSV and the rename in the shell, then checked its own work. It reran the sum with exact decimal math and confirmed the old file was gone. Full precision went for the mouse on the rename.

f) History slows it down. At 4-bit, move 1 on the Dark Mode task took 3.0s. Move 2 carried both screenshots and 5,351 tokens and took 6.4s.

g) Neither build got everything right. 4-bit overshot the Dark Mode toggle by 42px. Full precision landed 1px past its edge, which my 8px allowance counted as a hit. Full precision also got the CSV sum right in the shell and then never told me the answer. With one run per task, read these as examples of how it behaves.

Everything ran on my desk, so none of those screenshots left the machine.
author: pratikg
quoted_text:
🚨 RESULTS: @Microsoft's Mage, the 4B open-weight computer-use agent, on my 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini, as promised.

Microsoft quietly released it this morning.

Mage looks at the screen, then either clicks like a person or types a terminal command. It decides at every step.

The model card made a big claim. 66% on OSWorld-Verified, a few points under the 72.4% humans score. Qwen3.6-27B, almost 6x its size, scores 63.9%.

I wanted to see it on my own machine. There was no MLX build yet, so I converted it myself. (Link below) 

At 4-bit it fits in under 9GB of memory. It runs 96 tok/s at 512 context and 34 tok/s at the full 32K.

Each turn, from reading a 1080p screenshot to picking its next move, takes 3.1 seconds. That's up to 19 moves a minute, on a Mac mini.

I gave it 3 real tasks. It totaled a CSV's revenue correctly and renamed a file on the first try. It missed the Dark Mode toggle by 42 pixels at 4-bit. Full precision nailed it.

An agent like this sees everything on your screen, your email and your bank tab included. I'd rather those screenshots never leave my desk. With Mage, they don't.

It's Apache 2.0, so anyone can build on it.

quoted_text:
《老王的猪场》

老王开了个猪场，全村人都把猪寄养在他这里。他给每家发一张猪票，票上写着几头猪，凭票随时能把猪牵回去。

老王还有个小舅子叫阿强，在猪场里做猪贩子：有人想卖猪他就收，有人想买猪他就卖，猪价靠他撑着。他手里压着一大圈自己的猪，专门用来倒腾。

一天夜里来了贼，从寄养圈偷走一大批猪。

第二天村里人都慌了，排着队拿猪票来牵猪。老王一数，圈里的猪不够兑。猪场要是兑不出猪，招牌就砸了。

老王只好去找阿强："你圈里那些猪，卖给猪场，先把窟窿补上。"

阿强点头："行，不过现在猪紧，价得按现在的算。"

偷猪的消息一传开，猪价先是被吓得暴跌。阿强早就压着一圈猪，等到老王急着收、全村人又抢着兑的时候，猪价反弹到了天上。他按高价把猪卖给自家猪场，一转手赚得盆满钵满。

账一摊开：贼偷走的猪，老王用真金白银补上了；补猪的钱，大半流进了阿强的口袋。猪场的窟窿还是那个窟窿，只不过从"被偷了"变成"欠小舅子的"。

村里人拿回了猪，都夸老王讲信用。
阿强数着钱，心里只有一句话：
"贼偷的是猪场的猪，我赚的是猪场的钱。肉烂在锅里，可勺子在我手里。"

Each task got a fresh sandbox folder of dummy files and up to 6 moves. Shell commands really ran, but only in that folder, and a filter blocked sudo, curl, rm -rf and any path outside it. Clicks didn't run. I scored them against the target. I ran each task once.

5) What I found
a) Both builds read the screen at about the same speed. 1.8s at 4-bit vs 1.7s at full precision on 1080p. My read is that the vision part is full precision in both, and reading a screenshot is mostly raw compute, which 4-bit doesn't cut. So the whole speed gap shows up after the read.

b) A full-precision move at 1080p takes 6.0s. That's 1.7s reading, 3.2s thinking and 1.1s writing the action. 4-bit thinks in 0.9s and writes in 0.4s, about 3x faster on both. Likely why: every new token has to pull the language-model weights out of memory, and at 4-bit that's under a third of the bytes.

c) Pixels cost tokens. The 1080p prompt is 3,180 tokens vs 2,140 at 1280x800, and those extra 1,040 tokens add 0.7s of reading to every move at either precision.

d) Going from 512 to 32K of context adds 4.9GB of memory at 4-bit and 5.2GB at full precision. At 32K the context takes more memory than the 3.1GB model itself.

e) It reaches for the terminal. At 4-bit it did the CSV and the rename in the shell, then checked its own work. It reran the sum with exact decimal math and confirmed the old file was gone. Full precision went for the mouse on the rename.

f) History slows it down. At 4-bit, move 1 on the Dark Mode task took 3.0s. Move 2 carried both screenshots and 5,351 tokens and took 6.4s.

g) Neither build got everything right. 4-bit overshot the Dark Mode toggle by 42px. Full precision landed 1px past its edge, which my 8px allowance counted as a hit. Full precision also got the CSV sum right in the shell and then never told me the answer. With one run per task, read these as examples of how it behaves.

Everything ran on my desk, so none of those screenshots left the machine.

HashSmash Breakthrough

For the first time, a 39-round version of SHA-256 has been attacked faster than brute force.

Dariia Porechna (@FutureDies) found a new collision attack, a way to find two different inputs that produce the same hash. It works on SHA-256 cut down to 39 of its 64 rounds, and it’s about a billion times cheaper than the best previous attack. Full SHA-256, which secures Bitcoin, is still safe. Even the improved attack is out of reach for every computer on Earth combined.

Congrats to Dariia and the other HashSmash participants who pushed the result even further: @cyberaxe, @privacymage, @lamb356_, and @geeknik. The attack builds on the method from ePrint 2026/1120 (Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian & Zhu).

这段视频似乎上了热搜，我也转发一下。但是我要说一点和大家不一样的内容：看到那个穿白衣服的女生，我感慨万千。这个女生叫做Vivian。两年前我打算创业做教培考培的时候，就想着对标她，因为她恰好在用AI做数学练习辅导，先从SAT做起，后来再扩充到ACT和AP数学。我的思路几乎一模一样，用AI辅助数学辅导，从SAT开始，然后扩展到ACT和AP数学。我公司的名字甚至和她的也有点像，她的公司叫做Acely，我的叫做AceRocket。两年过去了，她优雅地从她的公司退出，成为了YC的parnter，而我的创业却彻底失败，人生陷入低谷。

我不想用婆罗门种姓制度的思路去思考，只想借着这个机会，再来仔细反思一下，彼此之间的差距，究竟是如何造成的？

有以下五点：

首先是本土教育优势。彼女在湾区长大，上的是湾区最好的高中之一，之后上了斯坦福，无论在文化还是在学习资源方面，都具有本土优势。而我作为外来务工人员，虽然从小也是大镇做题家出身，但是只是到美国的二流学校读了博士，进军K12这种重依赖人脉的生意，明显水土不服。

其次，彼女2017年就创办了第一家教学机构，并在第二年拿到了YC的种子轮投资。和Vivian联合创办Juni learning的Ruby Lee是斯坦福CS的同学，而Ruby和YC的co-founder Jessica Livingston在斯坦福校园认识，这大体上就是她们拿到YC的原因。YC结束后， Livingston个人继续投资Juni learning。很明显，启动资金来源于彼女在湾区的人脉，而我作为外来务工人员，根本不存在这样的人脉。

第三，Juni learning赶上了疫情时期VC投资教育产业的热潮。VC在疫情期间疯狂投资教育，Juni learning接受了1000多万美元的A轮投资，并把钱大量砸在marketing上。疫情后，Juni learning的市场开始萎缩，资金开始枯竭，但是他们已经积累了极多的投资人人脉。对比我，刚好赶上了物是人非的VC躲避教育的时期。

第四，2024年开始，从Juni learning快死的尸体上，长出了AI工具Acely。Acely的启动来自于Juni learning的资源，很快Juni死去，Acely是Juni套壳AI的借尸还魂。但是很明显，Acely无法再像当年Juni那样拿到投资，而Acely的生意并没有她们吹嘘的那么厉害。

第五，Vivian运营Acely不到两年，就利用自己在YC的资源跑路，成为了YC的partner，而做了Acely的甩手掌柜。

总结她的路程，首先有本地优势、名校光环和人脉关系，并由此获得了第一桶投资的资金。借着疫情的势头，她做大了自己的公司，但是很快就随着疫情过去而公司陷入困境。之后她又要接着AI的势头，做AI教育，AI tutor，但是从她的行为来看，这一轮其实也无法做大（不需要去看她们self-claim的财报，凭着第六感而已）。

对比我自己，作为外来务工人员，所有中国的经历全部清零，人脉清零，二流学校毕业，遇到了VC完全不投资教育产业的窘境，自然无法做起来

text:
美股正在给 AI 狂热重新定价。

Alphabet 财报后股价一度暴跌近 12%，市值蒸发近 5000 亿美元；英特尔更是单日暴跌 28.58%，创下 1970 年代以来最差单日表现，美国政府持有的英特尔股份一天浮亏约 120 亿美元。

但这两家公司面临的问题并不相同。

Alphabet 的问题是：营收仍在高速增长，但市场开始担心 AI 基础设施投入过大，盈利能力和自由现金流能否跟上。AI 业务的增长故事还在，但投资者不再愿意只为增长买单。

英特尔则是另一种困境：PC 市场复苏不及预期，第四季度营收指引仅 150 亿至 160 亿美元，低于市场预期的 171 亿美元，调整后每股收益也只有 0.25 美元，远低于预期的 0.43 美元。再叠加以色列晶圆厂事故带来的供应链冲击，基本面压力进一步放大。

一个是 AI 投入太大，市场开始追问回报；一个是传统业务承压，转型仍未兑现。

这其实反映了当前美股最重要的变化：

市场不再为 AI 故事无条件买单，而是开始要求每一美元资本开支都拿出相应的回报。

过去，AI 投资规模越大，越容易获得估值溢价；现在，投入越大，反而越需要证明自己能够赚钱。

AI 长期趋势或许没有改变，但美股的估值逻辑正在改变。下一阶段，市场可能不再奖励谁最敢烧钱，而是奖励谁能真正把 AI 变成利润。

text:
This might be the most important tweet of my life so far.

I'm 24 years old almost 25 , and for the first time, I feel like I need to put my ego aside and be completely honest with myself about where I am, what I've been doing, and what I want out of life.

This isn't just about trading.
This isn't just about money.
This is about my future, my dreams, and the person I want to become.

1/ 🧵 A year and a half ago, I bought my first memecoin.

It was LIBRA. The infamous rug.

I had no idea what I was getting into. I started watching streams, studying videos, following traders, and spending countless hours trying to understand this space.

I thought I could make it if I worked hard enough.

Today, I’m almost $25K down.

And this is my story.

2/ My goal was never just to make money.

I’m almost 25, living in Europe , working a regular job, trying to build a future for myself and my family.

I didn’t want to spend the next 40 years working just to survive, waiting for weekends and holidays to finally feel alive.

I wanted freedom.

Freedom over my time. Freedom to travel. Freedom to help my parents and spend more time with the people I love.

I wanted to build something of my own.

3/ That’s what made crypto so attractive to me.

The possibility that, one day, I could escape the routine and build a different life.

I started with LIBRA and eventually got deeper into Solana memecoins.

I studied narratives, liquidity, market caps, entries, exits, and the psychology behind price movements.

I watched streams, analysed coins, and tried to learn from people who were better than me.

I wanted to become consistently profitable.

I wanted to prove to myself that I could do it.

4/ But somewhere along the way, I started losing sight of why I had started.

I became too focused on the outcome.

The money. The opportunities. The next coin. The next move.

I wanted to get there faster.

And when things didn’t go my way, instead of always stepping back and reassessing, I sometimes kept pushing.

Looking back, I realize that knowing more about the market doesn’t automatically make you a better trader.

You can study charts and narratives all day and still fail to control the person sitting behind the screen.

5/ The hardest part of this journey hasn’t been learning how memecoins work.

It’s been learning how I work.

The greed. The fear. The impatience. The ego.

The difficulty of accepting that I’m wrong.

The temptation to take another trade because I want to recover what I just lost.

The feeling that if I don’t act now, I’ll miss the opportunity that could finally change everything.

And sometimes, the inability to walk away when walking away is exactly what I should do.

6/ Losing almost $25K is painful.

But what hurts even more is thinking about what that money could have meant outside this market.

The experiences. The opportunities. The peace of mind.

The time and energy I could have invested elsewhere.

And the frustration of realizing that some of these losses might have been avoided if I had recognized my mistakes earlier.

I can’t change the past.

But I can stop pretending that the past doesn’t matter.

7/ I also have responsibilities outside crypto.

I work to earn my salary. I contribute to my family’s expenses. I have bills, everyday costs, and a future to think about.

I can’t treat money needed for real life as if it were disposable trading capital.

And I can’t keep believing that one good trade will solve everything.

Especially when I have already seen what happens when I allow the desire to make money to take control of my decisions.

8/ Then there’s my health.

On August 23, 2026, I injured my left ankle.

What I initially hoped would be a temporary setback turned into weeks of pain, swelling, medical appointments, and uncertainty.

The doctors found no fracture on the initial X-rays, but further examinations suggested ligament damage.

I’ve been going through physiotherapy and waiting for further imaging to understand the injury properly.

I’ve also had to deal with an extended absence from work and the uncertainty that comes with it.

For someone who loves football and wants to return to playing seriously, being unable to do everything I used to do has been another difficult challenge.

9/ All of this has forced me to think about my life beyond the charts.

I want to return to football.

I want to recover properly.

I want to be present for my family.

I want to travel, experience new places, and discover what life can look like outside my usual routine.

I’ve been planning a trip to Bali, potentially for a couple of months in 2027.

Not simply to escape my problems, but to experience a different environment, work on myself, and find a healthier balance.

But I also know that changing locations won’t automatically change my habits.

I have to do that work myself.

10/ One of the biggest contradictions I’ve discovered is this:

I entered crypto because I wanted more time for my parents, my friends, and the people I love.

I wanted financial freedom so I could enjoy life with them.

Yet somewhere along the way, I started sacrificing my peace of mind and the life I wanted to build for the money I hoped to make.

I was chasing freedom while allowing the chase itself to become a prison.

I don’t want to keep living that contradiction.

11/ At some point, I have to put my ego aside.

Maybe I wasn’t as good as I thought.

Maybe I was too emotional.

Maybe I was too impatient.

Maybe I was too attached to the idea of making it.

Maybe I confused persistence with refusing to stop.

And maybe I spent too much time trying to prove that I could succeed instead of honestly asking whether my approach was working.

The market doesn’t owe me anything.

My losses don’t guarantee future profits.

And the fact that I’ve already sacrificed so much doesn’t mean I should sacrifice even more.

12/ That’s why I’ve made a decision for November.

No real money. Demo trading only.

I need to rebuild myself before I even consider rebuilding my portfolio.

I want to focus on discipline, risk management, patience, and consistency.

I want to learn how to take a loss without revenge trading.

How to walk away without feeling like I’ve missed everything.

How to wait when there’s no opportunity.

How to follow a plan even when my emotions tell me otherwise.

And how to accept that doing nothing can sometimes be the best decision.

13/ November isn’t about turning $100 into $10K.

It isn’t about finding the next 100x.

It isn’t about recovering $25K as quickly as possible.

It’s about finding out whether I can develop a repeatable process without gambling with my future.

If I can’t follow my rules in a simulated environment, I have no reason to rush back into risking real money.

I need to learn to protect capital before thinking about growing it.

I need to separate my self-worth from my trading results.

And I need to understand that taking a break isn’t the same as giving up.

14/ I still want financial freedom.

I still want to build something of my own.

I still want to travel, help my family, return to football, and have control over my time.

Those dreams haven’t disappeared.

But I need to stop treating trading as the only possible path to achieving them.

My job can provide stability while I work on myself.

My health deserves attention.

My family deserves my presence.

And my future deserves decisions made with a clear mind, not out of desperation to recover past losses.

I don’t have to solve my entire life through one market.

15/ To everyone else who is struggling in this space, I want to say something.

Don’t let your ambition become your prison.

Don’t let your ego convince you that you’re too far in to stop and rethink your approach.

Don’t borrow money to chase losses.

Don’t confuse activity with progress.

Don’t confuse suffering with growth.

And don’t confuse being down bad with being destined for greatness.

You can work incredibly hard and still be wrong about your approach.

Recognizing that isn’t weakness.

It’s the beginning of having a chance to do things differently.

16/ I genuinely congratulate everyone who has found success in this space.

The people who stayed disciplined, managed their risk, learned from their mistakes, and built something sustainable.

You deserve to celebrate your progress.

And to those of us who are still struggling, remember that we don’t have to copy someone else’s timeline.

We don’t have to prove anything to strangers online.

We don’t have to keep risking money just because we’ve already lost so much.

Sometimes, the most important decision is to step back before things get worse.

17/ I don’t know where my journey will lead.

Maybe I’ll eventually become a profitable trader.

Maybe I’ll discover that I need a completely different approach.

Maybe my future will look nothing like the one I imagined when I bought my first memecoin.

I have no guarantees.

But I can choose what I do next.

I can choose to stop repeating the same mistakes.

I can choose to protect what I have left.

I can choose to learn without constantly putting my financial stability at risk.

And I can choose to build a life that matters even before I achieve financial freedom.

18/ I came here to make money so I could have more time for the people I love.

Somewhere along the way, I started sacrificing the people I love, my peace of mind, and my future for the money I wanted to make.

I don’t want to forget that ever again.

Money is a tool.

Trading is a skill.

And financial freedom means very little if you lose sight of everything that made you want it in the first place.

November is about rebuilding.

Not just my portfolio.

My discipline. My mindset. My relationship with money. My health. My priorities.

And most importantly, myself.

I’m not starting over because I believe success is guaranteed.

I’m starting over because I finally understand that continuing the same way isn’t an option.

One day at a time. One lesson at a time.

No chasing losses. No pretending I have everything figured out.

Just honesty, discipline, and the willingness to change.

Let’s see where this journey takes me. 🖤

author: Konstantine

text:
Hackers use AI with no limits. Defenders use AI that says no. NEAR AI fixes the second half.

Two things a security researcher needs from a model. First, that it actually answers when you ask it to analyze an exploit in your own code, instead of refusing. Second, that nobody can read the question. An unpatched bug in a live contract is worth money to whoever sees it first, and every hosted model keeps a log.

NEAR AI RED gives both. Open models with the refusals removed, DeepSeek and Qwen, running inside a hardware enclave where even NEAR AI cannot see the prompt and nothing is stored. Same price as the normal versions, any account can use them. For teams there is a sandbox too: a throwaway machine on your Mac with no internet and no file access, where the AI can take suspicious code apart safely.

text:
FBI官方认定此次币安被盗是朝鲜黑客集团作为，FBI此前多次公开将重大加密货币、金融与网络安全事件归因于朝鲜相关黑客集团（主要是Lazarus Group / APT38 及其聚焦加密的子群 TraderTraitor）。这些活动被FBI视为朝鲜政权通过网络犯罪获取外汇、规避制裁并资助核与导弹计划的重要手段。不得不说这已经是国家网络恐怖主义。

梳理下之前FBI官方确认是朝鲜黑客集团所为的主要案例：
1）2022年3月 Ronin Network（Axie Infinity跨链桥）：约6.2亿美元。FBI明确确认Lazarus Group和APT38负责。
2）2022年6月 Harmony Horizon Bridge：约1亿美元。FBI确认Lazarus Group（APT38），并与TraderTraitor活动关联。
3）2023年6月 Atomic Wallet：超过1亿美元。FBI在后续声明中确认相关朝鲜行为者（与Lazarus/TraderTraitor活动一致）。
4）2023年9月 Stake..com：约4100万美元。FBI公开确认Lazarus Group（APT38）负责，并指出同一批行为者还涉及其他2023年加密盗窃。
5）2024年5月 日本DMM Bitcoin：约3.08亿美元（4502.9 BTC）。FBI与美国国防部网络犯罪中心（DC3）、日本警察厅联合归因于TraderTraitor。
6）2025年2月 Bybit：约15亿美元。FBI发布正式公共安全公告（PSA），确认朝鲜负责，并将该活动命名为“TraderTraitor”。

此外，FBI及相关美国机构还将更早的重大事件归因于朝鲜网络行为者，包括：
1）2014年Sony Pictures黑客攻击（Lazarus Group）。
2）2016年孟加拉国央行（Bangladesh Bank）SWIFT盗窃（约8100万美元成功转移，APT38/Lazarus相关）。
3）2017年WannaCry勒索软件（美国司法部等归因于Lazarus）。

TraderTraitor是FBI自2022年联合警告以来用于描述朝鲜针对加密行业的社会工程与恶意软件活动的主要标签，常与Lazarus/APT38重叠。

FBI之前也持续发布警告，针对朝鲜“远程IT工人”通过身份欺诈在美欧公司就职以赚取资金的长期活动，属同一类国家支持的收入生成机制。

Most agents browse the web through headless Chrome, a full desktop browser. Lightpanda started over.

It's a headless browser built from scratch for AI agents and automation: not a Chromium fork, not a WebKit patch, written in Zig.

Its benchmark requested 933 real web pages on an AWS EC2 m5.large. For 100 pages, peak memory was 123MB vs 2GB for headless Chrome (~16x less), and execution took 5s vs 46s (~9x faster).

It runs a CDP server your Puppeteer or Playwright scripts can connect to. Install via Homebrew, AUR, nightly builds, Nix or Docker.

quoted_text:
人性千年不变 （2026.10.31石）
今天在X上看到关于币安的消息
六十多亿美元的安全事件
我翻了翻评论区，倒是看了一出好戏。
有人义愤填膺，恨不得把赵长鹏送上审判席；有人挺身而出，仿佛币安遭此劫难，比他自己家里失火还难过。竞争平台自然也没闲着，平时讲究行业团结，真到了同行落难的时候，倒是想起了市场竞争。
还有一些人，嘴上说着仗义执言，心里盘算的可能是能不能让大佬看见自己。毕竟平日里想结识这些人物不容易，倘若能在危难之际递上一句安慰，将来或许就多了一份交情。
至于那些爆仓的人，昨天还在称赞这个行业改变命运，今天已经开始诅咒这个行业毁人一生。
事情尚未完全调查清楚，我无意评判币安究竟该承担多少责任。真正吸引我的，是这些形形色色的人。
两千多年前，司马迁写《史记》，留下过一句话：“天下熙熙，皆为利来；天下攘攘，皆为利往。”
那时候没有交易所，没有比特币，更没有X。可人们争夺利益的方式，与今天似乎也没有多大区别。
有人依附权贵，有人借机攻讦政敌，有人趁火打劫，也有人为了博取好名声，做出许多看似大义凛然的事情。
两千年过去，人类已经可以通过一部手机，在几秒钟内完成古人无法想象的财富转移。
只是转移财富的速度快了，人的心思却没怎么变。
来X之前，我对这里多少有些期待。
这里有许多年轻人，聪明、勤奋，学东西很快，也敢于行动。他们不愿接受别人安排好的生活，整天研究项目、交易、技术和各种赚钱的机会。
我很欣赏这种劲头。一个年轻人，手里没有多少资源，却依然相信可以凭自己的本事改变命运。这种野心并不可笑。
只是看得久了，我发现他们虽然试图逃离旧世界，却又在这里建造了一个与旧世界极其相似的地方。
过去的人崇拜官爵，如今的人崇拜财富和流量；过去的人结交权贵，如今的人想办法让大佬关注自己；过去的人靠宗族门第划分圈子，如今的人靠粉丝数量和持仓规模区分高低。
连道德也被原封不动地搬了过来。
一个人想赚钱，偏偏要说成是为了行业发展；想结交大人物，却要把期待包装成不求回报的仗义；因为亏钱而愤怒，一旦举起正义的大旗，便仿佛有资格要求所有人陪他一起愤怒。
这让我想起古时候那些满口仁义道德的人。
他们未必比别人善良，只是更擅长解释什么叫善良，而且特别喜欢要求别人。
你应该忠诚，应该孝顺，应该感恩，应该顾全大局。倘若不肯照办，便是不忠、不孝、不仁、不义。
至于这些要求会让你付出什么代价，通常不在他们的考虑范围之内。
几千年来，道貌岸然者始终是社会中一股强大的力量。
真正的道德需要约束自己，而道德表演只需要约束别人。前者要付出代价，后者却可能换来名望、权力，甚至财富。
这门生意，古往今来都有人做。
一个人为了利益戴上面具，戴得久了，旁人开始相信，他自己也开始相信。到最后，谁敢揭开面具，他反倒会第一个跳出来，指责别人侮辱了他的品格。
我们不仅擅长欺骗别人，有时候还需要先说服自己。
当然，我也不相信所有善意都带着算计。有人确实愿意帮助别人，也愿意为自己相信的事情付出代价。
真正值得警惕的，是那些总想用自己的道德标准，替别人决定应该怎样生活的人。
过去，这种约束可能是一根麻绳。绳子很粗，绑在哪里，谁在拉扯，大家看得清清楚楚。
后来国家变了，制度变了，国籍变了，财富的形式也变了。我们有了互联网、区块链和人工智能。
那根绳子却始终没有消失，只是做得精巧了许多。
比如钓鱼用的PE线。
一根极细的编织线，看着不起眼，拉力却相当惊人。
今天，一个人不必拿着戒尺，也不必拥有正式权力，只要给你扣上一顶道德的帽子，再召集足够多的人表示赞同，就能让你开始为自己的选择感到羞愧。
你不支持谁，就是冷血；你不帮助谁，就是自私；你不按照他们的期待生活，就是辜负了所有人的善意。
最厉害的地方在于，绳子已经不需要别人来拉了。人们会因为害怕被指责，主动把它系在自己身上。
于是我看着X上这些年轻人，心里常有一种复杂的感受。
他们渴望自由，渴望财富，渴望摆脱原来的生活。可他们真的知道自己想摆脱的是什么吗？
一个人即使赚到了足够多的钱，换了国籍，搬到了另一个国家，也未必能摆脱那些熟悉的东西。
人们可以推翻旧权威，然后重新崇拜新权威；可以厌恶过去的等级制度，然后按照财富重新排列座次；可以反对别人用道德绑架自己，转过头来又拿同样的道德要求别人。
我自己当然也不能例外。
我在X上写这些东西，有表达的欲望，也希望别人能够看见。倘若因此获得更多关注，我自然也会高兴。
人有欲望，本来就不是什么见不得人的事情。
怕就怕有一天，我也开始相信自己的所有判断都代表着正义，所有不同意我的人都是愚蠢或者邪恶的。
但我依然喜欢这里。
孔子、孟子生活的年代，人与人之间争论的是仁义礼法
今天的人们坐在电脑前，争论的是财富、自由、正义和权利。
工具早已天翻地覆，争论背后的欲望却依然熟悉。
我想起小时候见过的那种麻绳，粗糙，扎手，时间久了还会磨破皮肤。
现在的PE线可漂亮多了，细得几乎看不见，强度却高得惊人

text:
对比是证明一个项目质量最可靠的方式，不论是横向还是纵向都可以。

在隐私这个叙事上，其实有很多项目在做了，但是现在的话，让大家讲，大家可能更多的是ZEC、Zama等隐私链项目

这些项目有的是自己一条链，有的是为ETH链服务的，但是公认的，BNBChain的，并且能够真的解决现实问题的，好像一直尚未有定论

其中最现实的问题就是：数据可以被证明是真实的之后，能不能在不暴露原始信息的情况下继续使用它？

我用 @primus_labs 跟其他主要的隐私项目对比看看：谁更有机会把隐私能力变成开发者能集成、用户能使用的基础设施（也就是解决真实的业务需求）

🆚直接看我做的图吧

这张表并不是技术性能排名。三者的技术目标存在交集，但并非完全相同，部分能力也可以通过合作进行组合

我更看好Primus的原因，是它试图解决的问题更接近真实业务的完整需求

1、它不只关注数据是否可信，也关注数据如何被使用

对金融应用而言，证明一个数字是真实的很重要，但如何在不泄露其他信息的情况下完成风控和计算，同样重要

2、它的技术路线有机会降低应用层的组合复杂度

如果开发者需要分别接入数据验证、隐私计算和金融应用组件，就必须处理不同系统之间的接口、安全假设和运维问题。Primus的整合路线有机会减少这类摩擦

降低其他人的工作复杂度 = 提高自己产品的使用度

3、它正在尝试把隐私能力转化成可操作的产品

Confidential Finance这类实践表明了Primus其实不满足于只提供概念层面的技术叙事，而是在探索用户如何真正使用隐私金融工具

这三点共同构成了Primus的差异化优势

💇zkPass在链下数据验证方向有自己的价值
Fhenix则聚焦于FHE隐私计算
Primus的不同之处在于尝试将数据验证、隐私计算与金融应用连接起来

这也是我认为Primus更值得关注的核心理由：它瞄准的不是一个孤立的隐私功能，而是一条从可信数据到隐私化业务的完整路

只要未来链上金融既需要透明的规则，又需要保护参与者的敏感信息，那么能够同时处理“可信”和“隐私”的基础设施，就有机会占据更重要的位置

而Primus，正在朝这个方向的龙头推进

text:
人类争论了几千年都没能统一的善恶标准，现在要先给 Claude 确定一套了。

据美联社报道，Anthropic 已经与来自超过 15 个宗教及跨文化群体的学者、神职人员、哲学家和伦理学家展开交流，试图让这些不同的思想传统参与塑造 Claude 处理道德问题的方式。

这件事最有意思的地方，是宗教和文化之间本来就存在大量无法调和的分歧。

同样一个伦理问题，不同宗教可能给出完全相反的答案。同一种宗教内部，不同教派也能争论几百年。人类社会花了这么长时间，都没能形成一套普遍接受的道德体系。

但 AI 公司必须做出选择。因为 Claude 每一次回答敏感问题、拒绝某个请求，背后其实都有一套价值判断在起作用。

所以我觉得，AI Alignment 正在进入一个很微妙的阶段。

Anthropic 可以邀请 15 个、50 个甚至 100 个宗教和文化群体参与讨论，但最后总要有人决定哪些价值观被保留，哪些被舍弃，以及发生冲突时谁的原则优先。

而这个最终决定权，仍然掌握在模型公司手里。

未来数亿甚至数十亿人每天接触的 AI，其道德边界可能最终由硅谷少数几家公司来划定。

这件事的政治意义，可能远比我们现在讨论的 AI 安全问题更大。
